True to the duo's stripped-down setup, the song uses no bass guitar at all, and its Michel Gondry-directed video relies on clever in-camera visual effects as the band performs.

alabama shakes|gemini.fact: "Gemini," a six-and-a-half-minute highlight from Alabama Shakes' 2015 album Sound & Color, blends psych-funk guitar tones with Brittany Howard's echoing, almost otherworldly vocal delivery. Critics have pointed to its deep debt to vintage soul and funk, hearing echoes of Isaac Hayes' "Walk On By" and classic Wu-Tang Clan basslines in its slow-burning groove.

angel olsen|hi-five.fact: "Hi-Five," from Angel Olsen's 2014 album Burn Your Fire For No Witness, opens with the line "I feel so lonesome I could cry" - a nod to the classic Hank Williams song, though Olsen delivers it in a style closer to Roy Orbison. It came from the first album Olsen recorded with a full band, tracked in Asheville, North Carolina with drummer Josh Jaeger and bassist Stewart Bronaugh.

beabadoobee|switchblade.fact: "Switchblade" is a 2026 single from beabadoobee's album Pylon, marking a heavier, grunge- and emo-leaning turn in her sound. She's cited a longtime love of hardcore and Midwest emo as inspiration, and the title works as a metaphor for deciding whether to stand your ground or walk away, rather than a literal weapon reference.

beach house|once twice melody.fact: "Once Twice Melody" is the title track and opener of Beach House's 2022 double album of the same name - their eighth record and the first the duo produced entirely on their own. The sprawling 18-song project was recorded over several years at studios in Baltimore, Minnesota, and Los Angeles, and marked the first time the band used a live string ensemble, arranged by David Campbell.

beirut|a sunday smile.fact: "A Sunday Smile," from Beirut's 2007 album The Flying Club Cup, opens with a French waltz on organ before blooming into a bright, sweeping chorus. The album was inspired by bandleader Zach Condon's travels in France, built around a photo of hot-air balloons circling the Eiffel Tower that he kept pinned up in the studio.

big red machine|the ghost of cincinnati.fact: "The Ghost of Cincinnati" marks the first time Big Red Machine co-founder Aaron Dessner took the lead vocal on one of the project's own songs. Dessner originally wrote the track with Taylor Swift's catalog in mind, but she encouraged him to keep it for Big Red Machine's second album instead; the lyrics were co-written with filmmaker Nicole Riegel, inspired by her screenplay Dandelion.

binki|hotel window.fact: "Hotel Window" is a grungy 2023 single from Pennsylvania-raised singer-songwriter binki (born Baraka Andrew Ongeri), released as one of three singles leading up to his second EP, Antennae. The track pushed his usual hip-hop-and-indie-rock fusion into heavier, more guitar-driven territory than his earlier bedroom-pop songs.

boygenius|true blue.fact: "True Blue," from boygenius's 2023 album the record, is Lucy Dacus's tribute to the steady friendship she shares with bandmates Phoebe Bridgers and Julien Baker. Built around the idiom "true blue" (loyal and steadfast), its chorus - "It feels good to be known so well" - captures the comfort of being fully understood by people who've watched you grow up.

bright eyes|first day of my life.fact: Conor Oberst's "First Day of My Life," from Bright Eyes' 2005 album I'm Wide Awake, It's Morning, reached number 37 on the UK singles chart and was later voted the number-one love song of all time in an NPR Music listener poll. Its music video, directed by John Cameron Mitchell, won a Special Recognition Award at the GLAAD Media Awards.

broken social scene|this house is on fir.fact: "This House Is on Fire" began as an outtake from Broken Social Scene's 2009 sessions for Forgiveness Rock Record before finally surfacing on their 2022 rarities collection, Old Dead Young: B-Sides & Rarities. The dreamy, restrained track is built around Kevin Drew's languid lead vocal.

built to spill|in your mind.fact: "In Your Mind" comes from Built to Spill's 2001 album Ancient Melodies of the Future. Rather than following a standard verse-chorus structure, the song rides an insistent rhythm section and winding, Far Eastern-tinged guitar lines while frontman Doug Martsch half-speaks his way through the lyrics instead of singing them straight.

caribou|never come back.fact: "Never Come Back" was the very first finished track for Caribou mastermind Dan Snaith's 2020 album Suddenly, a record ultimately whittled down from over 900 draft songs. Snaith said the song came together quickly and naturally once he landed on its central synth chords and repeated vocal refrain.

devo|gut feeling / (slap your mammy).fact: "Gut Feeling" and its brief instrumental coda "(Slap Your Mammy)" close out side one of DEVO's 1978 debut, Q: Are We Not Men? A: We Are Devo!, produced by Brian Eno and recorded in Cologne, West Germany. The songwriting credits split the pair of tracks between guitarist Bob Mothersbaugh and keyboardist Mark Mothersbaugh on "Gut Feeling" and bassist Gerald Casale on "(Slap Your Mammy)."

dr. dog|talk is cheap.fact: "Talk Is Cheap," the lead single from Dr. Dog's 2024 self-titled album - their first in six years - was written by bassist Toby Leaman as a tribute to his wife. Leaman has said that despite not considering himself "a big love-song guy," nearly everything he wrote for the record was for her, and the song's jangling, Motown-indebted groove has drawn comparisons to David Bowie's Young Americans era.

duster|gold dust.fact: "Gold Dust" is a short, hazy instrumental interlude near the start of Duster's 1998 debut, Stratosphere, written and recorded by founding members Clay Parton and Canaan Dove Amber at their home studio, Low Space Orbit, using lo-fi analog gear. The hushed two-minute track helped define the record's warm, slow-core atmosphere that later made it a cult classic.

father john misty|mr. tillman.fact: "Mr. Tillman" was the promotional single for Father John Misty's 2017 album Pure Comedy, written during a stretch when Josh Tillman was living out of a hotel. The song includes a real-life cameo from singer-songwriter Jason Isbell, name-checked in the lyrics; Isbell has confirmed in interviews that the line was inspired by an actual encounter between the two musicians.

fleet foxes|lorelai.fact: "Lorelai," the opening track on Fleet Foxes' 2011 album Helplessness Blues, is widely noted as an homage to Bob Dylan's "4th Time Around" — a song Dylan wrote as a wry response to the Beatles' "Norwegian Wood." Frontman Robin Pecknold has cited Dylan and Brian Wilson as foundational influences on the band's melodic songwriting style.

fontaines d.c.|liberty belle.fact: Fontaines D.C.'s "Liberty Belle," released as a single in May 2017 ahead of their debut album Dogrel, is named for the Liberties, the historic Dublin neighborhood near BIMM music college where members Carlos O'Connell, Conor Curley, Conor Deegan, Grian Chatten, and Tom Coll first met and lived while forming the band. The song is a tribute to that working-class Dublin district.

franz ferdinand|no you girls.fact: Franz Ferdinand's "No You Girls" was inspired by frontman Alex Kapranos' memory of his first kiss, with a girl named Katherine, and how awkwardly the two misread each other. The song went through earlier working titles, including "Katherine Kiss Me" and "No You Girls Never Know," before landing on the 2009 album Tonight: Franz Ferdinand, and it reached a much wider audience after being featured in a worldwide iPod advertisement.

grizzly bear|a simple answer.fact: "A Simple Answer" appears on Grizzly Bear's 2012 album Shields, produced by the band's own Chris Taylor. The band initially recorded much of the album at a studio in Marfa, Texas, before scrapping most of those sessions and relocating to a cabin on Cape Cod, making Shields one of their most collaboratively written records.

grizzly bear|easier.fact: "Easier" opens Grizzly Bear's 2006 album Yellow House, which takes its title from the actual yellow Victorian house on Cape Cod belonging to singer Ed Droste's grandmother, where the band set up and recorded most of the record during a month-long stay. The homey, informal recording setting is often credited with giving the album its warm, intimate sound.

hot chip|flutes.fact: Hot Chip's "Flutes" grew out of a simple looped two-note flute sample and was one of the first songs written for their 2012 album In Our Heads. Joe Goddard has said its main inspiration was James Holden's remix of Nathan Fake's "The Sky Was Pink," and the band deliberately chose it as the album's first single because they considered it an unusually ambitious, constantly shifting track for them.

hot chip|spell.fact: Hot Chip's "Spell," from 2019's A Bath Full of Ecstasy, began when Joe Goddard and Alexis Taylor spent several days at Air Studios in London writing with material originally intended for Katy Perry's Witness album. The band later reworked the song for themselves, with Taylor's vocal performance partly inspired by one of his musical heroes, Prince.

kate bush|breathing.fact: Kate Bush's "Breathing" was released as a single from her 1980 album Never for Ever and recorded at London's famed Abbey Road Studios, co-produced by Bush and Jon Kelly. The track features backing vocals from English folk musician Roy Harper and reached number 16 on the UK singles chart, staying on the chart for seven weeks.

king krule|baby blue.fact: "Baby Blue" is a standout track on King Krule's 2013 debut album, 6 Feet Beneath the Moon, released when songwriter Archy Marshall was just 19 years old. The album was co-produced by Rodaidh McDonald, known for his work with Savages and the xx, and "Baby Blue" is especially noted for its clean, jazz-inflected guitar tone and trip-hop-style drums.

m83|do it, try it.fact: "Do It, Try It" was the lead single from M83's 2016 album Junk, the project's first full album in five years, written and produced by Anthony Gonzalez with a bouncy house-piano rhythm and a synth lead reminiscent of Wendy Carlos' score for A Clockwork Orange. The song later found a second life after being featured in the season 8 finale of the TV series Letterkenny.

margot & the nuclear so and so's|as tall.fact: "As Tall as Cliffs" comes from Margot & the Nuclear So and So's, an Indianapolis band formed in 2004 by childhood friends Richard Edwards and Andy Fry, who named the group after the character Margot in Wes Anderson's film The Royal Tenenbaums. By their 2006 debut, The Dust of Retreat, the lineup had grown to eight full-time members, and this song later appeared on both 2007's Not Animal and its 2008 companion release, Animal!.

mitski|townie.fact: Mitski's "Townie," the second single from her 2014 album Bury Me at Makeout Creek, actually got two separate music videos: one directed by Allyssa Yohana that premiered on Rookie in November 2014, and an animated version directed by illustrator Faye Orlove that premiered on The Fader the following March. The album itself marked a stylistic turn for the classically trained Mitski toward a scrappier, more rock-oriented sound, recorded largely in houses and makeshift studios with friends.

modest mouse|head south.fact: "Head South" appears on Modest Mouse's 1996 debut album, This Is a Long Drive for Someone with Nothing to Think About. The song tells the story of a restless Pacific Northwest surf-rock band — one with "no surf, just pine trees" — who dream of trading their gray hometown for a sunnier, idealized life elsewhere.

my morning jacket|complex.fact: "Complex" is a fuzzed-out rocker from My Morning Jacket's 2021 self-titled album. Frontman Jim James described the song as being about feeling like "a puzzle piece that won't fit," wrestling with how to make relationships and a career work in a fully satisfying way, and the track intentionally ends by collapsing into the sound of a vinyl record playing at the wrong speed.

r.e.m.|harborcoat.fact: "Harborcoat" opens R.E.M.'s 1984 album Reckoning, produced by Mitch Easter and Don Dixon at Reflection Sound Studio in Charlotte, North Carolina over just 16 days. The song's memorable chorus, "find my harborcoat, can't go outside without it," reportedly traces back to a 1983 tour stop in Los Angeles, when the band got word of a bad storm back home in Georgia.

radiohead|morning bell/amnesiac.fact: "Morning Bell" exists in two very different arrangements across Radiohead's companion albums: the Kid A version (2000) is built on looping Rhodes electric piano in a lopsided 5/8 time signature with a drum-machine beat, while the version on Amnesiac (2001), officially titled "Morning Bell/Amnesiac," recasts the song in straight time with stark acoustic and organ orchestration and no percussion at all. Guitarist Ed O'Brien has said the band actually forgot about one version during the sprawling sessions that produced both records before rediscovering it.

savages|she will.fact: "She Will" was given away as a free advance single ahead of Savages' 2013 debut album Silence Yourself. The whole record, including this track, was recorded in just three weeks at London's Fish Factory studio, produced by Johnny Hostile and Rodaidh McDonald, built around guitarist Gemma Thompson's spare, surf-tinged riff.

soccer mommy|your dog.fact: "Your Dog" was the breakthrough single Sophie Allison released under the Soccer Mommy name, arriving January 9, 2018 via Fat Possum Records as the lead single and opening track of her debut studio album, Clean.

sparks|hospitality on parade.fact: "Hospitality on Parade" opens Sparks' 1975 album Indiscreet, produced by Tony Visconti (known for his work with David Bowie and T. Rex) and released on Island Records. The album pushed brothers Ron and Russell Mael's art-pop sound into bigger, more theatrical orchestral territory.

st. vincent|down.fact: "Down" rides a funky synth bassline with Prince-style guitar and sitar, co-produced by St. Vincent and Jack Antonoff for her 2021 album Daddy's Home, a record steeped in 1970s New York sounds. Its music video styles St. Vincent after Andy Warhol Factory star Candy Darling, shot on vintage, grainy celluloid film to evoke that era's underground film look.

sufjan stevens|holland.fact: "Holland" is track seven on Sufjan Stevens' 2003 album Michigan (Greetings from Michigan, the Great Lake State), one of the first records in his later-abandoned plan to make an album for every U.S. state. Critics have described it as a gentle, postcard-like sketch of a teenage summer romance, carried by Stevens' banjo-and-horn arrangements.

talking heads|the lady don't mind.fact: "The Lady Don't Mind" was released as a single from Talking Heads' 1985 album Little Creatures, the record that marked the band's turn toward a brighter, brass-accented pop sound. A six-minute "Extended Mix" of the track was later added as a bonus cut on the album's 2005 reissue.

the avalanches feat. rivers cuomo & pink.fact: "Running Red Lights" teams Australian sample-collage group The Avalanches with Weezer's Rivers Cuomo on lead vocals and rapper Pink Siifu on a spoken interlude, released as a single in March 2020. Its video stars dancer Erik Cavanaugh moving through city streets and features a cameo from Sunset Strip billboard icon Angelyne.

the clash|clampdown.fact: "Clampdown" began as an instrumental guitarist Mick Jones called "Working and Waiting" before Joe Strummer added lyrics; it was recorded at Wessex Studios in London during the sessions for 1979's London Calling. The phrase "working for the clampdown" became one of the most quoted lines from that landmark double album.

the decemberists|rusalka, rusalka / the.fact: The title nods to the rusalka, a water spirit from Slavic folklore traditionally said to dwell in rivers and lakes. The song appears on The Decemberists' 2006 major-label debut The Crane Wife, an album built around two multi-part song cycles drawn from folk tales of different cultures.

the jesus and mary chain|happy when it r.fact: "Happy When It Rains" was the second single from The Jesus and Mary Chain's 1987 album Darklands, written by brothers William and Jim Reid and produced with Bill Price. The song reached number 25 on the UK singles chart and is often cited as one of the band's most melodic, hook-driven moments.

the jesus lizard|nub.fact: "Nub" is a standout track on The Jesus Lizard's 1991 album Goat, produced by Steve Albini at Chicago Recording Company over just a handful of weekend sessions. Guitarist Duane Denison's slide-guitar playing on the track is frequently singled out as one of the record's signature sounds.

the modern lovers|roadrunner.fact: Jonathan Richman wrote "Roadrunner" as a teenager as an ode to driving Massachusetts Route 128, inspired by the glow of the highway's radio towers at night. Musically it borrows its driving two-chord structure from the Velvet Underground's "Sister Ray," a band Richman idolized; the Modern Lovers recorded it in 1972, and it was finally released in 1976 produced by former Velvet Underground member John Cale.

the national|guilty party.fact: "Guilty Party" comes from The National's 2017 album Sleep Well Beast. Its music video, directed by artist Casey Reas, builds its visuals around Janus, the two-faced Roman god who looks simultaneously into the past and future, using that imagery to explore memory and its distortions.

the pop group|she is beyond good and evi.fact: "She Is Beyond Good and Evil" was The Pop Group's debut single, released in March 1979 on Radar Records and produced by British dub reggae pioneer Dennis Bovell. The track helped define the post-punk era by fusing funk, dub, and free-jazz textures, and it was later ranked among NME's best singles of 1979 and included in The Guardian's "1000 Songs Everyone Must Hear."

the war on drugs|change.fact: "Change" comes from The War on Drugs' fifth album, I Don't Live Here Anymore, released in October 2021 on Atlantic Records. Frontman Adam Granduciel wrote the six-minute track as a meditation on getting older and navigating personal upheaval, making it one of the emotional centerpieces of the record.

the white stripes|blue orchid.fact: "Blue Orchid" opens The White Stripes' 2005 album Get Behind Me Satan and was released as its lead single. Jack White built the song's signature riff around a new setting he discovered on an Electro-Harmonix POG (Polyphonic Octave Generator) pedal, later telling NPR's Terry Gross that the riff "turned everything around" and rescued the album's recording sessions.

the xx|fiction.fact: "Fiction" is the third track on The xx's 2012 album Coexist and marked bassist Oliver Sim's first lead vocal turn for the band. The bittersweet song follows a narrator infatuated with someone who only appears in his dreams, set against skittering digital percussion that echoes producer Jamie xx's remix work.

unknown mortal orchestra|can't keep chec.fact: "Can't Keep Checking My Phone" is a single by Unknown Mortal Orchestra, released in April 2015 ahead of their album Multi-Love. The track was A-listed on BBC Radio 6 Music and reached an even wider audience after being featured in the soundtrack of the video game FIFA 16.

vampire weekend|cape cod kwassa kwassa.fact: "Cape Cod Kwassa Kwassa" opens Vampire Weekend's self-titled 2008 debut album. Its stop-start, arpeggiated guitar line draws on Congolese guitar-pop styles associated with artists like Kanda Bongo Man, giving the song's New England imagery an Afropop backbone that critics compared to Paul Simon's Graceland.

waxahatchee|silver.fact: "Silver" appears on Waxahatchee's third album, Out in the Storm, released in 2017. For the track, singer-songwriter Katie Crutchfield double-tracked her own vocals, essentially harmonizing with herself throughout the song for a layered, intimate effect.

westside cowboy|alright alright alright.fact: Westside Cowboy is a British rock band formed in 2023 in Manchester. "Alright Alright Alright" was the band's second single, a high-energy "punk song about a cowboy" that playfully nods to the outlaw-ballad style of Johnny Cash, released ahead of their 2025 debut EP.

whitney|real love.fact: "REAL LOVE" is the lead single from Whitney's third album, SPARK, released in 2022 on Secretly Canadian. Chicago duo Julien Ehrlich and Max Kakacek wrote the punchier, synth-tinged track after moving back to their hometown in 2021, giving the band's usually soft sound a newly danceable edge.

wilco|war on war.fact: "War on War" appears on Wilco's acclaimed 2002 album Yankee Hotel Foxtrot. Frontman Jeff Tweedy has said the upbeat, acoustic-driven song is about accepting the possibility of failure as part of truly living, built around the line "you have to learn how to die, if you want to want to be alive."

wolf parade|what did my lover say? (it a.fact: "What Did My Lover Say? (It Always Had to Go This Way)" is the third track on Wolf Parade's 2010 album Expo 86, sung by Spencer Krug. Critics described it as a danceable, disco-tinged cousin to the band's earlier song "It's a Curse," built around Krug's vivid imagery of seaside holiday towns glinting "like giant shining earrings against the cheek of the sea."

yo la tengo|you can have it all.fact: Yo La Tengo's "You Can Have It All" is a cover of the 1970s soul tune written by Harry Wayne Casey of KC and the Sunshine Band and originally recorded by George McCrae. The band included their slowed-down, atmospheric rendition on their 2000 album And Then Nothing Turned Itself Inside-Out.

10,000 maniacs|these are days.fact: "These Are Days" was the lead single from 10,000 Maniacs' 1992 album "Our Time in Eden," written by guitarist Robert Buck and singer Natalie Merchant and recorded at Bearsville Studios in upstate New York. It topped Billboard's Modern Rock Tracks chart that November, helping push the album past a million and a half copies sold. The band later revisited it for their classic 1993 "MTV Unplugged" set.

adrianne lenker|dragon eyes.fact: "dragon eyes" comes from Adrianne Lenker's 2020 album "songs," which she wrote and recorded in about a month inside a one-room cabin in Westhampton, Massachusetts after a tour got canceled early in the pandemic. She tracked the record live to an eight-track tape machine, hoping to capture the sound of that small room along with the songs themselves. Lenker has called it one of her rawest and simplest songs, built around the plain wish "I just want a place with you."

alex g|kicker.fact: "Kicker" appeared on Alex G's 2015 album "Beach Music," his first release for Domino Records after years of self-releasing music on Bandcamp. The song closes on a dry, plainspoken line -- "Heaven, maybe freedom, what's the word? Right, I forgot, quiet is the closest thing we got" -- a turn of phrase critics compared to the deadpan aphorisms of songwriter David Berman.

andrew bird|skin is, my.fact: "Skin Is, My" grew out of an earlier instrumental called "Skin" that Andrew Bird released on his 2003 album "Weather Systems." Two years later he added lyrics and reworked the melody into a full song, which became one of the standout tracks on his breakthrough 2005 album "The Mysterious Production of Eggs."

angel olsen|shut up kiss me.fact: "Shut Up Kiss Me" is the lead single from Angel Olsen's 2016 album "My Woman," co-produced by Olsen and Justin Raisen and cut live in the studio with her full band. Olsen wrote and directed the song's music video herself, skating through an empty roller rink at night in the same sparkly silver wig she wore for her earlier "Intern" video.

animal collective|guys eyes.fact: "Guys Eyes" is track seven on Animal Collective's 2009 breakthrough "Merriweather Post Pavilion," recorded at Sweet Tea Studios in Oxford, Mississippi. The band brought in co-producer Ben Allen specifically for his skill mixing low-end sound, a key ingredient in the album's dense, bass-heavy production.

badly drawn boy|the shining.fact: "The Shining" opens Badly Drawn Boy's 2000 debut album "The Hour of Bewilderbeast," arranged with French horn and cello alongside Damon Gough's acoustic guitar. Despite the ominous title, it's a hopeful song built around the repeated wish to "put a little bit of sunshine" into someone's life. The album went on to win that year's Mercury Music Prize.

beach fossils|what a pleasure.fact: The title track of Beach Fossils' 2011 EP "What a Pleasure" grew out of late-night jam sessions between Dustin Payseur, bassist John Pena, and friend Jack Tatum of Wild Nothing. True to its name, the song's lyrics paint a sunny day at the beach -- kites in the air, kids building sandcastles, surfers catching waves -- set to bright, jangly, '80s-indebted guitar lines.

beck|already dead.fact: "Already Dead" appears on Beck's 2002 album "Sea Change," recorded with producer Nigel Godrich in the aftermath of a breakup. Much of the album's spare, acoustic material came together in about a week, a sharp pivot away from the dense sampling and studio trickery of earlier Beck records like "Odelay."

belle and sebastian|get me away from her.fact: Originally released on Belle and Sebastian's 1996 album "If You're Feeling Sinister," the song is a tongue-in-cheek, meta number about deciding to write a pop song out of frustration that "nobody writes them like they used to." Decades later, the band re-recorded it for the soundtrack of the 2019 film "Days of the Bagnold Summer."

big red machine|i won't run from it.fact: "I Won't Run From It" comes from the 2018 self-titled debut of Big Red Machine, the collaborative project between Bon Iver's Justin Vernon and The National's Aaron Dessner. It was recorded and mixed at Dessner's Long Pond studio in New York's Hudson Valley, opening with his folksy fingerpicking before building into strings, backing vocals, and drum machines.

big star|the ballad of el goodo.fact: Written by Alex Chilton and Chris Bell for Big Star's 1972 debut "#1 Record," the song's title phrase never actually shows up anywhere in the lyrics. It's instead built around a quietly defiant chorus of self-reliance -- "There ain't no one going to turn me 'round" -- carried by the band's layered, Beatles-indebted harmonies.

big thief|pretty things.fact: "Pretty Things" opens Big Thief's 2017 album "Capacity," which the band recorded with producer Andrew Sarlo at Outlier Inn, a snowbound studio tucked in the woods of upstate New York. Sarlo worked out most of the album's arrangements with the band on the spot, often turning a bare idea into a finished take within a few hours.

black belt eagle scout|run it to ya.fact: "Run It to Ya" was released in 2019 as a single from Black Belt Eagle Scout's (Katherine Paul's) album "At the Party With My Brown Friends." Paul has described it as a sparkling, starry-eyed song about the simple wonder of love, and its music video, directed by Evan James Benally Atwood, reimagines prom night as a joyful dance.

bon iver|death breast.fact: Styled on the album as "10 d E A T h b R E a s T," the song comes from Bon Iver's 2016 album "22, A Million." Its jumbled, glitchy capitalization follows a titling scheme Justin Vernon used across the whole record, mirroring the album's fractured, heavily processed electronic sound. Extended versions of the track arrived with lyric visuals built around artwork by designer Eric Timothy Carlson.

built to spill|car.fact: "Car" appeared on Built to Spill's 1994 album "There's Nothing Wrong with Love" and was released as a single. Centered on the line "I need a car, you need a guide, who needs a map?", the song became known as a kind of travel-without-a-destination mantra for the band, embracing curiosity over having a fixed plan.

built to spill|carry the zero.fact: "Carry the Zero" was the second single from Built to Spill's 1999 album "Keep It Like a Secret," produced by Phil Ek and recorded at Avast! Recording in Seattle and Bear Creek Studio in Woodinville, Washington. For that record, Doug Martsch and the band deliberately trimmed their songs down from the sprawling, six-plus-minute epics of 1997's "Perfect From Now On."

car seat headrest|weightlifters.fact: Will Toledo wrote "Weightlifters" -- the first song completed for 2020's "Making a Door Less Open" -- while on tour in 2015 or 2016. He's described it as being about the gap between saying you want to change and actually doing it, built around the half-joking, repeated resolution "I should start lifting weights." Its woozy opening synth line came from him bending a single held note up and down in Logic.

cheekface|flies.fact: Released in 2024 with Jeff Rosenstock guesting on baritone sax, "Flies" was written by Cheekface's Greg Katz and bassist Amanda Tannen together in their practice space. Katz has said some of the lyrics were drawn straight from life, including an actual room full of flies and his own repeated failed attempts at landing a kickflip.

cocteau twins|frou-frou foxes in midsumm.fact: The closing track on Cocteau Twins' 1990 album "Heaven or Las Vegas," the song carries one of the band's most famously inscrutable titles -- the phrase never actually turns up anywhere in Elizabeth Fraser's lyrics, and the band never explained what it means. Critics have singled it out as one of the record's most dramatic moments, closing out an album now widely regarded as a defining release of the dream pop genre.

courtney barnett|crippling self-doubt an.fact: "Crippling Self-Doubt and a General Lack of Confidence" appears on Courtney Barnett's 2018 album Tell Me How You Really Feel, written after the pressure following her acclaimed debut left her wrestling with writer's block and anxiety. The song's breezy, upbeat guitar-pop deliberately contrasts with its anxious lyrics, including the repeated admission "I don't know anything." Barnett has described the feeling behind it as "a natural state I've held with me since before I was a teenager," more psychological than tied to any one event.

dead kennedys|california uber alles.fact: Before it became a Dead Kennedys classic, Jello Biafra wrote the music for "California Uber Alles" while jamming on his roommate's bass guitar, and says the chorus's nasal, warbling melody was inspired more by Japanese Kabuki theater music than by rock and roll. The song debuted as the band's first single in 1979 on the independent Optional Music label before being re-recorded for their 1980 debut album, Fresh Fruit for Rotting Vegetables.

father john misty|i guess time just make.fact: "I Guess Time Just Makes Fools of Us All" is a nearly nine-minute, horn-laden closing track on Father John Misty's 2022 odds-and-ends collection Greatish Hits: I Followed My Dreams and My Dreams Said to Crawl. Although it was billed as a never-before-heard studio recording, Josh Tillman had actually been performing the song live on and off since 2019 before it finally got an official release.

fontaines d.c.|a lucid dream.fact: "A Lucid Dream" was released as a single off Fontaines D.C.'s second album, A Hero's Death (2020), a record the band made partly in response to the whirlwind success of their debut, Dogrel. Its music video, directed by Jordan Martin, intercuts footage of frontman Grian Chatten wandering city streets with archival historical footage, blending past and present.

future islands|balance.fact: "Balance" was the lead single from Future Islands' third album, On the Water, which the trio wrote and recorded during a retreat at a waterfront house in Elizabeth City, North Carolina. The track opens and closes with the sound of ocean waves, and its music video, directed by longtime collaborator Jay Buim, drew visual inspiration from the classic surf documentary The Endless Summer.

gang of four|ether.fact: "Ether," the opening track on Gang of Four's 1979 debut Entertainment!, was built around a striking production trick: singer Jon King's and guitarist Andy Gill's vocals were recorded onto separate stereo channels so they'd hit each ear independently, creating a disorienting call-and-response effect. The track was cut at The Workhouse studio in London, with Gill co-producing alongside King and Rob Warr.

grizzly bear|neighbors.fact: "Neighbors" was released as the fourth single from Grizzly Bear's 2017 album Painted Ruins, the band's first new record in five years. Bandmate Chris Taylor produced the album, with sessions split between the rustic Allaire Studios in Shokan, New York, and Taylor's own Terrible Studios in Los Angeles.

guided by voices|i am a scientist.fact: "I Am a Scientist" first appeared as a lo-fi, four-track home recording on Guided by Voices' 1994 breakthrough Bee Thousand, then got a fuller studio treatment on a same-named EP recorded live-in-studio with engineer Andy Shernoff. Frontman Robert Pollard has said the song and the album around it "opened the door" that let him make a living playing rock music, and thirty years later the band re-recorded it in hi-fi for the album's anniversary.

hot chip|colours.fact: "Colours" was the third single from Hot Chip's 2006 album The Warning, which had just earned the band a Mercury Prize nomination. Written by Alexis Taylor and Joe Goddard, the song got a CGI music video from director Nima Nourizadeh, his third clip for the band.

idles|car crash.fact: The video for IDLES' "Car Crash," the second single from 2021's Crawler, was directed by Matthew Cusick and edited by the band's own guitarist Lee Kiernan. Cusick built it from a personal archive of vintage car-collision footage from old films that he had been compiling as a hobby since 2001, shot from the disorienting point of view of passengers inside the vehicles.

iron & wine|you never know.fact: "You Never Know" appears on Iron & Wine's 2024 album Light Verse and opens with the nostalgic sounds of a creaking rocking chair and guitar strings being tuned up. Sam Beam built the song around the idea of life's open-ended possibilities, finding comfort in uncertainty rather than anxiety about it.

james chance & the contortions|contort y.fact: After "Contort Yourself" appeared on the Contortions' 1979 no-wave album Buy, manager Anya Phillips helped rebrand the group as "James White and the Blacks" for a disco-funk remake, after ZE Records offered James Chance $10,000 to make a dance record. The resulting disco single turned out too fast for club DJs to play, so labelmate August Darnell (of Kid Creole) remixed it at a slower tempo with a newly written guitar part.

june mcdoom|human angel.fact: "Human Angel" is a single from June McDoom's debut full-length album, Follow the Light, released on Jagjaguwar in October 2026 after several years of EPs. The song pairs acoustic balladry with a lush, Kate Bush-style vocal arrangement over a stuttering, syncopated drum pattern, and its music video was directed by Rena Johnson.

justice|flower in a hurricane (ft. tame.fact: "Flower in a Hurricane" debuted alongside the launch trailer for Grand Theft Auto VI in October 2026, marking the first time French duo Justice has composed music for a video game -- they're writing the game's full original score. The one-off single pairs Tame Impala's Kevin Parker and SZA singing in harmony over an '80s-style synth-rock riff, with King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard contributing organ and guitar.

kevin morby|a night at the little los an.fact: A Night at the Little Los Angeles collects the original four-track home demos Kevin Morby recorded in the backyard shed of his Kansas City home, a space he nicknamed "the Little Los Angeles," which he later developed into his 2020 album Sundowner. Dead Oceans released the demo versions as their own standalone album in October 2021, giving listeners the songs in their earliest, sparsest form.

khruangbin|pon pon.fact: "Pon Pon," from Khruangbin's 2024 album A La Sala, was inspired by a childhood game that bassist Laura Lee played growing up in Mexico. True to the trio's style, the song is built around a single repeating bass-and-guitar riff from Lee and Mark Speer rather than conventional chords, with drummer DJ Johnson locking into a funky groove beneath soft, melody-free whispered vocals.

king gizzard & the lizard wizard|30 past.fact: "30 Past 7," written by Stu Mackenzie, was the lead single from King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard's 2013 album Float Along - Fill Your Lungs, built around a dreamy, sitar-laced haze of synths and Pink Floyd-esque guitars. Its companion video, designed by artist Jason Galea, was meant to capture the feeling of "when you've got to wake up at 7:30am and go to a 9 to 5 job."

king gizzard & the lizard wizard|pleura.fact: "Pleura" appears on King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard's 2021 album L.W., the third installment of a microtonal-tuning trilogy that began with 2017's Flying Microtonal Banana and continued with 2020's K.G. When the band shared the song, they filmed, recorded, edited and uploaded a live performance video of it all within a single day.

kurt vile|hunchback.fact: Kurt Vile first released "Hunchback" on a 2009 EP credited to Kurt Vile & the Violators, produced by guitarist Adam Granduciel, who would go on to found The War on Drugs. A re-recorded version then appeared later that year on Vile's album Childish Prodigy, though Vile has said the looser EP cut is closer to how the band actually plays it live.

lucy dacus|ankles.fact: Lucy Dacus debuted "Ankles" live on Jimmy Fallon's show backed by a string section before releasing it as a single alongside "Limerence" in January 2025. It served as the lead single for her fourth album, Forever Is a Feeling, which drew on a rotating cast of producers including Dacus herself, Blake Mills, Bartees Strange and Melina Duterte.

marika hackman|33.fact: "33" opens Marika Hackman's 2025 album False Dogs, a record she wrote, arranged and produced entirely on her own. For the track she brought in a children's choir to voice a kind of shadow character urging her to "keep pushing" rather than get stuck dwelling on nostalgia or future anxiety.

mitski|love me more.fact: Mitski has said "Love Me More" went through more versions than any other track on her 2022 album Laurel Hell - at various points she and producer Patrick Hyland tried it fast, slow, and even as an old-style country song. After watching The Exorcist, she drew on Mike Oldfield's "Tubular Bells" for the idea of floating a repeating synth ostinato over the chorus, which became the track's signature hook.

my morning jacket|gideon.fact: "Gideon," from My Morning Jacket's 2005 album Z, was recorded at Allaire Studios in New York's Catskill Mountains with producer John Leckie, who had previously helmed landmark albums for Radiohead and the Stone Roses. It marked the Louisville band's first time recording a full album away from Kentucky, pushing their sound toward a more atmospheric, polished direction.

my morning jacket|time waited.fact: Jim James has said the lyrics to "Time Waited" came to him in a dream, where he was in a cafe listening to the song play. Musically, it builds its hook from a sampled piano part lifted from a lost album by pedal-steel virtuoso Buddy Emmons, and it became the first single from My Morning Jacket's 2025 album is, their first collaboration with producer Brendan O'Brien.

nia archives|crowded roomz.fact: "Crowded Roomz," from Nia Archives' 2024 debut album Silence Is Loud, was co-written and co-produced with Ethan P. Flynn, whose other credits include FKA twigs and slowthai, and blends jungle breakbeats with rippling indie-rock guitar. She wrote it after a summer of festival touring, inspired by the feeling of being surrounded by people without feeling truly known by any of them.

nick cave & the bad seeds|frogs.fact: "Frogs" was the first song Nick Cave wrote for the Bad Seeds' 2024 album Wild God, and he's described it as a metaphor for the creative process itself - leaping up toward inspiration again and again, then landing back down, "like a frog jumping onto a lily pad," as he put it, finding real beauty in that return to earth.

nilufer yanya|cold heart.fact: "Cold Heart" grew out of Nilufer Yanya revisiting and reworking a batch of songs with longtime collaborator Wilma Archer after touring behind her 2024 album My Method Actor. She's said the track changed completely from how she first imagined it, built around an open, spacious melody she treated as "a kind of experiment."

obongjayar|sweet danger.fact: "Sweet Danger," from Obongjayar's 2025 album Paradise Now, pairs a spaghetti-Western-style arrangement with Afrobeat rhythm, with the British-Nigerian singer leaning into falsetto choruses over a hypnotically repetitive bassline. Obongjayar has also lent his voice to tracks by Fred Again, Little Simz and Danny Brown.

ora the molecule|loveskatt.fact: "Loveskatt," the project of Norwegian artist Nora Schjelderup, comes from her 2025 album Dance Therapy and centers on the simple urge to build a home and a life with someone you love. The shimmering dance track picked up several official remixes that year, including versions from Midnight Magic, Prince Thomas and Nolan Gray.

parquet courts|freebird ii.fact: Parquet Courts' working title for this Wide Awake! track was "Credits for a Film About the Vietnam War," until someone in the band decided it sounded more like "Freebird 2" - a nod to the way crowds famously heckle bands by shouting "Free Bird" at shows. The joke title stuck even though the song has no actual connection to Lynyrd Skynyrd's ballad.

pavement|trigger cut.fact: "Trigger Cut," the second track on Pavement's 1992 debut Slanted and Enchanted, was released as a single that year and climbed to No. 76 on the UK singles chart, a rare chart showing for the famously lo-fi Matador Records band. Its full title pairs it with a short companion piece, "Wounded-Kite at :17," a tag so odd that even frontman Stephen Malkmus has said he can't remember where it came from.

perfume genius|nothing at all.fact: "Nothing at All," from Perfume Genius's 2020 album Set My Heart on Fire Immediately, was recorded at Sound City Studios in Van Nuys with producer Blake Mills, who brought in veteran session players Jim Keltner, Pino Palladino, Matt Chamberlin and Rob Moose. The same album featured a guest appearance from Phoebe Bridgers and backing vocals from Mike Hadreas's longtime creative partner, Alan Wyffels.

radiohead|morning bell.fact: Even though it appeared on Kid A in 2000, guitarist Ed O'Brien has said the band actually recorded this arrangement of "Morning Bell" after the differently arranged "Morning Bell/Amnesiac" cut that surfaced a year later - the band had simply forgotten they'd already tracked another take of the same song. On Kid A, it's one of the few songs where Radiohead sound like a traditional band playing together in a room, anchored by a driving Phil Selway drum part.

ride|home is a feeling.fact: "Home Is a Feeling" was one of the first two songs Ride released in 2017 when the band reunited after a 20-year hiatus, produced by Erol Alkan. Guitarist Andy Bell said they wanted the track to sound "jet lagged," so everything was recorded using varispeed -- tape sped up or slowed down from normal speed -- and the song was mixed by Alan Moulder, who had also mixed the band's classic 1990 album Nowhere.

sadurn|the weight.fact: "the weight" opens Sadurn's 2025 sophomore album, The Underworld. The Philadelphia project started as G DeGroot's solo bedroom recordings before growing into a full band with guitarist Jon Cox, whose soloing carries the song's widescreen outro alongside DeGroot's voice.

siouxsie and the banshees|hong kong gard.fact: "Hong Kong Garden" was Siouxsie and the Banshees' debut single, released in 1978 and reaching number 7 on the UK chart. It took its name from a real Chinese takeaway in Chislehurst, and its memorable hook was created by guitarist John McKay playing a toy xylophone with the wrong end of the beater while it was switched off, a trick later cited in Q magazine's list of the 100 greatest guitar tracks ever.

smog|cold blooded old times.fact: Bill Callahan's "Cold Blooded Old Times," recorded under his Smog alias for 1999's Knock Knock, reached a much wider audience the following year when it was included on the soundtrack to the hit film High Fidelity, appearing alongside tracks from Bob Dylan, the Velvet Underground and Stevie Wonder.

spoon|she's fine she's mine.fact: Spoon's version of "She's Fine, She's Mine" is a cover of a Bo Diddley original, released on the band's 2023 Memory Dust EP. The recording actually began years earlier during sessions for their Grammy-nominated album Lucifer on the Sofa, but was left unfinished until the band revisited it with fresh energy after touring that record.

stephen malkmus and the jicks|dragonfly.fact: "Dragonfly Pie" opens 2008's Real Emotional Trash, the first Jicks album to feature drummer Janet Weiss, formerly of Sleater-Kinney, who joined the band after previous drummer John Moen left to become a permanent member of the Decemberists.

stereolab|come and play in the milky nig.fact: "Come and Play in the Milky Night" closes Stereolab's 1999 album Cobra and Phases Group Play Voltage in the Milky Night. When the band played its first show in more than a decade in 2024, at the tiny Ramsgate Music Hall in England, this dreamy, low-key track was the one they chose to open the set.

superchunk|watery hands.fact: Superchunk's "Watery Hands," from 1997's Indoor Living, got a music video directed by Phil Morrison starring comedians David Cross and Janeane Garofalo as an overbearing "directing team" who keep forcing absurd, overwrought concepts onto what the band just wants to be a simple performance video.

sylvan esso|look at me.fact: "Look at Me," from Sylvan Esso's 2022 album No Rules Sandy, opens with the sound of a cassette tape rewinding and builds around ticking-clock percussion and woozy, Nintendo 64-inspired synth tones, with singer Amelia Meath repeating the title line 21 times over the course of the track.

t. rex|jeepster.fact: T. Rex's "Jeepster," from 1971's Electric Warrior, borrows its music and opening lines from Howlin' Wolf's "You'll Be Mine" (written by Willie Dixon) -- Marc Bolan openly admitted he'd "lifted it from a Howlin' Wolf song." The single, produced by Tony Visconti, peaked at number 2 on the UK chart.

talking heads|life during wartime.fact: "Life During Wartime," from 1979's Fear of Music, was produced by Brian Eno during his second collaboration with Talking Heads. The song's driving groove grew out of a bass-and-drums jam between Tina Weymouth and Chris Frantz before David Byrne built the rest of the arrangement on top, and it went on to become one of the band's most famous live showpieces.

the apples in stereo|dance floor.fact: "Dance Floor," the lead single from 2010's Travellers in Space and Time, got a music video featuring a cameo from actor Elijah Wood, who had signed the Apples in Stereo to his label, Simian Records, and had previously directed one of the band's earlier videos himself.

the avalanches|all the time in the world.fact: Weezer's Rivers Cuomo reunites with the Avalanches on "All the Time in the World," from their 2026 album No Bad Memories, having previously guested on the group's "Running Red Lights" back in 2020. This time he's joined by producers Vegyn, best known for his production work on Frank Ocean's Blonde and Endless, and Baby Marlboro.

the dance|do dada.fact: The Dance was a mutant-disco/no-wave outfit formed in 1979 when vocalist Eugenie Diserio and guitarist Steve Alexander left the punk band Model Citizens. "Do Dada," a cult favorite from their 1980 Dance for Your Dinner EP, later lent its name to a 2022 compilation gathering the band's scattered early recordings.

the decemberists|once in my life.fact: "Once in My Life," from 2018's I'll Be Your Girl, paired the Decemberists' folk roots with Roxy Music- and New Order-inspired synth textures under producer John Congleton. Its music video was made in collaboration with photographer Autumn De Wilde as a tribute to her brother Jacob, who is 7'2" and lives with Auditory Processing Disorder.

the fall|leave the capitol.fact: "Leave the Capitol" appears on the Fall's 1981 EP Slates, which the band pressed onto 10-inch vinyl specifically because that format was too long to qualify for the UK singles chart and too short for the albums chart -- a loophole that let it register instead on the UK Independent Singles chart, where it reached No. 3. Mark E. Smith later called Slates one of his favorite Fall releases, saying it was aimed at "people who didn't buy records."

the hold steady|sequestered in memphis.fact: "Sequestered in Memphis," the lead single from 2008's Stay Positive, is built on a Tad Kubler guitar riff and Franz Nicolay's organ-and-piano work, topped with a horn section and a big sing-along chorus. It became the Hold Steady's biggest radio hit, drawing more airplay than anything else in their catalog.

the jesus and mary chain|just like honey.fact: The song's famous opening drumbeat is a slowed-down, heavily reverbed recreation of Hal Blaine's intro to the Ronettes' 1963 hit "Be My Baby," played by then-Mary Chain drummer Bobby Gillespie, who later left to front Primal Scream. The track found a huge new audience decades later when Sofia Coppola used it to close out Lost in Translation (2003).

the kills|the good ones.fact: "The Good Ones" was the lead single from the duo's second album, No Wow (2005), and reached number 23 on the UK Singles Chart, making it one of the band's highest-charting singles up to that point. It helped establish the stripped-down, drum-machine-driven blues-rock sound that defined the Jamie Hince/Alison Mosshart duo's early run.

the magnetic fields|born on a train.fact: "Born on a Train" appears on 1994's The Charm of the Highway Strip, a Stephin Merritt concept album where nearly every song revolves around highways, trains, and the restlessness of travel, filtered through synth-pop rather than literal country instrumentation. One reviewer described the track's effect as a fortuitous stretch of radio crosstalk that projects Scott Walker into the middle of the Grand Ole Opry.

the mountain goats|cadaver sniffing dog.fact: "Cadaver Sniffing Dog" comes from 2019's In League with Dragons, an album that began as a planned rock opera about a benevolent wizard ruling a besieged seaside town called Riversend. As John Darnielle's songs took on an unexpectedly noir cast during writing, he joked that the result amounted to inventing a new genre he called "dragon noir."

the national|sea of love.fact: "Sea of Love," from 2013's Trouble Will Find Me, was captured as a one-take live studio performance by the band, a rarity for a group known for meticulous overdubbing. Its music video is a direct parody of Russian band Zvuki Mu's video for their song "Grubyj Zakat."

the rings|i wanna be free.fact: "I Wanna Be Free" was a 1977 single on the UK's Chiswick Records by the short-lived London punk band the Rings, built around singer John "Twink" Alder, a former drummer for psych-rock oddballs the Pink Fairies, alongside guitarist Alan Lee Shaw. After the Rings dissolved, surviving members regrouped as the Maniacs and cut another cult punk single, "Chelsea 77."

the smiths|how soon is now.fact: The song's shimmering, swirling intro came from a studio trick: Johnny Marr recorded a single rhythm guitar part, then he and producer John Porter re-amped that same track through four Fender Twin Reverb amplifiers, each set to a different tremolo speed, to build the pulsating, out-of-sync wobble that opens the song. Keeping all four amps in sync was so difficult that the band had to repeatedly stop and restart the recording.

the smiths|what difference does it make?.fact: The original sleeve for this 1984 single used a publicity still of actor Terence Stamp from the 1965 film The Collector, but Stamp hadn't actually granted permission for its use and initially refused. A limited batch of sleeves was quickly reissued with Morrissey recreating Stamp's pose himself, swapping the prop chloroform pad for a glass of milk, before Stamp relented and the original photo returned for all later pressings.

the strokes|one way trigger.fact: This synth-driven track from Comedown Machine (2013) drew immediate comparisons to a-ha's "Take On Me" thanks to its bubbling keyboard hook and Julian Casablancas pushing his vocal into a glassy falsetto reminiscent of Morten Harket. It also marked the first time an acoustic guitar had appeared on a Strokes recording.

the strokes|you only live once.fact: The track opens First Impressions of Earth (2006), an album the band built around the conceit of an alien seeing Earth for the first time. An alternate take of the song, sung differently and titled "I'll Try Anything Once," turned up as a B-side on the "Heart in a Cage" single.

the vaselines|son of a gun.fact: "Son of a Gun" first appeared on the Glasgow duo's 1987 debut EP. Kurt Cobain was an outspoken fan of the band, and Nirvana's BBC Peel session cover of the song later surfaced on their rarities compilation Incesticide, introducing the tune to a much wider audience than the Vaselines ever reached on their own.

vampire weekend|holiday.fact: "Holiday," from 2010's Contra, is the band's tribute to the Southern California ska-punk records they grew up on, especially Operation Ivy. Its arrangement is deliberately spare next to the band's ornate debut -- just guitar, bass, and drums, with a touch of piano added in the bridge.

velocity girl|sorry again.fact: "Sorry Again" was the lead single from the Maryland shoegaze band's 1994 album Simpatico! and became their best-known song, logging heavy college-radio rotation that year. It later found an unlikely afterlife soundtracking a Volkswagen commercial, giving the otherwise under-the-radar band a rare brush with the mainstream.

weyes blood|something to believe.fact: "Something to Believe" appears on 2019's Titanic Rising, which Natalie Mering recorded with producer Jonathan Rado of Foxygen, a self-described analog-gear devotee. The D'Addario brothers of the Lemon Twigs also contributed to the album's lushly layered, string-filled sessions.

wilco|heavy metal drummer.fact: On this Yankee Hotel Foxtrot (2001) track, Jeff Tweedy looks back fondly on the KISS cover bands he used to watch play outdoor summer shows near his hometown outside St. Louis. He's said the song is partly a mea culpa: as a know-it-all indie kid at the time, he looked down on those bands instead of just enjoying them the way everyone else did.

wilco|someone to lose.fact: Wilco previewed "Someone to Lose," from 2016's Schmilco, by releasing it as an early download exclusively for fans who preordered the album. The band also performed the song on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert ahead of the record's release.

wipers|mystery.fact: "Mystery" comes from the Portland band's 1980 debut, Is This Real?, a record now widely regarded as one of the most influential early American punk albums. Kurt Cobain publicly named Wipers mainman Greg Sage as one of his favorite songwriters, and Husker Du covered Wipers material in their own live sets.

yeah yeah yeahs|cheated hearts.fact: The third single from Show Your Bones (2006) was credited to all three band members, Karen O, Nick Zinner, and Brian Chase. Its music video was crowdsourced entirely from fan-submitted clips of people around the world performing the song themselves, including several men impersonating Karen O.

pavement|shady lane / j vs. s.fact: "Shady Lane" and "J vs. S" are presented as one continuous track on Pavement's 1997 album Brighten the Corners, with the song shifting into a languid instrumental coda (the "J vs. S" half) around the two-and-a-half-minute mark. Released separately as a two-part UK single with a Spike Jonze-directed video, "Shady Lane" became a UK Top 40 hit for the band -- a rare mainstream chart showing for Pavement.

spoon|chateau blues.fact: "Chateau Blues" was co-produced by Justin Meldal-Johnsen (known for his work with Beck and St. Vincent) and marked Spoon's first new music since their Grammy-nominated album Lucifer on the Sofa. It was recorded in Austin, Texas and Providence, Rhode Island, and the band liked it enough to release it immediately as a double A-side single with "Guess I'm Fallin' In Love" in August 2025 rather than wait for a full album.

dazy|ugly.fact: "Ugly" is one of seven newly recorded tracks on Dazy's compilation MAXIMUMBLASTSUPERLOUD Vol. 2: 24 Songs From 2023-2026, released on Lame-O Records. Dazy is largely the solo project of Richmond, Virginia musician James Goodson, and the song leans into a scratchy, late-'90s power-pop feel, mixing radio-static-style guitar effects with gritty, feedback-laced hooks.

radiohead|glass eyes.fact: "Glass Eyes" appears on Radiohead's 2016 album A Moon Shaped Pool, which was recorded at La Fabrique studio in Saint-Remy-de-Provence, France with longtime producer Nigel Godrich. To promote the record, the band released a weekly series of short video vignettes for each song, and "Glass Eyes" was notable for getting two separate visual treatments: one by AV artist Tarik Barri and another directed by the studio Weirdcore.

saya gray|lie down...fact: "LIE DOWN.." closes out Saya Gray's 2025 album SAYA, released via Dirty Hit. The record trades some of her usual synth-heavy sound for acoustic guitars and folk textures, and Gray has cited Joni Mitchell, Led Zeppelin, and The Beatles as influences while writing it during a solo trip across Japan.

ethel cain|janie.fact: "Janie" opens Ethel Cain's second album, Willoughby Tucker, I'll Always Love You (released August 8, 2025), which she wrote and self-produced for her own independent label, Daughters of Cain. The record is billed as a prequel to her 2022 debut Preacher's Daughter, revisiting an earlier chapter of her life before the events of that album.

the decemberists|don't carry it all.fact: "Don't Carry It All" opens The Decemberists' 2011 album The King Is Dead and features guest vocals from bluegrass singer Gillian Welch. The album marked a deliberate step back from the band's more conceptual, theatrical records, embracing a stripped-down Americana sound influenced by R.E.M. and Springsteen.

porridge radio|god of everything else.fact: "God of Everything Else" comes from Porridge Radio's 2024 album Clouds in the Sky They Will Always Be There for Me, produced by Dom Monks (a longtime engineer for Big Thief and Laura Marling) and recorded in Frome, England. Frontwoman Dana Margolin has said every song on the record started life as a poem, as she challenged herself to strip away musical tricks and let the words carry each song.

water from your eyes|playing classics.fact: "Playing Classics" is the second single from Water From Your Eyes' album It's A Beautiful Place, released on Matador Records. The six-minute track started out as an attempt to turn an existing guitar piece into a disco song after bandmate Rachel Brown asked for the album to include a dancefloor number, and the original demo actually ran twelve minutes long.

fontaines d.c.|big.fact: "Big" opens Fontaines D.C.'s 2019 debut album Dogrel, a title borrowed from a once-derided, working-class style of Irish poetry. In under two minutes, singer Grian Chatten declares "Dublin in the rain is mine" and "my childhood was small, but I'm gonna be big," setting up an album steeped in Dublin's changing streets and the influence of James Joyce's Dubliners.

mitski|happy.fact: "Happy" appears on Mitski's 2016 album Puberty 2. Mitski has explained the song imagines happiness as a visitor who shows up, stays a while, and then always leaves again, calling it a song about "this exhaustive and exhausting cycle" of chasing good feelings only to come back down from them.

father john misty|chloe.fact: "Chloe" is the opening track on Father John Misty's 2022 album Chloe and the Next 20th Century. Critics have described it as sounding like "the best Harry Nilsson song Harry Nilsson never wrote," built around silvery violins and cartoonish horns to paint a character portrait of the song's title subject.

alabama shakes|sound and color.fact: The title track of Alabama Shakes' 2015 album Sound & Color was recorded at Nashville's Sound Emporium, with the band co-producing alongside Blake Mills. The group spent over a year in the studio without having any new songs written in advance, and the shimmering, atmospheric title track signaled a deliberate expansion beyond their earlier soul-and-blues-rock sound.

of montreal|requiem for o.m.m.2.fact: "Requiem for O.M.M.2" opens of Montreal's 2005 album The Sunlandic Twins. The title plays on the band's own initials, and despite its breezy, carousel-like melody and giddy hooks, frontman Kevin Barnes packs the brief two-minute song with more musical ideas than some bands fit on a whole album.

curtis harding|the power.fact: "The Power" comes from Curtis Harding's 2025 album Departures & Arrivals: Adventures of Captain Curt, which he self-produced at Adrian Quesada's Electric Deluxe Recorders in Austin for ANTI- Records. Harding has described the roller-disco-inspired track as "a release valve," a way to push back against the weight of the world and still find joy, within an album loosely following a pilot's sci-fi journey home.

cass mccombs|that's that.fact: "That's That" appears on Cass McCombs' 2007 album Dropping the Writ, released on Domino Records. The song follows a narrator on a southbound road trip with an older companion, building a modest new life together, rendered with an understated, disarmingly tender pop touch.

cocteau twins|ivo.fact: "Ivo" opens Cocteau Twins' 1984 album Treasure and is a dedication to Ivo Watts-Russell, co-founder of their record label 4AD. The album's title itself works as both an adjective, describing the endlessly inventive melodic lines throughout the record, and an invitation for listeners to treasure it for years to come.

cocteau twins|iceblink luck.fact: "Iceblink Luck" was released as a single from Cocteau Twins' 1990 album Heaven or Las Vegas and peaked at No. 38 on the UK Singles Chart, the band's second single to crack the Top 40. It pointed toward a more accessible, pop-leaning direction for the group's famously ethereal sound.

mars|helen forsdale.fact: "Helen Forsdale" was one of four Mars tracks included on the Brian Eno-curated 1978 compilation No New York, a landmark document of New York's abrasive no wave scene. The song is built on a maniacally ascending bassline with shrieking, scraped guitar and half-chanted vocals, typifying the band's deliberately anti-rock, experimental approach.

model/actriz|diva.fact: "Diva" is the lead single from Model/Actriz's 2025 sophomore album Pirouette, released via True Panther and Dirty Hit. Frontman Cole Haden said the song came together unusually fast in the studio, with the lyrics written spontaneously in the booth rather than through the band's usual meticulous writing process. The Brooklyn-based group formed in 2016 when members first connected while attending Berklee College of Music in Boston.

panda bear|ferry lady.fact: "Ferry Lady" is a single from Panda Bear's 2025 album Sinister Grift, Noah Lennox's first solo album in five years, released on Domino Records. The dubby, psychedelic-pop track was created working alongside his Animal Collective bandmate Josh "Deakin" Dibb at Lennox's home studio in Lisbon, Portugal, and its music video was directed by longtime collaborator Danny Perez.

wild pink|fences of stonehenge.fact: "The Fences of Stonehenge" is the opening track and lead single from Wild Pink's album Dulling the Thorns, released via Fire Talk. Frontman John Ross said the song is about "figuring out what to do when you realize you outgrew a lot of stuff you used to like," and its driving, rock-forward sound marked a shift from the band's earlier, more ambient style.

royel otis|adored.fact: "Adored" opens Royel Otis's 2024 debut album Pratts & Pain, produced by Grammy-winning producer Dan Carey. The album takes its name from a South London pub near Carey's home studio where the Australian duo often worked out song ideas while recording.

the avalanches|all the time in the world.fact: "All the Time in the World" features Weezer frontman Rivers Cuomo alongside producers Vegyn and Baby Marlboro, and appears on The Avalanches' 2026 album No Bad Memories, the Australian sample-collage group's first album in six years. The sprawling, 31-track record is packed with guest appearances, including Jamie xx, Mike Patton, and Karen O, continuing the duo's signature style of stitching together samples from decades of recorded music.

perfume genius|clean heart.fact: "Clean Heart" is the third single from Perfume Genius's seventh album Glory (2025), released on Matador Records. Mike Hadreas recorded the hopeful, swelling track with producer Blake Mills and his longtime partner and musical collaborator Alan Wyffels, and the album also features a guest appearance from singer Aldous Harding.

madi diaz|god person.fact: "God Person" is the seventh track on Madi Diaz's 2024 album Weird Faith. In the stripped-down, minimalist song, Diaz pictures herself in the back pew of a church watching a congregation sing hymns with their eyes closed, using the image to explore her own ongoing search for spiritual connection.

sharon van etten and the attachment theo.fact: "Southern Life (What It Must Be Like)" comes from Sharon Van Etten's 2025 debut album with her new band, The Attachment Theory. Van Etten said the song is about trying to understand people with very different perspectives and backgrounds while extending compassion to your past, present, and future self; it came together quickly during a band jam session in Yucca Valley, California.

lambchop|up with people.fact: "Up With People" appears on Lambchop's 2000 album Nixon. The song's title and horn-and-handclap-driven, gospel-tinged sound were inspired by the real "Up with People" singing group, a wholesome traveling youth choir from the Nixon era famous for performing at Super Bowl halftime shows, which frontman Kurt Wagner used as a jumping-off point for one of the album's most euphoric tracks.

king gizzard and the lizard wizard|gamma.fact: "Gamma Knife" is the lead single from King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard's 2016 album Nonagon Infinity, recorded at Daptone Studios in Brooklyn. The song is built around an unusual 11/8 time signature and a drum breakdown drummer Michael Cavanagh was initially hesitant to attempt. It later placed 61st on Triple J's Hottest 100 for 2016, and filmmaker Edgar Wright has named it his favorite King Gizzard song, saying he'd love to use it in a future Baby Driver film.

the flaming lips|the w.a.n.d. (the will.fact: "The W.A.N.D. (The Will Always Negates Defeat)" is a single from The Flaming Lips' 2006 album At War with the Mystics. The riff-driven track became one of the band's more widely heard songs thanks to its use in Dell computer commercials and in the video games Major League Baseball 2K8 and NBA 2K16.

big thief|words.fact: "Words" is the second track on Big Thief's 2025 album Double Infinity, recorded over three weeks at New York's Power Station studios with producer Dom Monks. The song is a moody meditation on language itself, built around interlocking guitar lines, and its music video was directed by Noah Lenker, the brother of Big Thief singer Adrianne Lenker, marking the band's first non-live-performance video since 2017.

spellling|alibi.fact: "Alibi" is a single from SPELLLING's (Chrystia Cabral) 2025 album Portrait of My Heart, released on Sacred Bones. The power-chord-driven track features a guest appearance from Pat McCrory of the hardcore band Turnstile, and Cabral has said she drew on singer-songwriter Liz Phair's candid, direct lyricism while writing it.

beach house|norway.fact: "Norway" was written in 2008 after Norwegian broadcaster NRK commissioned Beach House to write a song inspired by the country's landscape, which the duo composed while riding a train between Bergen and Oslo. It became the lead single from their acclaimed 2010 album Teen Dream, and its accompanying short film, "Snorway," was inspired by the famous Dark Side of the Rainbow pairing of The Wizard of Oz with Pink Floyd's Dark Side of the Moon.

future islands|thrill.fact: "Thrill" is the penultimate track on Future Islands' 2020 album As Long As You Are, recorded with engineer Steve Wright at Wrightway Studios in Baltimore. It's a somber, synth-laden song anchored by frontman Samuel T. Herring's deep vocal performance, and its self-directed music video is simply a static close-up shot of Herring singing.

saintseneca|sweet nothing.fact: "Sweet Nothing" is a single from Saintseneca's 2025 album Highwalllow & Supermoon Songs, the Columbus, Ohio band's first album in more than seven years. Frontman Zac Little wrote the breezy song while on his honeymoon with his wife, Leticia Wiggins, and the record was produced by Mike Mogis, known for his work with Bright Eyes and Rilo Kiley.

beck|wave.fact: "Wave" became the centerpiece of Beck's 2014 album Morning Phase — he'd had the song sitting around for years from an earlier, shelved project, and once he saw how people reacted to it, he built the rest of the album around its mood. The basic tracks were cut in Los Angeles over just three days with longtime collaborators Smokey Hormel, Justin Meldal-Johnsen, and Joey Waronker, with orchestral arrangements by Beck's father, composer David Campbell. The song made its live debut at a Song Reader concert at Walt Disney Concert Hall in November 2013.

justice|flower in a hurricane (ft. tame.fact: "Flower In A Hurricane" is a 2026 single on which French duo Justice teamed up with Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard, written to score the launch trailer for Grand Theft Auto VI. The track leans into an '80s synth-rock sound, with a dramatic opening riff that critics compared to Dire Straits' "Money for Nothing." It continues a partnership between Justice and Tame Impala that began with the Grammy-winning "Neverender" from Justice's 2024 album Hyperdrama.

arlo parks|impurities.fact: "Impurities" comes from Arlo Parks' 2023 album My Soft Machine and was co-written with BROCKHAMPTON producer Romil Hemnani and Carter Lang. Parks has said the idea came together the night she first met Romil while out with friends, and the song is about the comfort of being around people who make you feel accepted, laughter and all. Musically it blends dreamy synths and drum machines with Parks' crisp, clear vocal delivery.

guerilla toss|ceo of personal and pleasu.fact: "CEO of Personal & Pleasure" is track three on Guerilla Toss's 2025 album You're Weird Now, released on Sub Pop. Frontwoman Kassie Carlson has described the song as being about letting go of her inner critic and taking charge of her own happiness, even when that process feels a little chaotic. The track is built on synthy, psychedelic pop grooves played in an unusual, off-kilter time signature.

spoon|inside out.fact: "Inside Out" appears on Spoon's 2014 album They Want My Soul and started life as a simple piano-and-vocal song that frontman Britt Daniel had carried around for a long time before the band built it up in the studio. The finished version layers synthesizers meant to emulate strings and harp tones, with Spoon drawing some of its punchy beat and harpsichord-like synth sound from an unexpected source: Dr. Dre production techniques. Keyboardist Alex Fischel, who'd joined the band from Britt Daniel's side project Divine Fits, contributed the song's glistening keyboard solos, and it went on to become Spoon's most-streamed song.

2nd grade|fender boys.fact: "Fender Boys" is track 11 on 2nd Grade's 2026 album Girls and Boys, their debut for Philadelphia's own Lame-O Records. The album is a concept record split into two halves — ten songs about different kinds of girls followed by ten songs about different kinds of boys — and "Fender Boys" opens the "boys" side. Like every song on the record, it was written by 2nd Grade frontman Peter Gill.

alex g|walk away.fact: "Walk Away" opens (Sandy) Alex G's 2019 album House of Sugar and is the record's longest track, built around just two repeated lines of lyrics stretched out over more than four minutes. The arrangement starts with a pitched-up vocal wail before backward-sounding ("backmasked") drums, guitar, piano, and keyboard are introduced one layer at a time until they all swirl together. It's a distinctive, slow-build intro to an album known for its unusual production tricks.

jim james|state of art (a.e.i.o.u.).fact: "State Of The Art (A.E.I.O.U.)" opens My Morning Jacket frontman Jim James's 2013 solo debut, Regions of Light and Sound of God. The album was self-produced and recorded at James's own home studio in Louisville, Kentucky, with James playing nearly every instrument himself aside from strings and drums. The track begins with the sound of a needle dropping on vinyl before James builds a hypnotic piano part up one layer at a time into a funk-tinged groove.

the strokes|at the door.fact: "At The Door" was released in February 2020 as the lead single from The Strokes' sixth album, The New Abnormal, produced by Rick Rubin and recorded at Shangri-La Studios in Malibu. It was a deliberately unexpected choice to kick off the band's first new album rollout in seven years: the song is moody and synth-driven, with almost no percussion and little guitar, closer in feel to Julian Casablancas' solo work than classic Strokes. The New Abnormal's cover art features the painting "Bird on Money" by Jean-Michel Basquiat.

wolf parade|this heart's on fire.fact: "This Heart's On Fire" closes out Wolf Parade's 2005 debut album, Apologies to the Queen Mary, released on Sub Pop. Written and sung by Dan Boeckner, the track has been compared to Bruce Springsteen's big, anthemic arena-rock era, serving as the album's dramatic send-off. The record was recorded with producer Howard Bilerman (known for his work with Arcade Fire) at Hotel2Tango studio in Montreal.

angel olsen|big time.fact: "Big Time" is the waltzing title track of Angel Olsen's 2022 album, co-written with her partner, musician Beau Thibodeaux. Over gently swaying, waltz-time chords, Olsen sings plainly about the joy of new love: "I'm loving you big time, I'm loving you more." The song marked a warmer, more open turn in Olsen's songwriting after several albums built around more guarded, enigmatic lyrics.

vampire weekend|cousins.fact: "Cousins" was the first single from Vampire Weekend's 2010 album Contra. The band wrote and recorded it while on tour in Mexico City and had it ready to debut live just days later in Guadalajara. Keyboardist Rostam Batmanglij called it bassist Chris Baio's most demanding bass part and drummer Chris Tomson's most demanding drum part to that point, and the music video has the band members swapping masks of each other's faces while rotating on a moving platform in a New York City alley.

duster|constellations.fact: "Constellations" is track eight on Duster's 1998 debut album, Stratosphere, recorded by the San Jose, California band in a makeshift home studio they nicknamed "Low Space Orbit." The song exemplifies Duster's minimalist slowcore sound — droning basslines, quiet vocals, and simple guitar parts — and its space-themed title was popular enough that it was later used to name the splatter-vinyl color variant released for the album's 25th-anniversary reissue.

pile|scaling walls.fact: "Scaling Walls" opens Pile's 2024 EP Hot Air Balloon, which was recorded during the same sessions as the Boston band's 2023 full-length, All Fiction. The track builds from plaintive verses into a towering climax, with synthesizers growing from a background whine into a full howl underneath buzzing, swelling guitars and singer-guitarist Rick Maguire's agile vocal performance.

the avalanches|highfield (feat. panda be.fact: "Highfield," featuring Animal Collective's Panda Bear, is one of 31 tracks on The Avalanches' 2026 album No Bad Memories, the Australian sample-collage group's fourth record. The album as a whole is built around the strangely nostalgic pull of advertising jingles, startup chimes, and other half-remembered commercial sounds from childhood, presented as a dense collage of fragments and full songs.

the beths|i'm not getting excited.fact: "I'm Not Getting Excited" comes from The Beths' 2020 album Jump Rope Gazers. Singer Elizabeth Stokes wrote it about the gap between external achievements and internal self-doubt — essentially, imposter syndrome — noting that people often ask "are you excited?" about good things happening in her life when the honest answer is complicated. The song's music video was filmed during the first month of New Zealand's COVID-19 lockdown and plays out as an animated collage of spooky "night terrors."

alex g|treehouse.fact: Alex G recorded "Treehouse" with singer Emily Yacina around 2011, and it stayed unofficial for years. After the song became popular as a TikTok sound, it received an official release in 2022 as a non-album single.

alvvays|dreams tonite.fact: "Dreams Tonite" is the second track on Alvvays' 2017 album Antisocialites and was released as a single in July 2017. Molly Rankin and Alec O'Hanley wrote all the album's songs, and the song earned a 2018 SOCAN Songwriting Prize nomination.

angel olsen|it's every season (whole new.fact: This version is an alternate take of the title track from Angel Olsen's 2020 album Whole New Mess. She recorded it during the All Mirrors sessions, and it adds drums, bass and brass arranged by Nate Walcott. It was the lead single for the 2021 box set Song of the Lark and Other Far Memories.

bat for lashes|prescilla.fact: "Prescilla" is one of four singles from Bat for Lashes' 2006 debut album Fur and Gold, along with "The Wizard," "Trophy" and "What's a Girl to Do?" It is the seventh track on the album.

beach fossils|sleep apnea.fact: "Sleep Apnea" is the third track on Beach Fossils' second album, Clash the Truth, released February 19, 2013, on Captured Tracks. The band later released a bossa nova version of the song with a saxophone solo.

beck|dreams.fact: Beck released "Dreams" in June 2015 as the first single from the album that became Colors. He wrote it with producer Greg Kurstin and Andrew Wyatt, and Beck and Kurstin played all the instruments and sang all the vocals themselves.

beck|morning.fact: "Morning" is from Beck's 2014 album Morning Phase, a companion to his 2002 album Sea Change. The album won Album of the Year at the 2015 Grammy Awards, along with Best Rock Album and Best Engineered Album, Non-Classical.

beck|devil's haircut.fact: "Devil's Haircut" was the second single from Beck's 1996 album Odelay, co-produced by Beck and the Dust Brothers. It reached No. 22 on the UK Singles Chart and No. 23 on the US Modern Rock Tracks chart.

cocteau twins|cherry-coloured funk.fact: "Cherry-Coloured Funk" opens the Cocteau Twins album Heaven or Las Vegas, released by 4AD in September 1990. Robin Guthrie produced it, and it was recorded at September Sound in London.

deerhunter|never stops.fact: "Never Stops" is the third track on Deerhunter's 2008 album Microcastle. The band recorded the album in about one week in April 2008 at Rare Book Room Studios in Brooklyn with producer Nicolas Vernhes.

dilly dally|desire.fact: "Desire" was the lead single from Dilly Dally's debut album Sore and is its opening track. The Toronto band released the album on October 9, 2015, through Partisan Records in the US and Buzz Records in Canada.

esther rose|new bad.fact: "New Bad" is the lead single from Esther Rose's 2025 album Want on New West Records. Ross Farbe of Video Age produced the album, which was recorded live to tape at the Bomb Shelter in Nashville.
