fleet foxes|fool's errand.fact: "Fool's Errand" was the second single from Fleet Foxes' 2017 album Crack-Up, released May 12, 2017. Robin Pecknold wrote all the songs and co-produced the album with Skyler Skjelset, and the video was shot on 35mm film.

future islands|swept inside.fact: "Swept Inside" is from Future Islands' second album, In Evening Air, released in March 2010 on Thrill Jockey. It has remained a regular part of the band's live sets.

james chance and the contortions|design.fact: "Design to Kill" opens the 1979 album Buy, released on ZE Records. James Chance wrote every track and produced the record, and played saxophone and keyboards on it. The album followed the band's appearance on the 1978 compilation No New York.

kevin morby|javelin.fact: "Javelin" is the lead single from Kevin Morby's 2026 album Little Wide Open, released on Dead Oceans. The album was produced by Aaron Dessner. Amelia Meath of Sylvan Esso and Mountain Man built a multi-tracked choir of backing vocals for the song.

lcd soundsystem|home.fact: "Home" is the 7:53 closing track of LCD Soundsystem's 2010 album This Is Happening. James Murphy produced the album between April 2009 and February 2010 in Los Angeles and New York City. The album reached No. 10 on the US Billboard 200 and No. 7 on the UK Albums Chart.

my morning jacket|wordless chorus.fact: "Wordless Chorus" opens My Morning Jacket's 2005 album Z, their first made with an outside producer, John Leckie. The band recorded it at Allaire Studios in the Catskill Mountains of New York instead of at home in Louisville. Guitarist Carl Broemel and keyboardist Bo Koster joined the band for this album.

my morning jacket|lay low.fact: "Lay Low" appears on My Morning Jacket's 2005 album Z, produced by John Leckie and Jim James. It was the band's first album with a professional producer. It was recorded at Allaire Studios in Shokan, New York, in the Catskill Mountains.

nation of language|too much enough.fact: "Too Much, Enough" was a single from Nation of Language's third album, Strange Disciple, released in 2023. The Brooklyn synth-pop trio made a video for it directed by Robert Kolodny. It features Jimmi Simpson, Reggie Watts, Kevin Morby, Tomberlin and Adam Green.

of montreal|i was a landscape in your dr.fact: The track is listed as "I Was a Landscape in Your Dream" on of Montreal's 2005 album The Sunlandic Twins, released on Polyvinyl. Kevin Barnes recorded the album almost entirely himself between May and October 2004, in Athens, Georgia and Oslo, Norway. Barnes is also the credited producer.

pavement|date with ikea.fact: "Date w/ IKEA" is on Pavement's 1997 album Brighten the Corners. It was written and sung by Scott Kannberg, also known as Spiral Stairs. The album was recorded in July 1996 at Mitch Easter's Drive-In Studio in Winston-Salem, North Carolina.

radiohead|stop whispering.fact: Radiohead re-recorded "Stop Whispering" for its US single release because they were unhappy with the Pablo Honey album version. Ed O'Brien said the new version was more atmospheric and compared it to Joy Division. The single came out in October 1993 and peaked at No. 23 on the US Modern Rock chart.

ratboys|anywhere.fact: "Anywhere" was released in October 2025 as the lead single from Ratboys' sixth album, Singin' to an Empty Chair, due in February 2026 on New West Records. The song was inspired by guitarist Dave Sagan's anxiously attached family dog. Julia Steiner and Sagan formed the band in 2010 after meeting at freshman orientation at Notre Dame.

sigur ros|gobbledigook.fact: "Gobbledigook" opens Sigur Ros's 2008 album Med sud i eyrum vid spilum endalaust and was its lead single. The band produced the album with Flood, and recorded it in New York, London and Havana. The album was released on XL Recordings in June 2008.

sleater-kinney|i wanna be your joey ramo.fact: "I Wanna Be Your Joey Ramone" is on Sleater-Kinney's 1996 album Call the Doctor, released on Chainsaw Records. The album was recorded in about four days in September 1995 with producer John Goodmanson. It has no bass player, and the songs were written for two guitars.

sonic youth|sunday.fact: "Sunday" was the only single from Sonic Youth's 1998 album A Thousand Leaves, released on Geffen. Its music video was directed by Harmony Korine and starred Macaulay Culkin. The single reached number 72 on the UK Singles Chart.

st. vincent|strange mercy.fact: "Strange Mercy" is the title track of St. Vincent's 2011 album on 4AD. Annie Clark recorded the album with producer John Congleton at Elmwood Studio in her hometown of Dallas, and it peaked at number 19 on the Billboard 200, her highest placement up to that point.

tame impala|desire be desire go.fact: "Desire Be, Desire Go" is a re-recording of a song first released on Tame Impala's self-titled EP. The 2010 album Innerspeaker was recorded mostly at Wave House in Western Australia from June to August 2009, with Kevin Parker performing all the instruments and producing it himself. The album peaked at number 4 on the ARIA Albums chart.

the beths|dying to believe.fact: "Dying to Believe" was the lead single from the New Zealand band The Beths' second album, Jump Rope Gazers (2020). Its music video is a four-step instructional parody titled "How to be the Beths," featuring the band members.

the cure|just like heaven.fact: "Just Like Heaven" was the third single from The Cure's 1987 album Kiss Me, Kiss Me, Kiss Me. It became the band's first American Top 40 hit, peaking at number 40 on the Billboard Hot 100.

the cure|fire in cairo.fact: "Fire in Cairo" appears on The Cure's debut album Three Imaginary Boys, released by Fiction Records on 8 May 1979. The album was recorded at Morgan Studios in London, produced by Chris Parry, and reached number 44 on the UK Albums Chart.

the decemberists|the rake's song.fact: "The Rake's Song" is on The Decemberists' 2009 album The Hazards of Love, released on Capitol Records. The album debuted at number 14 on the Billboard 200, selling roughly 19,000 copies in its first week.

the kills|sour cherry.fact: "Sour Cherry" is the ninth track on The Kills' 2008 album Midnight Boom, which was recorded in 2007 at the Key Club Recording Company in Benton Harbor, Michigan. The song was later featured in an episode of Gossip Girl and in the film The House Bunny.

the mars volta|inertiatic esp.fact: "Inertiatic ESP" is from The Mars Volta's 2003 debut album De-Loused in the Comatorium, co-produced by Rick Rubin and guitarist Omar Rodriguez-Lopez. Red Hot Chili Peppers bassist Flea played bass on most of the album, and the song was released as a single in September 2003.

the microphones|the glow.fact: The Microphones' album The Glow, Pt. 2 was recorded on 16-track analog tape at Dub Narcotic in Olympia, Washington, between May 2000 and March 2001. Phil Elverum played most of the instruments himself, and K Records released it on September 11, 2001. Pitchfork later named it the best album of 2001.

the replacements|favorite thing.fact: "Favorite Thing" is the fourth track on The Replacements' 1984 album Let It Be, running just 2:19. The album title reportedly came from the band agreeing to name it after the next song to play on the radio, which happened to be the Beatles' "Let It Be." It was produced by Steve Fjelstad, Paul Westerberg, and Peter Jesperson.

the white stripes|my doorbell.fact: "My Doorbell" was the second single from The White Stripes' 2005 album Get Behind Me Satan and was recorded in March 2005 at Third Man Studios. It reached number 10 on the UK Singles chart and earned a 2006 Grammy nomination. The black-and-white video, directed by The Malloys, was filmed at the Magic Castle in Hollywood with the duo playing for a crowd of children.

tv on the radio|golden age.fact: "Golden Age" was the first single from TV on the Radio's 2008 album Dear Science, released August 26, 2008 on 4AD and produced by Dave Sitek. Rolling Stone ranked it number 12 on its list of the 100 best songs of 2008, and the band Phish began covering it in concert in 2009.

yo la tengo|aselestine.fact: "Aselestine" is the fourth track on Yo La Tengo's 2023 album This Stupid World, released as its second single on January 11, 2023. The album was recorded at the band's own studio space in Hoboken, New Jersey and produced by the band, with C. J. Camerieri playing French horn on the track.

green day|nice guys finish last.fact: Nice Guys Finish Last opens Green Day's 1997 album Nimrod and was its fourth and final single. It was used in the 1999 football movie Varsity Blues, and its video shows the band as a mock football team parodying the Green Bay Packers, with a voice-over imitating NFL Films narrator John Facenda.

enrique iglesias|i like it.fact: I Like It, from Enrique Iglesias's 2010 album Euphoria, features Pitbull and was produced by RedOne, who co-wrote it with both artists. It interpolates Lionel Richie's 1983 hit All Night Long, reached the top ten in the US, and hit No. 4 in the UK.

the breeders|cannonball.fact: Cannonball was the lead single from The Breeders' 1993 album Last Splash. Kim Deal wrote it and co-produced it with Mark Freegard, and it reached No. 44 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 2 on the Alternative Songs chart. The video was directed by Spike Jonze and Kim Gordon.

a tribe called quest|check the rhime.fact: Check the Rhime was the first single from A Tribe Called Quest's 1991 second album, The Low End Theory. Written by Q-Tip, Phife Dawg and Ali Shaheed Muhammad, it hit No. 1 on Billboard's Hot Rap Songs chart and was certified Gold by the RIAA.

kenny rogers & sheena easton|we've got t.fact: We've Got Tonight was written by Bob Seger, whose own version from the 1978 album Stranger in Town peaked at No. 13 on the Hot 100. Kenny Rogers and Sheena Easton recorded it as a duet in 1983 at the suggestion of their label chairman, and it topped the country chart.

james brown|living in america.fact: Living in America was written by Dan Hartman and Charlie Midnight and released in December 1985 for the film Rocky IV, where James Brown performs it during Apollo Creed's ring entrance. It reached No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100 and won Brown a Grammy for Best Male R&B Vocal Performance.

abba|thank you for the music.fact: Thank You for the Music is on ABBA's 1977 album ABBA: The Album, and was one of three songs from the mini-musical The Girl with the Golden Hair, performed on their 1977 tour. It was not a UK single until November 1983, when it became a minor top-forty hit.

jefferson airplane|somebody to love.fact: Somebody to Love was written by Darby Slick and first recorded in 1966 by the Great Society, with his sister-in-law Grace Slick singing. When she joined Jefferson Airplane she brought the song along, and it became a top-ten hit from their 1967 album Surrealistic Pillow.

america|a horse with no name.fact: A Horse with No Name was written by Dewey Bunnell and released in late 1971 in Europe and early 1972 in the US. Many listeners thought it was Neil Young because of the vocal resemblance, and it knocked Young's Heart of Gold out of the No. 1 spot on the Billboard Hot 100.

herman's hermits|there's a kind of hush.fact: There's a Kind of Hush was written by Les Reed and Geoff Stephens, whose group the New Vaudeville Band recorded it first in 1967. Herman's Hermits' version, produced by Mickie Most, reached No. 4 in the US, and the Carpenters took it back into the charts in 1976.

beck|nobody's fault but my own.fact: Nobody's Fault but My Own is from Beck's 1998 album Mutations, which he produced with Nigel Godrich. Critics have described it as a psychedelic raga built on open-tuned guitar and sitar, and it was released as a single in Japan in 1999.

bjork|it's oh so quiet.fact: Bjork's It's Oh So Quiet, from her 1995 album Post, is a cover of a 1951 Betty Hutton song, which itself was an English-language version of the German song Und jetzt ist es still, recorded by Horst Winter in 1948. Spike Jonze directed the video, and the single reached No. 4 in the UK.

superchunk|hello hawk.fact: Hello Hawk was the first single from Superchunk's 1999 album Come Pick Me Up, which was produced by Jim O'Rourke. The album's title comes from a line in the song, and the arrangement adds strings and horns to the band's usual guitar sound.

de la soul|me myself and i.fact: Me Myself and I, released in 1989 from De La Soul's debut album 3 Feet High and Rising, is built on a sample of Funkadelic's (Not Just) Knee Deep, an idea from Prince Paul and Maseo. It was the group's only No. 1 on the Billboard R&B chart.

haim|summer girl.fact: Summer Girl, released by Haim in July 2019, was co-produced by Ariel Rechtshaid and Rostam Batmanglij. The band has said its gentle groove was inspired by Lou Reed's Walk on the Wild Side, and its music video was directed by Paul Thomas Anderson.

barry white|can't get enough of your lov.fact: Can't Get Enough of Your Love, Babe was released in June 1974 as the first single from Barry White's third album, Can't Get Enough. It topped both the Billboard Hot 100 and R&B charts, replacing Eric Clapton's I Shot the Sheriff at No. 1.

gary lewis & the playboys|green grass.fact: Green Grass was written by the British songwriting duo Roger Cook and Roger Greenaway and released by Gary Lewis & the Playboys in 1966 on Liberty Records. It reached No. 8 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 1 in Canada.

desmond dekker and the aces|(poor mi) is.fact: Israelites, written by Desmond Dekker and producer Leslie Kong, reached No. 1 on the UK Singles Chart in spring 1969, widely described as the first reggae song to do so. It also climbed to No. 9 on the US Billboard Hot 100 that June.

boston|don't look back.fact: Don't Look Back is the title track of Boston's 1978 second album, and it reached No. 4 on the Hot 100. Tom Scholz has said he made no demo and worked the song out directly on the master tape. It is the only track on the album without drums, with Brad Delp singing all the vocals.

u2|mysterious ways.fact: Mysterious Ways, from U2's 1991 album Achtung Baby, began as a jam called Sick Puppy, and the band at first liked only Adam Clayton's bass part. The Edge's funky, wah-flavored guitar came from a sound he found on his gear, and the song spent a then-record nine weeks atop Billboard's Modern Rock Tracks chart.

the everly brothers|wake up little susie.fact: Wake Up Little Susie was written by the husband-and-wife team Felice and Boudleaux Bryant and released by the Everly Brothers on Cadence Records in September 1957. It went to No. 1 on the Billboard pop chart and spent seven weeks at the top of the country chart. The Bryants wrote 29 songs for the duo.

the white stripes|there's no home for yo.fact: There's No Home for You Here opens the White Stripes' 2003 album Elephant, which Jack White produced. It was recorded at Toe Rag Studios in London on an eight-track recorder, and Jack White has said they pushed that equipment as far as it could go with heavy overdubbing.

drifters|up on the roof.fact: Up on the Roof was written by Gerry Goffin and Carole King and recorded by the Drifters in 1962 with Rudy Lewis on lead vocal. Produced by Leiber and Stoller, it reached No. 5 on the US pop chart in early 1963. Carole King, James Taylor and Laura Nyro have all recorded it too.

billie eilish|bad guy.fact: bad guy, from Billie Eilish's 2019 debut album When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?, was written with and produced by her brother Finneas O'Connell. It hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in August 2019, ending the 19-week run of Old Town Road, and it won both Record of the Year and Song of the Year at the 2020 Grammys.

foo fighters|up in arms.fact: Up in Arms is on Foo Fighters' 1997 album The Colour and the Shape. It is one of only two songs on the record that still features original drummer William Goldsmith, because Dave Grohl re-recorded most of the other drum parts himself.

genesis|land of confusion.fact: Land of Confusion, from Genesis's 1986 album Invisible Touch, reached No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100. Its music video used caricature puppets from the British TV show Spitting Image and won the Grammy for Best Concept Music Video.

john parr|st. elmo's fire (man in motion.fact: St. Elmo's Fire (Man in Motion) was written by John Parr and David Foster for the 1985 film St. Elmo's Fire, and Foster produced it. It reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in September 1985 and earned Parr a Grammy nomination.

the dandy warhols|we used to be friends.fact: We Used to Be Friends was the lead single from The Dandy Warhols' 2003 album Welcome to the Monkey House. It became the theme song of the TV series Veronica Mars and reached No. 18 on the UK Singles chart.

bruce springsteen|born to run.fact: Born to Run, the title track of Bruce Springsteen's 1975 album, took months of sessions in 1974 at 914 Sound Studios in New York, with as many as eleven guitar tracks layered on it. It is his most-performed live song, and it was part of the Super Bowl XLIII halftime show in 2009.

u2|all because of you.fact: All Because of You is the sixth track on U2's 2004 album How to Dismantle an Atomic Bomb and was released as a single in 2005. It was produced by Steve Lillywhite, mixed by Flood, and reached No. 6 on the US Modern Rock chart. The video shows the band playing on a flatbed truck driving from Manhattan to Brooklyn.

big time rush|music sounds better with u.fact: Music Sounds Better with U, from Big Time Rush's 2011 album Elevate, features rapper Mann and was produced by Ryan Tedder. Its credits include Thomas Bangalter and Alain Quême of the French duo Stardust, whose 1998 hit Music Sounds Better with You inspired it.

carly simon|nobody does it better.fact: Nobody Does It Better was the theme to the 1977 James Bond film The Spy Who Loved Me, with music by Marvin Hamlisch and lyrics by Carole Bayer Sager. It was the first Bond theme since Dr. No (1962) with a title different from the film's. It peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 and was nominated for an Oscar for Best Original Song.

alanis morissette|hand in my pocket.fact: Hand in My Pocket, from Alanis Morissette's 1995 album Jagged Little Pill, was written by Morissette and producer Glen Ballard. It was her first No. 1 in Canada and topped the US Alternative Airplay chart. It was once considered as the theme for the Dawson's Creek pilot.

foals|my number.fact: My Number, from Foals' 2013 album Holy Fire, was produced by Flood and Alan Moulder. It reached No. 23 on the UK Singles chart, the band's highest-charting single at that point, and was certified double platinum in the UK.

the roots|don't feel right.fact: Don't Feel Right was the lead single from The Roots' 2006 album Game Theory. It first circulated online as a free download in May 2006, and features a hook sung by Maimouna Youssef with ?uestlove on drums.

chromatics|shadow.fact: Shadow by Chromatics was released in September 2015 through Adult Swim's singles series. It was written for their planned album Dear Tommy, which never came out, and it later gained wider attention when it was featured in Twin Peaks: The Return.

dave matthews band|stay (wasting time).fact: Stay (Wasting Time) is the second single from Dave Matthews Band's 1998 album Before These Crowded Streets, produced by Steve Lillywhite. It spent seven weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Adult Alternative chart and peaked at No. 8 on the Modern Rock chart.

lionel richie|hello.fact: Hello, from Lionel Richie's 1983 album Can't Slow Down, was released as a single in February 1984. It hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent six weeks at No. 1 in the UK. Its music video, directed by Bob Giraldi, features a character who sculpts a clay head of Richie.

charlie rich|behind closed doors.fact: Behind Closed Doors, written by Kenny O'Dell and produced by Billy Sherrill, was released in 1973 and spent 20 weeks at No. 1 on the country chart. It won Grammys for Best Country Song and Best Country Vocal Performance, Male, plus Song of the Year and Single of the Year from both the CMA and the ACM.

drifters|this magic moment.fact: This Magic Moment was written by Doc Pomus and Mort Shuman and recorded by The Drifters in December 1959, with Ben E. King on lead vocals. It was released in January 1960 and reached No. 16 on the Hot 100. Jay and the Americans' 1968 cover went higher, reaching No. 6.

cheap trick|i want you to want me.fact: Cheap Trick first recorded I Want You to Want Me for their 1977 album In Color, but it did not chart in the US. A faster live version from their April 1978 Budokan concerts was released in 1979, reaching No. 7 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 1 in Japan, and it became their signature song.

gerry & the pacemakers|you'll never walk.fact: You'll Never Walk Alone was written for the 1945 Rodgers and Hammerstein musical Carousel. Gerry & The Pacemakers recorded it in July 1963 with producer George Martin, and it spent four weeks at No. 1 in the UK. Liverpool fans then began singing it at Anfield, and it became the club's anthem.

spoon|lines in the suit.fact: Lines in the Suit is a track from Spoon's 2001 album Girls Can Tell. For the album's 20th anniversary, the band shared a 1999 home demo called Lines in the Suit - 30 Minutes Old, which Britt Daniel recorded when the song was only half an hour old.

bill callahan|riding for the feeling.fact: Riding for the Feeling is the fifth track on Bill Callahan's 2011 album Apocalypse, released on Drag City. Its Wurlitzer and electric piano parts were played by Jonathan Meiburg, and its music video is an animation of a ski jumper hovering over a looping mountain range.

janet jackson|together again.fact: Together Again, from Janet Jackson's 1997 album The Velvet Rope, was written and produced by Jackson with Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis. It hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in January 1998 and became her best-selling single in the UK. Jackson donated part of its worldwide sales to the American Foundation for AIDS Research.

christopher cross|sailing.fact: Sailing, from Christopher Cross's 1979 self-titled debut album, reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in August 1980. It won Record of the Year, Song of the Year, and Arrangement of the Year at the Grammys, and Cross also took Best New Artist. Cross has said it wasn't originally meant to be a single.

dave clark five|over and over.fact: The Dave Clark Five's Over and Over, released in October 1965, reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 that December. It was the band's only American No. 1. The song was written by Robert James Byrd, who recorded it as Bobby Day in 1958.

b.j. thomas|hooked on a feeling.fact: Hooked on a Feeling was written by Mark James, and B.J. Thomas released the first recording in 1968, with Reggie Young playing electric sitar. It reached No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100. Swedish group Blue Swede later took a 1973 cover to No. 1 in 1974.

dionne warwick|i'll never fall in love a.fact: I'll Never Fall in Love Again was written by Burt Bacharach and Hal David for the 1968 Broadway musical Promises, Promises. Dionne Warwick's version, released in late 1969, reached No. 6 on the Billboard Hot 100 in early 1970. It also topped the Easy Listening chart.

sheryl crow|if it makes you happy.fact: If It Makes You Happy was the lead single from Sheryl Crow's 1996 self-titled album. It reached No. 10 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 9 in the UK. Crow co-wrote it with Jeff Trott and produced it, and it won the 1997 Grammy for Best Female Rock Vocal Performance.

platters|(you've got) the magic touch.fact: The Platters released (You've Got) The Magic Touch in 1956, and it reached No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100.

jackie wilson|(your love keeps lifting m.fact: Jackie Wilson's Higher & Higher was recorded in Chicago in July 1967 and produced by Carl Davis. Wilson first sang it like a ballad until Davis told him to jump on the percussion. It hit No. 1 on the R&B chart and No. 6 on the Hot 100, and was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame in 1999.

arcade fire|sprawl ii (mountians beyond.fact: Sprawl II (Mountains Beyond Mountains), from Arcade Fire's 2010 album The Suburbs, is sung by Régine Chassagne. Its title comes from Tracy Kidder's 2003 book Mountains Beyond Mountains. It was released as the album's sixth single in 2012, and Pitchfork named it Best New Track.

mariah carey|all i want for christmas is.fact: All I Want for Christmas Is You, from Mariah Carey's 1994 album Merry Christmas, was co-written and co-produced with Walter Afanasieff and recorded at The Hit Factory in New York. It first hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in December 2019, 25 years after release, a record gap. It is certified Diamond by the RIAA.

whitney houston|how will i know.fact: How Will I Know, from Whitney Houston's 1985 debut album, was written by George Merrill and Shannon Rubicam and produced by Narada Michael Walden. The demo was first written with Janet Jackson in mind, but her management passed on it. Houston's version hit No. 1 on the Hot 100 in February 1986.

dire straits|sultans of swing.fact: Sultans of Swing was inspired by a Dixieland jazz band playing to a nearly empty pub in south London. Mark Knopfler said the song came alive when he bought his first Fender Stratocaster in 1977. After BBC Radio London DJ Charlie Gillett played the demo, it reached No. 4 in the US from the 1978 debut album Dire Straits.

chantay's|pipeline.fact: The Chantays' Pipeline was released in late 1962 and reached No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100. The tune was first titled Liberty's Whip, after the film The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance. The band renamed it after seeing a surfing movie showing the Banzai Pipeline in Hawaii.

donna fargo|you can't be a beacon if you.fact: You Can't Be a Beacon (If Your Light Don't Shine) was released by Donna Fargo in 1974 as the lead single from her album Miss Donna Fargo. It went to No. 1 on the Billboard country chart, her fifth country chart-topper. It was written by Marty Cooper rather than Fargo herself.

the guess who|these eyes.fact: These Eyes, written by Randy Bachman and Burton Cummings, was released by The Guess Who in Canada in December 1968. It appeared on the 1969 album Wheatfield Soul and reached No. 6 on the Billboard Pop chart, the group's first US top-ten hit. It was later certified gold.

drake|hotline bling.fact: Hotline Bling was released in 2015 and later included on Drake's album Views as a bonus track. Its instrumental samples Timmy Thomas's 1972 song Why Can't We Live Together. It peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 and won two Grammys in 2017, including Best Rap Song.

ride|leave them all behind.fact: Leave Them All Behind, the opening track on Ride's 1992 album Going Blank Again, runs 8:17, yet Creation Records founder Alan McGee insisted on releasing it as a single. Produced by Alan Moulder, it entered the UK chart at No. 9, the first Creation single to reach the UK top ten.

peabo bryson|if ever you're in my arms a.fact: If Ever You're in My Arms Again, from Peabo Bryson's album Straight from the Heart, was released in 1984. It was written by Cynthia Weil, Michael Masser, and Tom Snow, with Masser producing. It reached No. 10 on the Hot 100, his first top ten there, and spent four weeks at No. 1 on the Adult Contemporary chart.

haim|gasoline.fact: Gasoline is from Haim's 2020 album Women in Music Pt. III, written by the three Haim sisters and Rostam Batmanglij. It was produced by Ariel Rechtshaid, Danielle Haim, and Rostam. A remix featuring Taylor Swift came out as a single in February 2021, and Swift has called it her favorite song on the album.

earth, wind & fire|boogie wonderland fea.fact: Boogie Wonderland, released in 1979 as the lead single from Earth, Wind & Fire's album I Am, features vocal group The Emotions. Written by Allee Willis and Jon Lind and produced by Maurice White and Al McKay, it reached No. 6 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 4 in the UK. It won the Grammy for Best R&B Instrumental Performance.

talib kweli|get by.fact: Get By, from Talib Kweli's 2002 album Quality, was produced by Kanye West and built on a sample of Nina Simone's version of Sinnerman. Released as the album's third single in 2003, it peaked at No. 77 on the Billboard Hot 100 and is considered Kweli's most successful solo hit.

diana ross & the supremes|stop! in the n.fact: Stop! In the Name of Love was written and produced by the Motown team of Holland-Dozier-Holland and recorded in January 1965 at Hitsville U.S.A. with the Funk Brothers on instruments. It reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and appeared on the album More Hits by The Supremes. The group's hand-gesture choreography for the song debuted on the TV show Shindig!

gerry rafferty|baker street.fact: Baker Street, from Gerry Rafferty's 1978 album City to City, is known for its saxophone riff played by session musician Raphael Ravenscroft, who was reportedly paid about 27 pounds. The single reached No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100, held out of the top spot by Andy Gibb's Shadow Dancing, and No. 3 in the UK.

gene chandler|duke of earl.fact: Duke of Earl grew out of vocal warm-up exercises by the Dukays, the group Gene Chandler belonged to. Released on Vee-Jay Records in late 1961, it hit No. 1 on the Billboard pop and R&B charts in 1962. Chandler took his stage name from the actor Jeff Chandler.

air|la femme d'argent.fact: La Femme d'argent opens Air's 1998 debut album Moon Safari, running just over seven minutes. The French duo of Nicolas Godin and Jean-Benoit Dunckel recorded the album in 1997 in Paris and produced it themselves, using vintage keyboards like the Rhodes, Moog and Korg MS-20.

waylon jennings, willie nelson, johnny c.fact: Highwayman was written by Jimmy Webb, who recorded it first in 1977; Glen Campbell cut it next. The 1985 version by The Highwaymen (Waylon Jennings, Willie Nelson, Johnny Cash and Kris Kristofferson) has each of the four verses sung by a different member. It hit No. 1 on the Billboard country chart, and Webb won the Grammy for Best Country Song.

glen campbell|southern nights.fact: Southern Nights was written and first recorded by Allen Toussaint in 1975. Glen Campbell's 1977 version reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and the country and adult contemporary charts. Its distinctive guitar lick came from his friend Jerry Reed.

gordon lightfoot|rainy day people.fact: Rainy Day People, from Gordon Lightfoot's 1975 album Cold on the Shoulder, was produced by Lenny Waronker. It spent a week at No. 1 on the Billboard Easy Listening chart in May 1975 and peaked at No. 26 on the Hot 100. Jim Gordon played drums and Nick DeCaro arranged the strings.

the shins|fighting in a sack.fact: Fighting in a Sack is track 6 on The Shins' 2003 album Chutes Too Narrow, released on Sub Pop and issued as a single in 2004. The album was recorded in James Mercer's basement in Portland, Oregon.

harold melvin & the blue notes|if you do.fact: If You Don't Know Me by Now was written by Kenny Gamble and Leon Huff and released in 1972, with Teddy Pendergrass singing lead. It reached No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100. Simply Red's 1989 cover went to No. 1 in the US and won a Grammy for Best R&B Song.

hall & oates|she's gone.fact: She's Gone first appeared on Hall & Oates' 1973 album Abandoned Luncheonette and peaked at only No. 60. After the duo moved to RCA, Atlantic reissued it in 1976 and it climbed to No. 7. Tavares' cover became their first R&B No. 1 in 1974.

all-4-one|i swear.fact: I Swear was first recorded by John Michael Montgomery in 1993 and written by Gary Baker and Frank J. Myers. All-4-One's 1994 cover spent 11 consecutive weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and won a Grammy. It was the No. 2 song of 1994 on the Billboard year-end chart.

the roots|the seed (2.0).fact: The Seed (2.0), from The Roots' 2002 album Phrenology, features Cody ChesnuTT on guitar and vocals. It is an uptempo retooling of his own song The Seed from his album The Headphone Masterpiece. Released as a single in 2003, it reached No. 33 on the UK chart.

alvvays|in undertow.fact: In Undertow, released in June 2017, is the lead single and opening track of Alvvays' second album Antisocialites. Norman Blake of Teenage Fanclub sang backing vocals and played additional guitar, and John Congleton co-produced. The video shows singer Molly Rankin in an astronaut helmet.

kenny rogers & dolly parton|islands in t.fact: Islands in the Stream was written by the Bee Gees' Barry, Robin and Maurice Gibb, and was originally meant for Diana Ross. Reworked as a duet for Kenny Rogers and Dolly Parton, it was released in 1983 on Eyes That See in the Dark. It knocked Total Eclipse of the Heart from No. 1 on the Hot 100.

men without hats|the safety dance.fact: The Safety Dance, written by singer Ivan Doroschuk, came out in Canada in 1982 from the album Rhythm of Youth. It peaked at No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1983. Its video, filmed in an English village with Morris dancers and a maypole, was directed by Tim Pope.

harry chapin|cat's in the cradle.fact: Cat's in the Cradle, from Harry Chapin's 1974 album Verities & Balderdash, began as a poem by his wife Sandra. It became Chapin's only No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and entered the Grammy Hall of Fame in 2011. It is often wrongly credited to Cat Stevens.

simon & garfunkel|america.fact: America was recorded in February 1968 at Columbia Studio A in New York and appeared on Simon & Garfunkel's album Bookends. Paul Simon based it on a 1964 road trip. Yes recorded a prog rock version that reached No. 46 on the US Hot 100 in 1972.

glen campbell|wichita lineman.fact: Wichita Lineman was written by Jimmy Webb and released by Glen Campbell in late 1968, produced by Al De Lory. Session bassist Carol Kaye of the Wrecking Crew played its descending intro, and the single reached #3 on the US pop chart and #1 on the country chart. The recording was later added to the Library of Congress's National Recording Registry.

backstreet boys|everybody (backstreet's.fact: Everybody (Backstreet's Back) was written and produced by Swedish hitmakers Denniz Pop and Max Martin and was the lead single from the Backstreet Boys' international album Backstreet's Back in 1997. It reached #4 on the US Billboard Hot 100 and #3 in the UK. Although it was released in the summer, its spooky video made it a Halloween favorite.

ray charles|lonely avenue.fact: Lonely Avenue was written by Doc Pomus and recorded by Ray Charles for Atlantic Records in 1956. It reached #6 on the R&B chart and is considered Pomus's first major hit as a songwriter. Charles later included it on his 1958 album Yes Indeed!

creedence clearwater revival|bad moon ri.fact: Bad Moon Rising was the lead single from Creedence Clearwater Revival's 1969 album Green River. It reached #2 on the US Hot 100 and became the band's only #1 in the UK, spending three weeks on top in September 1969.

modern english|i melt with you.fact: I Melt With You was the second single from Modern English's 1982 album After the Snow and reached #78 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1983. The band re-recorded it for their 1990 album Pillow Lips, and that version climbed to #76 on the Hot 100.

lisa lisa & the cult jam|head to toe.fact: Head to Toe, from Lisa Lisa & Cult Jam's 1987 debut album Spanish Fly, was produced by the group Full Force. It hit #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in June 1987, and the album's follow-up single Lost in Emotion also reached #1 that year.

magdalena bay|image.fact: Image is a 2024 single from Magdalena Bay's second album, Imaginal Disk, released on Mom + Pop Music. It was written and produced by the duo, Matthew Lewin and Mica Tenenbaum. Its music video, directed by Amanda Kramer, shows Tenenbaum getting an 'imaginal disk' upgrade in a waiting room, and a remix called Image (Grimes Special) followed.

jackson browne|running on empty.fact: Jackson Browne's 1977 album Running on Empty was recorded almost entirely while he was on tour, with tracks captured on stage, backstage, in hotel rooms, and on the tour bus. The album peaked at #3 on the Billboard 200, and the title track reached #11 on the Hot 100.

beyonce|countdown.fact: Countdown, from Beyonce's 2011 album 4, samples the spoken countdown from Boyz II Men's 1991 song Uhh Ahh. Boyz II Men members Michael Bivins, Nathan Morris and Wanya Morris are credited as writers because of it. Wanya Morris noted that Destiny's Child had opened for the group on an early tour.

james taylor|shower the people.fact: Shower the People is from James Taylor's 1976 album In the Pocket. It reached #22 on the Billboard Hot 100 and topped the Easy Listening chart, giving Taylor his third song to do so.

vampire weekend|a-punk.fact: A-Punk was released in February 2008 as the second single from Vampire Weekend's self-titled debut album, produced by bandmate Rostam Batmanglij. It reached #25 on Billboard's Modern Rock chart and was certified Gold by the RIAA in 2013, the band's first gold single. The song opens the 2008 film Step Brothers.

adele|rumour has it.fact: Rumour Has It, from Adele's 2011 album 21, was written by Adele with Ryan Tedder, who also produced it, even though Rick Rubin had been set to produce the whole album. Tedder said they wrote it on the first day and Adele sang it in one pass on the second.

bruce springsteen|human touch.fact: Human Touch is the title track of Bruce Springsteen's 1992 album, which debuted at #2 on the Billboard 200. Released as a double A-side single with Better Days, it reached #16 on the Hot 100 and #1 on the Mainstream Rock chart.

celine dion|if you asked me to.fact: If You Asked Me To was written by Diane Warren and first recorded by Patti LaBelle in 1989 for the James Bond film Licence to Kill, reaching #79 on the Hot 100. Celine Dion covered it in 1992 for her self-titled English-language album, and her version hit #4 on the Hot 100 and #1 in Canada.

creedence clearwater revival|born on the.fact: Born on the Bayou opens Creedence Clearwater Revival's 1969 album Bayou Country. John Fogerty, from California, wrote it about an imagined Louisiana childhood and said he had never lived in the swamp setting he described.

joe cocker|you are so beautiful.fact: You Are So Beautiful was written by Billy Preston and Bruce Fisher, and Preston first released it in 1974 on his album The Kids & Me. Joe Cocker's slower version, on his 1974 album I Can Stand a Little Rain, was produced by Jim Price and peaked at #5 on the Billboard Hot 100.

joe jackson|is she really going out with.fact: Is She Really Going Out with Him? was Joe Jackson's first US chart hit, from his 1979 debut album Look Sharp! Released on A&M, it initially failed to chart when issued in late 1978, but it later reached #21 on the Billboard Hot 100 in August 1979 and spent 15 weeks on the chart.

wild pink|ilysm.fact: "ILYSM" is the title track of Wild Pink's fourth album, released October 14, 2022, on Royal Mountain Records. It was shared as a single on July 27, 2022, with a visualizer made using the Dall-E 2 AI system. John Ross co-produced the album with Peter Silberman of The Antlers and Justin Pizzoferrato, and guests include J Mascis of Dinosaur Jr. and Julien Baker.

dr. dog|the breeze.fact: "The Breeze" opens Dr. Dog's fifth album, Fate, which came out July 22, 2008, on the band's Park the Van label. The album was mixed by Bill Moriarty and mastered by Greg Calbi. Brendan Cooney wrote the string and horn arrangements.

man man|mister jung stuffed.fact: "Mister Jung Stuffed" opens Man Man's third album, Rabbit Habits, released April 8, 2008, on Anti- Records. At just 2:28, it charges out of the gate with schoolyard-style chants and a fast, clap-filled rhythm, according to Exclaim's review.

junip|line of fire.fact: "Line of Fire" is the 5:39 opening track on Junip's second album, Junip, released in April 2013 on City Slang in Europe and Mute in North America. The Swedish trio of Jose Gonzalez, Tobias Winterkorn and Elias Araya recorded the album in 2011-2012. The song was used in commercials for the Breaking Bad series finale and has been featured on The Blacklist, The Originals and Elementary.

cocteau twins|fifty-fifty clown.fact: "Fifty-Fifty Clown" is track 4 on Cocteau Twins' sixth album, Heaven or Las Vegas, released September 17, 1990, on 4AD in the UK and Capitol in the US. The band produced the album themselves at September Sound in Twickenham, London. It reached No. 7 on the UK Albums Chart.

clap your hands say yeah|in this home on.fact: "In This Home on Ice" is the ninth track on Clap Your Hands Say Yeah's 2005 self-titled debut. The band self-produced, self-released and self-distributed the album, and online music blogs helped it spread. The first CD run was too small to meet demand, so they had to press more. The band later signed with the UK label Wichita Recordings, which issued the album overseas in January 2006.

dinosaur jr.|sludgefeast.fact: "Sludgefeast" is the third track on Dinosaur Jr.'s second album, You're Living All Over Me, released December 14, 1987, on SST Records. The label was founded by Black Flag's Greg Ginn. The album was recorded in New York with engineer Wharton Tiers, who also worked with Sonic Youth. It is now widely regarded as one of the most influential alternative rock albums.

dinosaur jr.|tiny.fact: "Tiny" is track 2 on Dinosaur Jr.'s 2016 album Give a Glimpse of What Yer Not, and was one of its two singles, along with "Goin Down." Its music video came out June 20, 2016, and the album followed on August 5, 2016. J Mascis produced the album at his Bisquiteen Studio in Amherst, Massachusetts. The cover art is by German painter Daniel Richter, a fan of the band.

beach house|woo.fact: "Woo" is track 9 on Beach House's 2018 album 7, released May 11, 2018, on Sub Pop. It was recorded at Palmetto Studio in Los Angeles. The album was co-produced by Peter Kember (Sonic Boom) after the duo parted ways with longtime producer Chris Coady, and mixed by Alan Moulder.

runnner|get real sleep.fact: "Get Real Sleep" is a single from A Welcome Kind of Weakness, the second full-length album from Runnner, the Los Angeles project of songwriter and producer Noah Weinman. The album was released on Run For Cover Records and Civilians. It was his first studio-recorded album and moved away from his earlier home-recorded lo-fi sound toward a bigger sound recalling the early-2000s indie rock boom.

durand jones & the indications|really wa.fact: "Really Wanna Be With You" is track 6 on Flowers, the fourth album by Durand Jones & The Indications, released June 27, 2025, on Dead Oceans. The band self-produced it, with Aaron Frazer, Durand Jones, Steve Okonski and Blake Rhein credited as producers. They wrote most of the album together at Rhein's Chicago home studio, building many tracks from one-take demos.

beck|loser.fact: "Loser" was written and recorded at Carl Stephenson's home, where he looped a guitar part on an 8-track and layered in sitar and samples before Beck added improvised vocals. Producer Tom Rothrock said the song was largely finished in about six and a half hours. Bong Load first pressed just 500 copies of the 12-inch single in March 1993. After Beck signed with DGC, the song peaked at No. 10 on the Billboard Hot 100 in April 1994 and hit No. 1 in Norway.

the white stripes|we're going to be frie.fact: "We're Going to Be Friends" was recorded in February 2001 at Easley-McCain Recording in Memphis for the album White Blood Cells, and released as a single in 2002. It was the first White Stripes song used in a film, playing over the opening credits of Napoleon Dynamite in 2004. It has been covered by Jack Johnson for the Curious George soundtrack and by Bright Eyes with First Aid Kit.

duster|me and the birds.fact: "Me and the Birds" comes from Contemporary Movement, the second album by the San Jose, California band Duster. It was released on Up Records in August 2000, two years after the band's 1998 debut Stratosphere.

unknown mortal orchestra|meshuggah.fact: "Meshuggah" is the third track on V, the double album Unknown Mortal Orchestra released on Jagjaguwar on March 17, 2023. The band shared it as the last single before the album came out. The band is led by New Zealand-born songwriter Ruban Nielson.

galaxie 500|tugboat.fact: Galaxie 500 recorded "Tugboat" in February 1988 with producer Mark Kramer at his Noise New York studio. In a single eight-hour session the trio recorded seven songs, including "Tugboat" and "Oblivious". "Tugboat" became the lead single from their debut album Today, released in 1988.

siouxsie and the banshees|slowdive.fact: "Slowdive" was released in 1982 as the first single from Siouxsie and the Banshees' fifth studio album, A Kiss in the Dreamhouse. The shoegaze band Slowdive later took their name from the song. Singer Rachel Goswell, a big Siouxsie fan, suggested it after another member proposed "Slowburn".

neko case|this tornado loves you.fact: "This Tornado Loves You" is the opening track of Neko Case's 2009 album Middle Cyclone. Case co-produced the album with Darryl Neudorf, and it was recorded in several places including Tucson, Toronto and Vermont. It debuted at number three on the Billboard 200, the highest debut by an independent release that year.

joy division|isolation.fact: "Isolation" is on Joy Division's album Closer, which was recorded in March 1980 at Britannia Row Studios in London with producer Martin Hannett. The song is built on an electronic drum pattern played by Stephen Morris and a synthesizer part from Bernard Sumner. According to Peter Hook, Hannett also worked to save the song's ending after a tape-editing mishap.

fugazi|i'm so tired.fact: "I'm So Tired" is on Instrument Soundtrack, a 1999 Dischord Records release that scored Jem Cohen's documentary film about Fugazi. Unlike most of the band's loud, driving music, it is a short piano ballad of about two minutes, played and sung by Ian MacKaye. Pitchfork's review singled it out as a surprising and beautiful moment on the album.

the clash|spanish bombs.fact: "Spanish Bombs" was recorded in 1979 at Wessex Studios in London for The Clash's double album London Calling. The album was produced by Guy Stevens, who was known for unconventional studio methods, and was released in the UK on December 14, 1979.

ugly casanova|so long to the holidays.fact: "So Long to the Holidays" closes Sharpen Your Teeth, the only album by Ugly Casanova. The album was released on Sub Pop on May 21, 2002, and was produced by Brian Deck. Ugly Casanova was a side project of Modest Mouse singer Isaac Brock, who wanted to try new methods and genres outside his main band.

cake|i will survive.fact: Cake's version of "I Will Survive" is a cover of the 1978 Gloria Gaynor disco hit, and it appeared on their 1996 album Fashion Nugget. Cake slowed the song down and gave it a drier, rock arrangement. It became one of the album's most successful singles, along with "The Distance".

my bloody valentine|soon.fact: "Soon" was the lead track of My Bloody Valentine's 1990 Glider EP, which reached number 2 on the UK Indie Chart. A separate 12-inch single of "Soon" featured a remix by Andrew Weatherall that did not appear on any other MBV release. A different mix of the song was later included on the 1991 album Loveless.

billy bragg|a new england.fact: Billy Bragg's "A New England" first appeared on his 1983 debut Life's a Riot with Spy vs Spy. Kirsty MacColl recorded a cover in 1985 that reached number 7 on the UK Singles Chart and became her best-selling song. Her version was produced by Steve Lillywhite, and Bragg wrote an extra verse for it that he sometimes still sings in concert.

vampire weekend|white sky.fact: "White Sky" is on Vampire Weekend's second album, Contra, released in January 2010 and produced by bandmate Rostam Batmanglij. Ezra Koenig has said the song began as a roughly 30-second loop Batmanglij made on his computer, and Koenig then built a melody around it. The band first played it live in January 2008, and it was released as a single in August 2010.

belle and sebastian|seeing other people.fact: "Seeing Other People" is the second track on Belle and Sebastian's 1996 album If You're Feeling Sinister. The album was recorded in only five days and mixed in three, in the same Glasgow studio used for their debut Tigermilk. Engineer Tony Doogan worked to keep the recording style similar to the first record.

lucy dacus|night shift.fact: "Night Shift" opens Lucy Dacus's second album, Historian, and was its lead single. The album was recorded in Nashville in March 2017 and produced by Collin Pastore, who also produced her debut No Burden. John Congleton mixed it, and Matador Records released it on March 2, 2018.

lorde|royals.fact: Lorde struggled to find a title for her breakout hit until she saw a photo of baseball star George Brett signing baseballs, wearing a jersey that said "Royals." The word on the shirt gave the song its name, even though the song has nothing to do with baseball. It appears on her 2013 debut album Pure Heroine.

rolling stones|love is strong.fact: The video for this 1994 Voodoo Lounge single was directed by David Fincher and showed the Rolling Stones as giants towering over Manhattan. Shot in black and white with effects by Digital Domain, it won the Grammy for Best Short Form Music Video. The song was co-produced by Don Was.

kazumi totaka|kaeru no tame ni kane wa n.fact: Kazumi Totaka composed the music for the Game Boy adventure Kaeru no Tame ni Kane wa Naru (For the Frog the Bell Tolls). He is also famous for "Totaka's Song," a tiny 19-note melody he hides as an Easter egg in almost every game he scores, first discovered on the Mario Paint title screen.

isaac hayes|walk on by (single edit).fact: Isaac Hayes stretched Burt Bacharach's "Walk On By" to about 12 minutes on his 1969 album Hot Buttered Soul. The album hit number 1 on the R&B chart and number 8 on the Billboard 200. The 4:34 single edit reached number 30 on the Billboard Hot 100.

king harvest|dancing in the moonlight.fact: King Harvest's version of "Dancing in the Moonlight" reached number 13 on the US Billboard Hot 100 in 1972. English band Toploader covered it in 2000 and scored a UK hit, helped by its use in a supermarket TV ad. The song was written by Sherman Kelly, and was first recorded by his band Boffalongo.

chordettes|lollipop.fact: The Chordettes' 1958 "Lollipop" is famous for its "pop" sound, made by one singer putting a finger in her mouth and flicking it out. The song peaked at number 2 on the Billboard pop chart. The Chordettes' version came out after an earlier recording by Ronald & Ruby, which reached number 20 on the Hot 100.

basement jaxx|where's your head at.fact: This 2001 single from Basement Jaxx's album Rooty is built on samples from two Gary Numan songs, "M.E." and "This Wreckage." The album was named after the duo's own club night, Rooty, held at a small bar in Brixton, London.

asuka hayazaki, atsuko asahi, hajime wak.fact: The music for Pikmin 3 was written by Nintendo composers Asuka Hayazaki, Atsuko Asahi, and Hajime Wakai. There was no official soundtrack album with track-by-track credits, so fans worked out who wrote which song from initials in the internal audio file names.

coldplay|viva la vida.fact: "Viva la Vida" was Coldplay's first UK number one, and it was the first UK number one based solely on download sales. It also became their first number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in June 2008, making them the first British group to top that chart since the Spice Girls' "Wannabe" in 1997.

norman greenbaum|spirit in the sky.fact: The crunchy fuzz guitar sound on "Spirit in the Sky" came from a fuzz circuit built into the body of Norman Greenbaum's Fender Telecaster. Released in December 1969, the single went gold in the US with about two million copies sold, and peaked at number 3 in April 1970.

j cole|work out.fact: J. Cole produced "Work Out" himself as the first single from his debut album Cole World: The Sideline Story. It uses the ending production of Kanye West's "The New Workout Plan" and interpolates the chorus of Paula Abdul's "Straight Up," and clearing the sample reportedly delayed its release.

david byrne & brian eno|strange overtone.fact: "Strange Overtones" was released as a free download on August 4, 2008, as the lead single from David Byrne and Brian Eno's album Everything That Happens Will Happen Today. It was first demoed in Eno's London home studio and finished in New York by Byrne and Leo Abrahams. The album was the duo's first joint work since 1981's My Life in the Bush of Ghosts.

one direction|little things.fact: "Little Things" was co-written by Ed Sheeran and Fiona Bevan, and Sheeran has said they first wrote it when he was 17. It was released as the second single from One Direction's 2012 album Take Me Home and became the group's second UK number one.

sinead o'connor|nothing compares 2 u.fact: Prince wrote "Nothing Compares 2 U" for his side project The Family, who released it on their 1985 debut album. Sinead O'Connor's 1990 version, from I Do Not Want What I Haven't Got, spent four weeks at number 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and topped the UK chart for a month.

spice girls|wannabe.fact: Wannabe was the Spice Girls' debut single and reached No. 1 in the UK in July 1996, staying there for seven weeks. It went on to top the charts in dozens of countries, including the US in early 1997, and won British Single of the Year at the 1997 BRIT Awards. It remains the best-selling single by a female group in UK history.

spin doctors|two princes.fact: Two Princes was a track from the Spin Doctors' 1991 album Pocket Full of Kryptonite, which became a smash in 1993 and peaked at No. 7 on the Billboard Hot 100. It topped the charts in Iceland and Sweden, and the album reached No. 3 on the Billboard 200 and sold over five million copies in the US.

rod stewart|you're in my heart (the fina.fact: From Rod Stewart's 1977 album Foot Loose & Fancy Free (produced by Tom Dowd), this song name-checks two of his favorite football clubs, Glasgow Celtic and Manchester United. The album's inner sleeve even shows the team names drifting out of a car stereo. It reached No. 4 in the US and No. 3 in the UK.

the flirtations|nothing but a heartache.fact: The Flirtations formed in New York in 1962 and moved to England for a fresh start, where this song was written and produced by Wayne Bickerton and Tony Waddington for Deram Records in 1968. It flopped in the US at first, but a 1969 reissue climbed to No. 34 on the Billboard Hot 100. It is now a Northern Soul favorite.

the sonics|have love will travel.fact: Richard Berry wrote this song in 1959, and its title was inspired by the TV western Have Gun, Will Travel. The Sonics' raw 1965 version on Here Are the Sonics changed the key from G to C and tweaked the riff. Many assume a fuzz guitar, but the buzzing sound comes largely from the saxophone. The Black Keys later covered it.

stereolab|miss modular.fact: Miss Modular was the lead single from Stereolab's 1997 album Dots and Loops, released on 1 September 1997 on the band's Duophonic label. It was made in collaboration with the German duo Mouse on Mars, and Dan the Automator remixed the title track. It peaked at No. 60 on the UK Singles Chart.

suede|trash.fact: Trash was released on 29 July 1996 as the first single from Suede's album Coming Up, produced by Ed Buller. It peaked at No. 3 in the UK, tying the band's highest placing, and sold more than Stay Together to become their biggest seller. It also topped the Finnish chart.

janet jackson|what have you done for me.fact: Released in January 1986, this was the lead single from Janet Jackson's breakthrough album Control, produced by Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis. It peaked at No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100 and is widely credited with replacing her earlier pop-ingenue image with a bold, independent sound.

*nsync|better place.fact: Better Place, released in September 2023 for the Trolls Band Together soundtrack, was the first new *NSYNC single in about two decades. Justin Timberlake co-wrote and co-produced it. It debuted at No. 25 on the Billboard Hot 100, matching the group's earlier debut spot for I Want You Back in 1998.

stevie wonder|isn't she lovely.fact: Isn't She Lovely, from the 1976 album Songs in the Key of Life, was never released as a commercial single because Stevie Wonder refused to cut its six-plus minutes to fit a 45 rpm record. Wonder played nearly every instrument himself, including the harmonica solo, and a shorter promo edit still got heavy radio play.

elton john|philadelphia freedom.fact: Elton John and Bernie Taupin wrote Philadelphia Freedom as a tribute to his friend, tennis star Billie Jean King, and the World TeamTennis Philadelphia Freedoms team. Released in early 1975, it hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 on April 12, 1975, and was John's fourth US chart-topper.

little richard and his band|ready teddy.fact: Ready Teddy was written by John Marascalco and Robert 'Bumps' Blackwell, recorded by Little Richard on May 9, 1956 at J&M Studio in New Orleans, and released on Specialty that June as the B-side of Rip It Up. Elvis Presley, Buddy Holly and others went on to cover it.

kelly clarkson|stronger (what doesn't ki.fact: Stronger (What Doesn't Kill You) was written by Kelly Clarkson, Jorgen Elofsson, Ali Tamposi and David Gamson, with Greg Kurstin producing. It hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in February 2012, Clarkson's third chart-topper after A Moment Like This and My Life Would Suck Without You, and also reached No. 1 on 11 different Billboard charts.

phil collins|i wish it would rain down.fact: Eric Clapton plays lead guitar on this single from Phil Collins' 1989 album ...But Seriously, backed by a large gospel choir. Collins said it was as close as he gets to writing a blues song and felt it was an 'Eric song.' It reached No. 3 on the US Hot 100 and was the top song of 1990 in Canada.

run-d.m.c.|sucker m.c.'s (krush-groove 1.fact: Sucker M.C.'s, also called Krush-Groove 1, debuted in 1983 as the B-side of Run-D.M.C.'s It's Like That. It was built on a stripped-down Oberheim DMX drum machine beat with no melody, which helped define the sparse sound of 1980s hip hop. The 'Krush' in the title nods to Orange Krush, the backing band Russell Simmons wanted named in the lyrics.

johnny nash|i can see clearly now.fact: Johnny Nash wrote "I Can See Clearly Now" himself and recorded it in 1972 as the title track of his album. It reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in November 1972, and Nash was among the first non-Jamaican artists to record reggae-flavored pop in Jamaica.

britney spears|oops....i did it again.fact: The title track of Britney Spears's second album, released in 2000, was written and produced by the Swedish team of Max Martin and Rami Yacoub. They recorded much of Britney's early work at Cheiron Studios in Stockholm.

gladys knight & the pips|every beat of m.fact: Johnny Otis wrote "Every Beat of My Heart," and his group the Royals first recorded it in 1952. In 1961 Gladys Knight & the Pips released it as their debut single on Vee-Jay, and it became their first top-ten Billboard Hot 100 hit.

doobie brothers|takin' it to the streets.fact: "Takin' It to the Streets" was the title track of the Doobie Brothers' 1976 album and the first single to feature Michael McDonald's songwriting and lead vocal. McDonald had joined the band the year before.

mcguire sisters|sincerely.fact: "Sincerely" was first recorded in 1954 by the Moonglows, written by group leader Harvey Fuqua. The McGuire Sisters' 1955 cover version went to number one on the Billboard charts.

billy joe royal|down in the boondocks.fact: Joe South wrote and produced "Down in the Boondocks," Billy Joe Royal's breakthrough 1965 hit. Royal and South were longtime friends, and the single reached number 9 on the Billboard Hot 100.

katy perry|last friday night (tgif).fact: Released in 2011, "Last Friday Night (T.G.I.F.)" was the fifth number-one single from Katy Perry's album Teenage Dream. That tied Michael Jackson's record for the most number ones from one album, set with Bad in 1987, and made her the first woman to do it.

vanessa williams|save the best for last.fact: "Save the Best for Last" was written by Wendy Waldman, Jon Lind and Phil Galdston and appears on Vanessa Williams's 1991 album The Comfort Zone. It topped the Billboard Hot 100 in 1992, becoming her biggest hit.

drifters|there goes my baby.fact: Recorded in 1959 with Ben E. King on lead vocal and produced by Leiber and Stoller, "There Goes My Baby" was an early R&B hit to use a string section. It reached number two on the Billboard Hot 100 and number one on the R&B chart.

deftones|passenger.fact: "Passenger" is on Deftones' 2000 album White Pony and features guest vocals by Maynard James Keenan of Tool. The song won a following among fans of both bands.

ella fitzgerald|after you've gone.fact: "After You've Gone" was written in 1918 by Turner Layton and Henry Creamer, and it became a jazz standard recorded by many artists. Ella Fitzgerald was one of the major vocalists to record it.

whitney houston|i have nothing.fact: "I Have Nothing" was written by David Foster and Linda Thompson for the 1992 film The Bodyguard. It earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song.

junior murvin|police & thieves.fact: Junior Murvin's 1976 single was produced by Lee "Scratch" Perry at his Black Ark studio in Kingston, and its high falsetto earned Murvin comparisons to Curtis Mayfield. The Clash covered it on their 1977 debut album, helping bring reggae to punk audiences.

england dan & john ford coley|i'd really.fact: Parker McGee wrote "I'd Really Love to See You Tonight," and England Dan & John Ford Coley recorded it in 1976. It reached number two on the Billboard Hot 100 and topped the Adult Contemporary chart.

arctic monkeys|mardy bum.fact: "Mardy" is Northern English slang for sulky or moody, and it was first recorded in print in Sheffield in the 1870s. Arctic Monkeys put the phrase on their 2006 debut album, Whatever People Say I Am, That's What I'm Not, and a University of Sheffield linguist credits the band with spreading the word nationwide.

elvis presley|can't help falling in love.fact: Elvis recorded this for the 1961 film Blue Hawaii. Its melody comes from "Plaisir d'amour,", a French song composed in 1784 by Jean-Paul-Egide Martini. Writers Hugo Peretti, Luigi Creatore and George David Weiss adapted it, and Elvis's version hit No. 1 in the UK in 1962.

fleetwood mac|monday morning.fact: Lindsey Buckingham wrote "Monday Morning" for a planned second Buckingham Nicks album. That album never happened after their label dropped the duo. It ended up opening Fleetwood Mac's 1975 self-titled album, along with other songs the pair brought to the band.

wilson phillips|release me.fact: "Release Me" was the second No. 1 single on the Billboard Hot 100 from Wilson Phillips' 1990 self-titled debut album. It followed their first chart-topper, "Hold On."

duane eddy|rebel-'rouser.fact: "Rebel-'Rouser" was written by Duane Eddy and producer Lee Hazlewood and released on Jamie Records in 1958. It started as the B-side of "Stalkin'." Hazlewood took Eddy's basic track to a Los Angeles studio to add a honking saxophone overdub, handclaps and shouts, and Dick Clark's plays on American Bandstand helped make it a national hit.

gary puckett & the union gap|this girl i.fact: "This Girl Is a Woman Now" was released in August 1969. It reached No. 9 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 2 on the easy listening chart. It was written by Victor Millrose and Alan Bernstein and produced by Dick Glasser.

macklemore|can't hold us ft. ray dalton.fact: "Can't Hold Us" reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in May 2013. That made Macklemore & Ryan Lewis the first duo to send their first two singles to No. 1, following "Thrift Shop." Singer Ray Dalton was a Seattle gospel and soul musician working as a tennis instructor when producer Ryan Lewis brought him in.

alice in chains|no excuses.fact: "No Excuses" is from the 1994 acoustic-leaning EP Jar of Flies. The EP debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, the first EP ever to do so, with first-week sales above 141,000.

joe cocker & jennifer warnes|up where we.fact: Jack Nitzsche, who scored An Officer and a Gentleman (1982), asked Buffy Sainte-Marie to help finish the song's melody, and Will Jennings wrote the lyrics. The song hit No. 1 on the Hot 100, and the writers won the Academy Award and Golden Globe for Best Original Song. Cocker and Warnes also won a Grammy for the duet.

luther vandross|here and now.fact: "Here and Now" won Luther Vandross his first Grammy, for Best Male R&B Vocal Performance. It was also his first single to reach the Billboard Hot 100 top ten, peaking at No. 6.

four tops|ain't no woman (like the one i.fact: This Four Tops hit was written by Dennis Lambert and Brian Potter and released in January 1973 on ABC/Dunhill from the album Keeper of the Castle. It was first recorded by Hamilton, Joe Frank & Reynolds. The Four Tops' version reached No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100 and went gold.

lana del rey|video games.fact: "Video Games" began as one of many video collages Lana Del Rey made and uploaded online, and she directed the video herself using clips that included webcam footage of her singing. It was re-released through Interscope on October 7, 2011, as the lead single from her album Born to Die.

blondie|(i'm always touched by your) pre.fact: This song was written by former Blondie bassist Gary Valentine, who had just left the band, and drummer Clem Burke persuaded the group to record it anyway. It appeared on the 1978 album Plastic Letters and reached No. 10 in the UK, though it was never a US single.

amy grant|baby, baby.fact: "Baby Baby" was co-written by Amy Grant and Keith Thomas, who also produced it. It topped the Billboard Hot 100 for two weeks in April 1991 and was the first hit from her album Heart in Motion, which sold 5 million copies.

moonglows|sincerely.fact: The Moonglows recorded "Sincerely" in October 1954 in Chicago for Chess Records, and it hit No. 1 on the Billboard R&B chart. The McGuire Sisters' cover became the best-selling version, topping the pop charts in early 1955.

hank ballard & the midnighters|finger po.fact: "Finger Poppin' Time" came out on King Records in April 1960 and reached No. 7 on the pop chart and No. 2 on the R&B chart. It sold over a million copies and earned a 1960 Grammy nomination for Best R&B Performance.

one direction|live while we're young.fact: "Live While We're Young" was released September 28, 2012, as the lead single from Take Me Home. It was written by Savan Kotecha, Rami Yacoub and Carl Falk, the same team behind "What Makes You Beautiful." It posted the highest one-week opening sales for a song by a non-US artist.

boards of canada|turquoise hexagon sun.fact: This track first appeared on the 1996 EP Hi Scores, Boards of Canada's first widely distributed release, on Skam Records. It was reused on their 1998 debut album, Music Has the Right to Children. The duo's Hexagon Sun name comes from the collective the brothers formed in the early 1990s.

bryan adams|(everything i do) i do it fo.fact: Bryan Adams co-wrote this with Michael Kamen and Robert John "Mutt" Lange for Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves (1991). It spent 16 straight weeks at No. 1 in the UK, the longest unbroken run in British chart history, and seven weeks at No. 1 in the US.

marshall crenshaw|someday, someway.fact: Marshall Crenshaw has said the song began as a take on Gene Vincent's "Lotta Lovin'." Robert Gordon covered it in 1981, and that version helped get Crenshaw's own recording noticed. Crenshaw's 1982 version reached No. 36 and was his only solo Top 40 hit.

beyonce|halo.fact: "Halo" was written by Ryan Tedder, Evan Bogart and Beyonce for her album I Am... Sasha Fierce. It was nominated for Record of the Year and won Best Female Pop Vocal Performance at the 52nd Grammy Awards.

the cars|just what i needed.fact: Ric Ocasek wrote "Just What I Needed," but he picked bassist Benjamin Orr to sing it. It was recorded in early 1978 at AIR Studios in London with producer Roy Thomas Baker, known for his work with Queen. It reached No. 27 on the Hot 100 from the band's self-titled debut.

death cab for cutie|title and registrati.fact: "Title and Registration" was the third single from Death Cab for Cutie's fourth studio album, Transatlanticism (2003). It was written by Ben Gibbard and Chris Walla, and its title refers to the papers kept in a car's glove compartment.

hot chelle rae|tonight tonight.fact: "Tonight Tonight" is Hot Chelle Rae's biggest hit, peaking at No. 7 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2011. The band formed in Nashville in 2005, and the song was the lead single from their second album, Whatever.

commodores|easy.fact: Lionel Richie wrote "Easy" for the Commodores in 1977. It hit No. 1 on the Soul Singles chart and No. 4 on the Hot 100. Faith No More's 1992 cover topped the charts in Australia and reached No. 3 in the UK.

m83|steve mcqueen.fact: "Steve McQueen" appears on M83's 2011 double album Hurry Up, We're Dreaming. The band released an official video for it about a year after the album came out, in late 2012.

night ranger|sister christian.fact: Drummer Kelly Keagy wrote "Sister Christian" about his younger sister, Christy, after noticing on a visit home to Oregon how fast she was growing up. The title was originally "Sister Christy" but the rest of the band thought he was singing "Christian." It reached No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100 from the album Midnight Madness.

new edition|candy girl.fact: "Candy Girl" was New Edition's debut single, released in July 1983 on Streetwise Records, when the group members were only about 14 to 15 years old. It launched the Boston group's career.

electric light orchestra|strange magic.fact: Jeff Lynne wrote and produced "Strange Magic" for ELO's 1975 album Face the Music, which reached No. 8 on the US album chart. It was released as a single in 1976 in two different edits, one for the US and one for the UK.

dionne warwick|walk on by.fact: Burt Bacharach and Hal David's "Walk On By" was recorded by Dionne Warwick at Bell Sound Studios in New York in late 1963 and reached No. 6 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1964. Her recording was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame in 1998, and Isaac Hayes later turned it into a 12-minute epic on Hot Buttered Soul.

george harrison|what is life.fact: George Harrison wrote "What Is Life" in 1969 with his friend Billy Preston in mind, but kept it for himself. It appeared on his 1970 triple album All Things Must Pass, with Preston playing keyboards, and was released as a US single in February 1971.

etta james|something's got a hold on me.fact: Etta James released "Something's Got a Hold on Me" in 1962 on Argo Records as the third single from her self-titled album. It showed off the gospel roots she had sung since childhood and reached No. 4 on the R&B chart.

chuck berry|memphis, tennessee.fact: Chuck Berry's 1959 "Memphis, Tennessee" was only the B-side of "Back in the U.S.A." and peaked at No. 87. Lonnie Mack's 1963 instrumental version hit No. 5, and Johnny Rivers took a live version to No. 2 in 1964. The song has been covered more than 200 times.

impressions|it's all right.fact: The Impressions' "It's All Right" (1963) reached No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 1 on the R&B chart. It was one of the group's biggest early hits, with Curtis Mayfield leading the group.

paramore|still into you.fact: "Still Into You" is from Paramore's 2013 self-titled album. It peaked at No. 24 on the Billboard Hot 100, tying the band's previous best at that time, and became their first top-ten hit on the Mainstream Top 40 chart.

the power station|some like it hot.fact: The Power Station was a 1985 supergroup of Duran Duran members John and Andy Taylor, Chic's Tony Thompson, and singer Robert Palmer. "Some Like It Hot" was produced by Chic's Bernard Edwards and reached No. 6 on the Billboard Hot 100.

lenny kravitz|let love rule.fact: Lenny Kravitz's 1989 debut album Let Love Rule, released on Virgin Records, was written and produced by Kravitz, who played most of the instruments himself. Its title track reached No. 89 on the Hot 100, and the album peaked at No. 61 on the Billboard 200.

sparks|beat the clock.fact: "Beat the Clock" came from Sparks' 1979 album No. 1 in Heaven, produced by disco pioneer Giorgio Moroder. It reached No. 10 on the UK Singles Chart in August 1979, the band's third and final UK top-ten single.

free|all right now.fact: Andy Fraser wrote "All Right Now" in a dressing room after a poor show, because the band needed an upbeat rocker to close their sets. It reached No. 2 in the UK and No. 4 on the US Billboard Hot 100 in 1970, and its album Fire and Water was Free's most successful.

ok go|the writing's on the wall.fact: The 2014 video for "The Writing's on the Wall" was shot in a Brooklyn warehouse as a single continuous take with 28 optical illusions. It reportedly took nearly three weeks of rehearsal and about 50 takes to get right.

haim|the wire.fact: "The Wire" was the fourth single from HAIM's 2013 debut album Days Are Gone. It reached No. 16 on the UK Singles Chart and No. 12 in Australia.

The Everly Brothers|Bye, Bye Love.fact: Written by the husband-and-wife team Felice and Boudleaux Bryant, 'Bye Bye Love' was reportedly turned down by about 30 acts before the Everly Brothers recorded it. It became their first big hit in 1957, reaching No. 2 on the Billboard pop chart and No. 1 on the country chart.

Elvis Presley|Little Sister.fact: Written by Doc Pomus and Mort Shuman, 'Little Sister' was recorded at RCA Studio B in Nashville on June 25-26, 1961. It reached No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100 and, paired with '(Marie's the Name) His Latest Flame,' hit No. 1 in the UK.

Katy Perry|California Gurls feat. Snoop.fact: 'California Gurls' was written by Katy Perry with Dr. Luke, Max Martin, Bonnie McKee, Benny Blanco and Snoop Dogg, and topped the Billboard Hot 100 in 2010. It was the first of five No. 1 singles from Teenage Dream, tying Michael Jackson's Bad for the most from one album.

Cher|Believe.fact: Producer Mark Taylor used Auto-Tune on Cher's vocals for 'Believe' because the studio had no vocoder, helping popularize the effect, then new, as a pop sound. The song won the Grammy for Best Dance Recording and was also nominated for Record of the Year.

Barbra Streisand|Memory.fact: 'Memory' comes from Andrew Lloyd Webber's musical Cats, and Lloyd Webber himself produced Streisand's version. It was one of two new tracks on her 1981 album Memories, which reached No. 10 and went 5x Platinum in the US.

Bobby Brown|My Perogative.fact: 'My Prerogative' was co-written by Bobby Brown with Gene Griffin and Teddy Riley and is considered one of the first major new jack swing hits. It reached No. 1 on both the Billboard Hot 100 and the R&B chart and came from the album Don't Be Cruel (1988).

The Weeknd|Call Out My Name.fact: 'Call Out My Name' debuted at No. 1 on Billboard's Hot R&B Songs chart in April 2018, the week his EP My Dear Melancholy, reached No. 1 on the Billboard 200. Frank Dukes produced and co-wrote it, and Nicolas Jaar received a credit for a sample of his song 'Killing Time.'

Johnny Williams|Slow Motion (Part 1).fact: 'Slow Motion (Part 1)' was released in 1972 on Philadelphia International Records, the label of producers Gamble & Huff. AllMusic calls it Johnny Williams' biggest hit, and it was a Top Ten R&B single.

Rod Stewart|The First Cut Is The Deepest.fact: Cat Stevens wrote 'The First Cut Is the Deepest' in 1967, and P.P. Arnold released the first version that year, before Stevens recorded it himself. Rod Stewart's 1976 recording, from A Night on the Town, became a big UK hit.

Clinic|Distortions.fact: 'Distortions' is a single from Clinic's 2000 debut album Internal Wrangler, and reached No. 80 on the UK Singles Chart. The Liverpool band, formed in 1993 under the name Pure Morning, is known for wearing surgical masks on stage, which singer Ade Blackburn calls a tacky pun on the band name.

Chicago|Does Anybody Really Know What Ti.fact: Keyboardist Robert Lamm wrote and sang lead on this song, which appeared on the band's 1969 debut Chicago Transit Authority. It was recorded in January 1969 and released as a single in late 1970.

Rolling Stones|Tumbling Dice.fact: 'Tumbling Dice' was recorded for Exile on Main St. while the band lived as tax exiles in southern France, with sessions at Nellcote and later Sunset Sound in Los Angeles. Mick Taylor played bass on the track, and Nicky Hopkins added piano.

Edwin McCain|I'll Be.fact: 'I'll Be' was written and performed by Edwin McCain as the first single from his album Misguided Roses and went to US radio in October 1997. It has since become a popular first-dance song at weddings.

James Brown and The Famous Flames|Please.fact: King Records founder Syd Nathan reportedly disliked 'Please, Please, Please,' calling it a stuttering record because of its repeated title. Released on the King subsidiary Federal in 1956, it became James Brown's first hit and reached the top 6 of the R&B chart.

Amy Winehouse|Back to Black.fact: The album Back to Black was made with producers Mark Ronson and Salaam Remi, and Ronson brought in Sharon Jones' band the Dap-Kings for a vintage sound. The title track draws on 1960s girl-group pop and Phil Spector's Wall of Sound, and the Dap-Kings later became Winehouse's touring band.

James Carr|The Dark End of the Street.fact: Dan Penn and Chips Moman wrote the song in Memphis during a 1966 DJ convention, in a hotel room offered by Goldwax producer Quinton Claunch on condition they give him the song for James Carr. Carr's recording, cut at Royal Studios, reached No. 10 on the R&B chart and was later covered by artists including Aretha Franklin and Linda Ronstadt.

Mumford & Sons|I Will Wait.fact: 'I Will Wait' was the lead single from Mumford & Sons' second album Babel, produced by Markus Dravs and released in 2012. The song was Grammy-nominated, and Babel went on to win Album of the Year.

Bryan Adams Rod Stewart, Sting|All For L.fact: 'All for Love' was written by Bryan Adams, Robert John 'Mutt' Lange and Michael Kamen for The Three Musketeers soundtrack. Producer Lange reworded the Musketeers' motto 'All for one' into the title, and Kamen suggested Adams add two more singers, leading to Rod Stewart and Sting. It reached No. 1 in the US and in several other countries.

Bob Seger & The Silver Bullet Band|Like.fact: 'Like a Rock' is the title track of Seger's 1986 album and became famous as the theme of Chevrolet truck commercials from 1991 to 2004. Chevy reportedly wanted Springsteen's 'Born in the U.S.A.' first, and Seger turned the offer down for a long time before agreeing.

Bon Jovi|You Give Love A Bad Name.fact: Co-written with Desmond Child, 'You Give Love a Bad Name' was the first single from Slippery When Wet and became Bon Jovi's first Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 in November 1986. 'Livin' on a Prayer' followed it to No. 1 about eleven weeks later.

BTS|Dynamite.fact: 'Dynamite,' released August 21, 2020, was BTS's first fully English-language single and became their first No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100. It earned the group their first Grammy nomination, for Best Pop Duo/Group Performance.

Bloc Party|Like Eating Glass.fact: 'Like Eating Glass' opens Bloc Party's debut album Silent Alarm, produced by Paul Epworth with the band. The record was made in part at DeltaLab Studios in Copenhagen during summer 2004, with additional recording in London.
