Stevie Wonder|You Are The Sunshine Of My.fact: From Talking Book (1972), the song reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and won Stevie Wonder a Grammy for Best Male Pop Vocal Performance. The first lines are sung by backing singers Jim Gilstrap and Lani Groves, and Wonder sings the rest.

Icona Pop|I Love It.fact: Charli XCX wrote 'I Love It' in about 30 minutes during a session in Sweden with Patrik Berger, then gave it to Icona Pop, who re-recorded it with her vocals featured. It peaked at No. 7 on the Billboard Hot 100 after a boost from an HBO Girls episode.

Frankie Valli|My Eyes Adored You.fact: Written by Bob Crewe and Kenny Nolan, the song was first recorded by the Four Seasons in 1974 and rejected by Capitol and Atlantic before Frankie Valli got it released on Private Stock Records. It hit No. 1 on March 22, 1975, and was knocked off the top by 'Lady Marmalade,' another Crewe and Nolan song.

Billy Joel|The River Of Dreams.fact: 'The River of Dreams' draws on gospel and spirituals, with a gospel choir on the recording. It peaked at No. 3 on the Hot 100, and its parent album, with a cover painted by Christie Brinkley, became Joel's fourth No. 1 album in 1993.

Jerry Lee Lewis|Whole Lotta Shakin' Goin.fact: Jerry Lee Lewis cut his version at Sun Studio in Memphis in a single take in February 1957, with producer Jack Clement already rolling tape. Big Maybelle had recorded the song first in 1955, and Lewis's version reached No. 3 on the Hot 100 and was added to the Library of Congress National Recording Registry in 2005.

Dusty Springfield|Wishin' And Hopin'.fact: Burt Bacharach and Hal David wrote this song, and Dionne Warwick first recorded it in 1963 as a B-side and album track. Dusty Springfield heard Warwick's version and recorded her own at Olympic Studios; DJs began playing the album cut, which pushed her label to issue it as a US single, where it became a Top 10 hit.

James Blake|Limit to Your Love.fact: James Blake's minimalist cover of Feist's song (written by Feist and Chilly Gonzales for her album The Reminder) opens his 2011 self-titled debut album. Zane Lowe named it his 'Hottest Record in the World' in September 2010, and the single peaked at number 39 on the UK Singles Chart.

Commodores|Lady (You Bring Me Up).fact: This 1981 hit from the album In the Pocket was written by William King, Shirley Hanna-King and Harold Hudson, with Lionel Richie singing lead. It reached number 8 on the Billboard Hot 100 and number 5 on the R&B chart, and earned a Grammy nomination for Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals.

Minako Hamano|Super Metroid (Ending).fact: The Super Metroid ending music is an extended arrangement by Minako Hamano, who co-scored the game, built on a heroic brass theme originally composed by Kenji Yamamoto. Yamamoto has said the original theme came to him suddenly while he was driving home from work.

Cat Stevens|Moonshadow.fact: Cat Stevens has said he wrote 'Moonshadow' while on holiday in Spain, when he looked down on a moonlit night and noticed his own shadow. It was released as a single on Island in the UK in 1970 and in the US on A&M in 1971, and appears on the album Teaser and the Firecat, which reached the top 3 in both the UK and US.

Death Cab for Cutie|The New Year.fact: 'The New Year' opens Death Cab for Cutie's 2003 album Transatlanticism, produced by guitarist Chris Walla on Barsuk Records. It was released as the album's second single in February 2004, and the album went on to be certified Platinum by the RIAA.

New York Dolls|Personality Crisis.fact: 'Personality Crisis' opens the New York Dolls' 1973 self-titled debut album on Mercury, which was recorded at the Record Plant in New York and produced by Todd Rundgren, formerly of the band Nazz. Engineer Jack Douglas reportedly handled much of the work at the board while Rundgren was rarely in the studio.

Felt|Rain of Crystal Spires.fact: 'Rain of Crystal Spires' opens Felt's 1986 album Forever Breathes the Lonely Word and was issued as a single on Creation Records in September 1986. It was released after the band moved to Creation that year, and the Felt discography lists it as a UK indie chart hit.

Danny & The Juniors|At The Hop.fact: The song was originally called 'Do the Bop,' but American Bandstand host Dick Clark worried the bop dance fad was fading and suggested changing the chorus to 'Let's go to the hop.' The group had previously performed as the Juvenairs, and the record went on to spend multiple weeks at number one in 1958.

Air France|Collapsing Outside Your Doors.fact: The Swedish duo Air France (Joel Karlsson and Henrik Markstedt) released this track, listed as 'Collapsing at Your Doorstep', on their 2008 EP No Way Down on Sincerely Yours. The EP's vocals on this track are by Teresa Jaksetic, and Pitchfork rated it 8.6 and placed it at number 14 on its top 50 albums of 2008.

Maroon 5|Moves Like Jagger feat. Christi.fact: 'Moves Like Jagger' reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100, becoming Maroon 5's second chart-topper after 'Make Me Wonder.' It paired Adam Levine with fellow NBC's The Voice coach Christina Aguilera, earned a Grammy nomination for Best Pop Duo/Group Performance, and has sold over 14 million digital copies.

Built to Spill|You Were Right.fact: 'You Were Right' is on Built to Spill's 1999 album Keep It Like a Secret, produced by Phil Ek and Doug Martsch and recorded at Bear Creek Studio in Woodinville, Washington. The song is built as a collage of well-known lyrics from other artists' songs, and it nearly missed the album over copyright concerns before Warner Bros. secured permission at the last minute.

Del the Funky Homosapien|Mistadobalina.fact: 'Mistadobalina' was the second single from Del the Funky Homosapien's 1991 debut album I Wish My Brother George Was Here on Elektra, and peaked at number 6 on the Billboard Hot Rap Songs chart. Del, a cousin of Ice Cube, started out writing lyrics for Ice Cube's group Da Lench Mob, and the album title nods to George Clinton.

Crosby, Stills & Nash|Southern Cross.fact: Stephen Stills wrote 'Southern Cross' with Rick and Michael Curtis by reworking their song 'Seven League Boots,' and it appears on the 1982 album Daylight Again. The sailing-themed song reached number 18 on the Billboard Hot 100 and became a concert staple for Jimmy Buffett and his Coral Reefer Band.

Crowded House|Don't Dream It's Over.fact: Neil Finn wrote 'Don't Dream It's Over' for Crowded House's 1986 self-titled debut album, produced by Mitchell Froom. It reached number two on the Billboard Hot 100 and number one in New Zealand, and won Song of the Year and Best Video at the first ARIA Music Awards in 1987.

Camera Obscura|Keep It Clean.fact: 'Keep It Clean' is track two on Camera Obscura's second album, Underachievers Please Try Harder, released in August 2003 on Merge Records. Every track on the album was written by singer Tracyanne Campbell, and the album was produced by Geoff Allan with the band.

Sparks|A Big Surprise.fact: 'A Big Surprise' opens Sparks' 1977 album Introducing Sparks, their second and final album for Columbia Records. It was issued as a UK single in September 1977 backed with 'Forever Young,' and Record Collector later singled it out as one of the album's highlights.

The Decemberists|The Perfect Crime #2.fact: 'The Perfect Crime #2' is track five on the Decemberists' 2006 album The Crane Wife, produced by Tucker Martine and Chris Walla. Reviewers called it the band's funkiest song to date, noting a slinky bass line, funky keyboards and a prominent cowbell, and it was released as a single in 2007.

Jessie J|Price Tag.fact: 'Price Tag' was written by Jessie J with Dr. Luke, Claude Kelly and B.o.B, and produced by Dr. Luke. It entered at number one on the UK Singles Chart, topped the charts in Ireland and New Zealand, and was the lead US single from her debut album Who You Are.

Partridge Family|I Think I Love You.fact: Tony Romeo wrote 'I Think I Love You,' the Partridge Family's debut single, released in August 1970, a month before the TV show premiered. David Cassidy sang lead with backing by Los Angeles session players associated with the Wrecking Crew, and it hit number one on the Hot 100 for three weeks and was the best-selling single of 1970.

The Flaming Lips|Feeling Yourself Disint.fact: 'Feeling Yourself Disintegrate' is on the Flaming Lips' 1999 album The Soft Bulletin, recorded between 1997 and 1999 at Tarbox Road Studios in Cassadaga, New York, and produced by the band with Dave Fridmann and Scott Booker. The album's symphonic sound was partly achieved by detuning and layering MIDI keyboards, and Pitchfork ranked it third on its list of the best albums of the 1990s.

Coleman Hawkins|La Rosita.fact: Coleman Hawkins recorded 'La Rosita' on the 1957 album Coleman Hawkins Encounters Ben Webster, cut in Los Angeles with an Oscar Peterson-led rhythm section including Herb Ellis, Ray Brown and Alvin Stoller. He recorded it again in 1959 for Prestige on the album Hawk Eyes with Charlie Shavers on trumpet.

James Taylor|Carolina In My Mind.fact: James Taylor began writing 'Carolina in My Mind' at producer Peter Asher's London flat while recording his 1968 debut for the Beatles' Apple Records at Trident Studios. Paul McCartney is reported to have played bass on it, and the original single only reached number 67 in the US on its 1970 reissue, before Taylor's 1976 re-recording became the version most listeners know.

Beyonce|Crazy In Love feat. Jay Z.fact: The famous horn hook in 'Crazy in Love' is a sample of the Chi-Lites' 1970 song 'Are You My Woman (Tell Me So)', which producer Rich Harrison had treasured long before working with Beyonce. She reportedly worried at first that the beat sounded too retro, and the song went on to win the Grammy for Best R&B Song.

Katy Perry|Teenage Dream.fact: The title track helped make Katy Perry's album Teenage Dream the second album ever to produce five No. 1 singles on the Billboard Hot 100, tying Michael Jackson's Bad. She was the first woman to do it, with the other chart-toppers being "California Gurls," "Firework," "E.T.," and "Last Friday Night (T.G.I.F.)."

Guided by Voices|The Official Ironmen Ra.fact: This Guided by Voices crowd favorite is the fourth track on the 1996 album Under the Bushes Under the Stars, released on Matador. It came out as a single on February 27, 1996, a month before the album, and a Grammy.com piece calls it a chest-beating anthem for the devoted fans.

Dan Fogelberg|Leader Of The Band.fact: Dan Fogelberg wrote this song for his father, Lawrence Fogelberg, a music teacher and band director who led bands at Pekin Community High School in Illinois. It appeared on the 1981 album The Innocent Age, and Dan said he was glad to give his father the tribute while he was still alive.

Dead Or Alive|You Spin Me Round (Like A.fact: Stock Aitken Waterman, who produced this Dead or Alive hit, scored their first UK No. 1 with it in March 1985. It was the lead single from the album Youthquake and also reached No. 11 on the US Billboard Hot 100.

Genesis|Follow You Follow Me.fact: Released in February 1978 from the album ...And Then There Were Three..., this was Genesis's first UK top 10 hit, reaching No. 7, and their first US top 40 hit, reaching No. 23. It was the song that brought the group its first worldwide pop success.

Fleetwood Mac|Dreams.fact: "Dreams" is Fleetwood Mac's only No. 1 single on the Billboard Hot 100, reaching the top in 1977 as the second single from Rumours. Stevie Nicks has said she wrote it in about 10 minutes on a keyboard at the studio.

Dirty Projectors|Rise Above.fact: Dirty Projectors' 2007 album Rise Above is Dave Longstreth's re-creation of Black Flag's 1981 album Damaged, rebuilt entirely from memory. He hadn't heard the original since middle school, so the arrangements, track order and many lyrics differ sharply from it.

Jackie DeShannon|Put A Little Love In Yo.fact: Jackie DeShannon co-wrote this song with her brother Randy Myers and soul singer Jimmy Holiday. Her 1969 recording reached No. 4 on the Hot 100, her biggest US hit, and Annie Lennox and Al Green took a cover to No. 9 in 1988.

Michael Jackson|Rock With You.fact: Rod Temperton wrote this song, and Quincy Jones produced it for Off the Wall. Temperton had first hoped it would appear on an album by his group Heatwave, and it was also offered to Karen Carpenter before Jackson recorded it. It spent four weeks at No. 1 on the Hot 100 in early 1980.

Drake|Forever.fact: "Forever" teams Drake with Kanye West, Lil Wayne and Eminem. It was released in August 2009 for the LeBron James documentary More than a Game and peaked at No. 8 on the Billboard Hot 100. It was Drake's highest debut at the time.

The Highwomen|Highwomen.fact: The opening track of The Highwomen's 2019 debut album is a response to Jimmy Webb's "Highwayman," which the Highwaymen made famous. Brandi Carlile and Amanda Shires adapted Webb's idea with his blessing and help. They gave each singer a different role, including a freedom rider, a healer and a preacher.

Duncan Sheik|Barely Breathing.fact: "Barely Breathing" peaked at No. 16 on the Billboard Hot 100 but stayed on the chart for 55 weeks. It earned Duncan Sheik a Grammy nomination for Best Male Pop Vocal Performance, and he later became a Broadway composer.

Dexy's Midnight Runners|Geno.fact: "Geno" was Dexys Midnight Runners' first UK No. 1, reaching the top on 3 May 1980 for two weeks. It is a tribute to soul singer Geno Washington, who fronted the Ram Jam Band, and Kevin Rowland's brother took him to see Washington perform when he was 11.

Kenta Nagata, Satomi Terui|Mario Kart 7.fact: The Mario Kart 7 staff credits theme is led by a saxophone and quotes other music from the game, including the Title Screen theme and Toad Circuit. Kenta Nagata and Satomi Terui composed the game's music, though the Super Mario Wiki cannot say which of them wrote this piece.

Elton John|Harmony.fact: "Harmony" closes Elton John's 1973 double album Goodbye Yellow Brick Road. The sessions were planned for Jamaica, but the studio there proved unusable, so the band moved to the Chateau d'Herouville in France. Gus Dudgeon produced the album, and it was recorded there in May 1973.

The Beach Boys|Sloop John B..fact: "Sloop John B." began as a Bahamian folk song called "The John B. Sails," and the Beach Boys based their version on the Kingston Trio's 1958 recording. Al Jardine suggested that the band record it, and Brian Wilson arranged it for Pet Sounds with an elaborate a cappella vocal section.

Eagles|Best Of My Love.fact: "Best of My Love" gave the Eagles their first No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in March 1975. It was the third single from On the Border, and Glenn Frey, Don Henley and J.D. Souther wrote it while working on the album in London.

Dionne Warwick|I Say A Little Prayer.fact: Burt Bacharach and Hal David wrote and produced this song, and Dionne Warwick's version reached No. 4 on the Hot 100 in late 1967. Aretha Franklin's cover from her album Aretha Now was a top 10 hit in 1968, and Bacharach later said hers was better than their own recording.

Neutral Milk Hotel|The King of Carrot Fl.fact: This track opens side one of In the Aeroplane Over the Sea, which was recorded at Pet Sounds studio in Denver in 1997 and released in 1998 on Merge Records. Producer Robert Schneider got the album's fuzzy sound by using heavy compression instead of guitar pedals or effects.

Little Richard|Tutti Frutti.fact: "Tutti Frutti" was recorded in September 1955 at Cosimo Matassa's J&M Studio in New Orleans. Robert "Bumps" Blackwell produced the session, and Fats Domino's backing band played on it. Specialty Records released it in October 1955, only weeks after the session, and it reached No. 17 on the pop chart and No. 2 on the R&B chart.

Andrew W.K.|Party Hard.fact: "Party Hard" came out in October 2001 from Andrew W.K.'s debut album I Get Wet and was his first mainstream hit, reaching No. 19 on the UK singles chart. It later turned up in commercials for products including Coors Light and Expedia.

13th Floor Elevators|You're Gonna Miss M.fact: Roky Erickson first recorded this song with his earlier Austin band, the Spades, before the 13th Floor Elevators re-recorded it. It reached No. 55 on the Billboard Hot 100, the band's only US chart single, and it is one of the earliest rock songs to feature Tommy Hall's electric jug.

Blessid Union of Souls|Hey Leonardo.fact: "Hey Leonardo (She Likes Me for Me)" is from Blessid Union of Souls' third album, Walking Off the Buzz, released April 27, 1999 on V2 Records. The single reached No. 8 on the Billboard Mainstream Top 40 chart.

Don Henley|All She Wants To Do Is Dance.fact: Written by Danny Kortchmar, who also co-produced Building the Perfect Beast with Henley and Greg Ladanyi, this was the album's second single. It reached No. 9 on the Billboard Hot 100 and topped the Top Rock Tracks chart, Henley's third chart-topper there.

Bee Gees|You Should Be Dancing.fact: Released in 1976 as the first single from Children of the World, it hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent seven weeks atop the US Hot Dance Club Play chart. It was later included on the Saturday Night Fever soundtrack, and is often cited as the first chart-topper to feature Barry Gibb's falsetto.

Doobie Brothers|Rockin' Down The Highway.fact: Tom Johnston wrote it in the same rented room in San Jose where he wrote 'Listen to the Music' and 'China Grove.' It is track 2 on the Doobie Brothers' 1972 album Toulouse Street, right after 'Listen to the Music,' and was first released as the B-side of 'Jesus Is Just Alright.'

Aesop Rock|Daylight.fact: 'Daylight' is on Aesop Rock's 2001 album Labor Days, his first project for the Definitive Jux label and a concept album about the working life. It became the title of a 2002 EP that also included a reworking called 'Night Light.'

The Cookies|Chains.fact: Written by Gerry Goffin and Carole King, 'Chains' was a 1962 hit for the girl group the Cookies. The Beatles covered it on their debut album Please Please Me, recorded February 11, 1963, with George Harrison singing lead.

Michael Murphey|Wildfire.fact: Written by Michael Murphey and Larry Cansler, 'Wildfire' was the lead single from the 1975 album Blue Sky - Night Thunder. It reached No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100 and topped the Adult Contemporary chart.

Chapterhouse|Pearl.fact: Chapterhouse formed in Reading, England in 1987 and began by playing alongside Spacemen 3. 'Pearl' features guest vocals by Rachel Goswell of Slowdive, and their debut album Whirlpool (1991) reached No. 23 on the UK Albums Chart.

Katy Perry|Part of Me.fact: Written by Perry, Dr. Luke, Max Martin and Bonnie McKee, 'Part of Me' was left off the original Teenage Dream because Perry felt it did not fit the album. It was reworked as the lead single of the 2012 reissue Teenage Dream: The Complete Confection and debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.

Aphex Twin|Avril 14th.fact: This two-minute piano piece from Aphex Twin's 2001 album Drukqs was reportedly recorded on a Yamaha Disklavier, a computer-controlled piano. Every year musicians post their own cover versions around April 14, and Kanye West sampled it on 'Blame Game.'

Maroon 5|Love Somebody.fact: Written by Adam Levine, Nathaniel Motte, Ryan Tedder and Noel Zancanella, with Tedder and Zancanella producing, it was the fourth and final single from Overexposed (2012). It peaked at No. 10 on the Billboard Hot 100.

Doug E. Fresh|The Show.fact: Released in August 1985 as Doug E. Fresh & the Get Fresh Crew, 'The Show' features Fresh's human beatboxing, and its B-side 'La Di Da Di' was rapped by Slick Rick, then billed as MC Ricky D. The track's melody borrows from the Inspector Gadget theme, and it reached No. 7 on the UK Singles Chart.

Eagles|The Long Run.fact: Written by Don Henley and Glenn Frey, the title track was released as a single in November 1979. The album took from March 1978 to September 1979 to record across studios in Florida and Los Angeles, with producer Bill Szymczyk finishing the final mix at 5:59 a.m. on September 1, 1979.

Koji Kondo|Super Mario 64 (Staff Roll).fact: Koji Kondo composed the Super Mario 64 'Staff Roll' end-credits theme in C major. It is track 35 of the official soundtrack at 3:27, returned in the Nintendo DS remake, and was added to Nintendo Music on December 24, 2024.

Chicago|Baby, What A Big Surprise.fact: Peter Cetera wrote and sang this song, his only songwriting credit and lead vocal on Chicago XI (1977). It reached No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100 and was the last Top 10 hit by Chicago's original lineup.

Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young|Teach Your.fact: The pedal steel guitar on this Graham Nash song was played by the Grateful Dead's Jerry Garcia, who was recording in the next studio. In return, CSNY reportedly agreed to help the Dead improve their vocal harmonies, and the song reached No. 16 in 1970.

The Four Seasons|Working My Way Back To.fact: Written by Sandy Linzer and Denny Randell, the Four Seasons' 1966 version reached No. 9 on the Billboard Hot 100. The Spinners covered it in 1979 with a new bridge by Michael Zager, and their medley reached No. 1 in the UK.

Sleater-Kinney|One More Hour.fact: This track is from Sleater-Kinney's third album, Dig Me Out (1997, Kill Rock Stars), produced by John Goodmanson. It marked the first album with drummer Janet Weiss alongside Corin Tucker and Carrie Brownstein, and the song was issued as a single in 1998.

Nina Simone|My Baby Just Cares for Me.fact: Nina Simone recorded it in the late 1950s, and it appeared on her debut album Little Girl Blue. It became a hit decades later when a 1987 Chanel No. 5 TV ad used it, and the reissued single reached No. 5 in the UK.

Cascada|Everytime We Touch.fact: Cascada's dance hit borrows its chorus from Maggie Reilly's 1992 song of the same name, and Reilly is credited as a songwriter. Cascada's version reached No. 10 on the Billboard Hot 100, topped the Dance Radio Airplay chart, and peaked at No. 2 in the UK.

Gary Lewis & The Playboys|She's Just My.fact: This 1965 single reached No. 3 and was one of seven straight Top 10 hits for Gary Lewis & the Playboys between 1965 and 1966. Session musician Leon Russell, later a solo star, helped arrange and produce their hits.

Pharrell Williams|Happy.fact: Pharrell wrote and produced 'Happy' for Despicable Me 2, and it was nominated for the Best Original Song Oscar. He performed it at the 86th Academy Awards on March 2, 2014, and its 24 Hours of Happy website played the song on a loop with 24 different four-minute takes.

Yo La Tengo|Sugarcube.fact: The video for 'Sugarcube' (from I Can Hear the Heart Beating as One, 1997) was made with the Mr. Show crew and stars Bob Odenkirk and David Cross as instructors at a 'rock school.' The band said it aired on MTV only once or twice, and a director's cut with 30 extra seconds was released for the album's 25th anniversary.

Madonna|Take A Bow.fact: Co-written by Babyface, who also sings backing vocals, 'Take a Bow' is from Madonna's 1994 album Bedtime Stories. It spent seven weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, her longest run at the top.

Elvis Costello|Veronica.fact: Elvis Costello co-wrote 'Veronica' with Paul McCartney for the 1989 album Spike. It reached No. 19 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 1 on the Modern Rock chart, making it Costello's highest-charting US Top 40 hit.

Eurythmics|Would I Lie To You.fact: Annie Lennox and Dave Stewart wrote it, and Stewart produced the album Be Yourself Tonight (1985). The single reached No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100, their third US Top 10 hit, and No. 17 in the UK.

The Beach Boys|When I Grow Up (To Be A M.fact: Written by Brian Wilson and Mike Love, this 1964 single reached No. 9 in the US. It was included on The Beach Boys Today! (1965), which reached No. 4 on the Billboard album chart.

Olivia Newton-John|Please Mr. Please.fact: "Please Mr. Please" was written by Bruce Welch and John Rostill of The Shadows, and Welch had recorded it himself in 1974 without much success. Olivia Newton-John's 1975 version reached No. 3 on the US Billboard Hot 100.

Paul McCartney|Maybe I'm Amazed.fact: Paul McCartney recorded "Maybe I'm Amazed" at EMI's Abbey Road Studio Two in February 1970 for his debut solo album, playing guitars, bass, piano, organ and drums himself. Linda McCartney sang backing vocals.

5th Dimension|Aquarius, Let The Sunshine.fact: The 5th Dimension's medley of two songs from the musical Hair hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 for six weeks in 1969. It won the 1970 Grammy for Record of the Year, the group's second win in that category after "Up, Up and Away."

Styx|Fooling Yourself (The Angry Young M.fact: Tommy Shaw's song from Styx's 1977 album The Grand Illusion switches time signatures, with 6/8 in the intro and outro, 4/4 in the vocal sections, and a synthesizer solo in 7/4. It peaked at No. 29 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1978.

Del Amitri|Roll To Me.fact: "Roll to Me" was the third single from Del Amitri's 1995 album Twisted and became the Scottish band's biggest US hit, reaching No. 10 on the Billboard Hot 100. It did less well at home, peaking at No. 22 in the UK.

Bon Iver|Skinny Love.fact: Justin Vernon recorded the album For Emma, Forever Ago, which includes "Skinny Love," over about three months in a remote hunting cabin in northwestern Wisconsin that belonged to his father. "Skinny Love" became the album's best-performing single and later went gold.

Mike Posner|Cooler Than Me.fact: "Cooler Than Me" was the lead single from Mike Posner's debut album and peaked at No. 6 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2010. It has since been certified multi-platinum by the RIAA.

A Tribe Called Quest|Jazz (We've Got).fact: "Jazz (We've Got)" was the second single from A Tribe Called Quest's 1991 album The Low End Theory, which blended jazz samples with minimalist bass and drum breaks. Rolling Stone reports the beat was a rearrangement of one Q-Tip heard while visiting producer Pete Rock.

Falco|Der Kommissar.fact: Falco's "Der Kommissar" reached No. 1 in several countries including West Germany, Austria and Italy. English-speaking audiences mostly knew the 1982 cover by the British band After the Fire, which climbed into the US Top 5 in 1983.

Glenn Frey|The Heat Is On.fact: "The Heat Is On" was written and produced by Harold Faltermeyer and Keith Forsey for the film Beverly Hills Cop, and Glenn Frey recorded his vocal in a single day. It reached No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1985, the highest-charting solo single by any Eagles member.

Mahito Yokota|Super Mario Galaxy.fact: Mahito Yokota composed, arranged and orchestrated much of the Super Mario Galaxy score with Koji Kondo. The orchestral music was performed by the Mario Galaxy Orchestra and conducted by Koji Haishima. Kondo reportedly rejected Yokota's first Latin-style ideas as sounding cute rather than cool, which pushed the score toward an orchestral sound for Mario's first trip into space.

Henry Mancini|Moon River.fact: Henry Mancini composed "Moon River" with lyrics by Johnny Mercer for the 1961 film Breakfast at Tiffany's. It won the Academy Award for Best Original Song and the Grammy for Record of the Year. An inlet near Mercer's hometown of Savannah, Georgia, was later named Moon River.

Gloria Gaynor|I Will Survive.fact: "I Will Survive" started out as the B-side of Gloria Gaynor's 1978 single, whose A-side was a cover called "Substitute." Dance-club DJs flipped the record, and the song became a disco-era No. 1 hit.

The Beach Boys|I Get Around.fact: "I Get Around" became the Beach Boys' first No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in the week of July 4, 1964, replacing Peter and Gordon's "A World Without Love." It was also the first thing they recorded after the Beatles took over the charts, and it was their breakthrough hit in the UK.

AC/DC|Highway to Hell.fact: Highway to Hell, released in 1979, was the first of three AC/DC albums produced by Robert John "Mutt" Lange. The label wanted a more radio-friendly sound, and the album became the band's first to reach the US Top 20.

Jackie Wilson|Lonely Teardrops.fact: "Lonely Teardrops" was co-written by Berry Gordy, his sister Gwendolyn Gordy and Roquel "Billy" Davis, who used the pen name Tyran Carlo. Jackie Wilson's 1958 recording on Brunswick reached the top of the R&B chart and No. 7 on the pop chart.

The Beach Boys|Fun, Fun, Fun.fact: Brian Wilson and Mike Love wrote "Fun, Fun, Fun," and its opening guitar riff was based on Chuck Berry's "Johnny B. Goode." Released in early 1964, it peaked at No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100, held back by the Beatles' singles.

Men I Trust|Show Me How.fact: Montreal trio Men I Trust released "Show Me How" as a single in 2018, and it was later re-recorded for their album Oncle Jazz. Producers Statik Selektah and Heavy Mellow sampled it for Joey Bada$$'s "Show Me," and the band performed it with him on The Tonight Show.

Bjork|Human Behaviour.fact: "Human Behaviour" was the 1993 lead single from Bjork's debut solo album Debut, produced and co-written by Nellee Hooper. Its video was the first Bjork collaboration with director Michel Gondry and was nominated for a 1994 Grammy for Best Short Form Music Video.

Human League|Human.fact: "Human" was written and produced by Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis at their Flyte Time studio in Minneapolis, after Virgin Records suggested the pairing. In 1986 it reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, the band's second and final chart-topper there after "Don't You Want Me."

Irene Cara|Fame.fact: "Fame," written by Michael Gore and Dean Pitchford for the 1980 film of the same name, won the Academy Award for Best Original Song, and the film also won Best Original Score. Irene Cara performed at the Oscar ceremony, where she sang both of her nominated songs from the film.

The Allman Brothers Band|Ramblin' Man.fact: Dickey Betts wrote and sang "Ramblin' Man," the lead single from the 1973 album Brothers and Sisters. It was the band's only Top 10 single, peaking at No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100, held from No. 1 by Cher's "Half-Breed."

Boney M.|Rasputin.fact: "Rasputin" was the second single from Boney M.'s 1978 album Nightflight to Venus and was written by Frank Farian, George Reyam and Fred Jay. It reached No. 1 in Germany, Austria and Australia and went to No. 2 in the UK.

Alicia Keys|Fallin'.fact: "Fallin'" spent six non-consecutive weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2001. At the 2002 Grammys it won Song of the Year, Best R&B Song and Best Female R&B Vocal Performance, and Keys won five awards that night, tying the record for a woman in a single night.

Bread|If.fact: David Gates wrote and produced "If," which Bread released in 1971 as a single from the album Manna. It reached No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent three weeks at No. 1 on the Easy Listening chart.

FUN.|Carry On.fact: "Carry On" is a track from fun.'s 2012 album Some Nights, which was nominated for Album of the Year at the 55th Grammy Awards. The band performed the song on that Grammy telecast, the same night their single "We Are Young" won Song of the Year.

the olivia tremor control|jumping fences.fact: "Jumping Fences" is the third track on The Olivia Tremor Control's debut album, Music from the Unrealized Film Script: Dusk at Cubist Castle. The neo-psychedelic album came out on Flydaddy Records on August 6, 1996, and packs 27 songs into about 74 minutes. A separate Jumping Fences EP followed in 1997.

the national|not in kansas.fact: "Not in Kansas" is the tenth track on The National's I Am Easy to Find, released May 17, 2019 on 4AD. It was the band's eighth studio album and first since 2017's Sleep Well Beast. The album was paired with a 24-minute short film directed by Mike Mills and starring Alicia Vikander.

mary in the junkyard|blood.fact: "Blood" was released as the fifth single from mary in the junkyard's debut album, Role Model Hermit, ahead of its July 3, 2026 release on AMF Records. The trio recorded the album in London in the summer of 2025 with producer Oli Bayston. The song also has its own music video.

angel olsen|chance.fact: "Chance" appears on Angel Olsen's 2020 album Whole New Mess as a stripped-down take on "Chance (Forever Love)" from All Mirrors. Whole New Mess was recorded solo in a converted church studio in Anacortes, Washington, with just her guitar and occasional organ in place of the orchestral arrangements. It won a 2021 Libera Award for Best Folk/Bluegrass Record.

beach house|only you know.fact: "Only You Know" is track 10 on Beach House's 2022 double album Once Twice Melody, which came out February 18, 2022. The album was rolled out to the public in four "chapters," and this song arrived in the third one.

the go! team|ladyflash.fact: "Ladyflash" is a single from The Go! Team's debut album Thunder, Lightning, Strike, released in 2004. The album earned a 2005 Mercury Prize nomination, up against Coldplay and Bloc Party, with Antony and the Johnsons winning. The single's UK re-issue brought the band national radio airplay on BBC Radio 1 and Xfm.

king gizzard & the lizard wizard|the dri.fact: "The Dripping Tap" runs 18 minutes 17 seconds and was the lead single from King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard's 2022 album Omnium Gatherum, released March 9, 2022. It was first composed during the sessions for 2019's Fishing for Fishies and re-recorded after the COVID-19 lockdowns. It opens as a slow, lo-fi blues before turning into a full jam about 70 seconds in.

bon iver|666 t.fact: "666 ʇ" is on Bon Iver's 2019 album i,i, which was recorded at April Base in Eau Claire, Wisconsin, and Sonic Ranch in Tornillo, Texas. The album was released track by track, one per hour, on August 8, 2019, with the full album following the next day.

the feelies|the boy with the perpetual n.fact: "The Boy with the Perpetual Nervousness" opens The Feelies' debut album Crazy Rhythms, released on Stiff Records in the UK on February 29, 1980. The album was recorded in 1979 in New York City and produced by band members Bill Million and Glenn Mercer with Mark Abel. A 2009 reissue added a demo version of the song as a bonus track.

mission of burma|that's how i escaped my.fact: At just 2:04, "That's How I Escaped My Certain Fate" was written by bassist Clint Conley and closes Mission of Burma's 1982 album Vs. The album was recorded at Normandy Sound in Rhode Island in a large room to capture the raw energy of their live shows, and added tape and electronic effects, mainly from Martin Swope.

dummy|full spectrum dominance.fact: "Full Spectrum Dominance" was the lead single from the Los Angeles band Dummy's album do you love the color of the sky?, their first for Polyvinyl Record Co. The album came out October 16, 2026, and the song is its third track, following "April Limousine" and "Alluvial Fan."

beirut|the penalty.fact: "The Penalty" is track 7 on Beirut's second album, The Flying Club Cup, released October 9, 2007 on 4AD. Zach Condon wrote all the tracks and plays many instruments on the record, including accordion, euphonium and French horn. He drew inspiration from French chanson and a 1910 color photo of hot air balloons at a Paris World's Fair.

bloc party|banquet.fact: "Banquet" was recorded in 2004 at Exchange in London and produced by Paul Epworth and the band. After a first release on Moshi Moshi, it was re-released by Wichita on April 25, 2005, and reached No. 13 on the UK Singles Chart. It became the band's first US Modern Rock entry and has been certified Platinum in the UK.

land of talk|dogs.fact: "Dogs" was released October 14, 2026 as a double single with "Cats" ahead of Land of Talk's sixth album, LASTS, due November 13, 2026 on Saddle Creek. The album was recorded in a cabin in rural Harrington, Quebec, with Michael Feuerstack playing bass and pedal steel and handling engineering and mixing.

panda bear|bros.fact: "Bros" runs 12 and a half minutes and appeared on Panda Bear's 2007 album Person Pitch, which Noah Lennox made in Lisbon, Portugal, largely out of samples. Pitchfork ranked the track No. 3 on its Top 100 Tracks of 2007 and No. 48 on its Top 500 Tracks of the 2000s.

strongboi|dizzy.fact: strongboi is a Berlin-based duo whose 2023 collaborative album built online buzz before their hazy, summery EP 1. "dizzy" is a laid-back funk single meant to evoke the fading energy of summer, and the duo has a London show at Scala on November 27 and a North American tour set for early 2027.

fake names|if you could see me today.fact: Fake Names is a punk supergroup featuring Brian Baker (Minor Threat, Bad Religion) and Dennis Lyxzen (Refused), plus Michael Hampton, Johnny Temple and new drummer Mario Rubalcaba. "If You Could See Me Today" is track nine on their third album Punk Ruins, recorded at Electrical Audio in Chicago and due on Epitaph October 23. It blends jangle pop with the band's D.C. post-hardcore roots.

fontaines d.c. with rosalãa|where is go.fact: "Where Is Gone?" is a duet with Rosalia from Fontaines D.C.'s fifth album Dopamine Chamber, released October 16 and produced by James Ford. Rosalia is the only featured artist on the album's tracklist, and the single arrived October 12.

spoon|can i sit next to you.fact: "Can I Sit Next to You" was the second single from Spoon's 2017 album Hot Thoughts on Matador, released February 21, 2017. The album was produced by Dave Fridmann and Spoon, recorded partly at Fridmann's Tarbox Road studio in New York, and peaked at No. 17 on the Billboard 200.

the war on drugs|pain.fact: "Pain" is track two on The War on Drugs' 2017 album A Deeper Understanding, released on Atlantic Records and produced by Adam Granduciel. The album reached No. 10 on the Billboard 200 and No. 3 in the UK, and won the Grammy for Best Rock Album at the 60th Annual Grammy Awards.

les savy fav|let's get out of here.fact: "Let's Get Out of Here" is track four on Les Savy Fav's 2010 album Root for Ruin, released on Frenchkiss Records. The album leaked in late July and got a digital release on August 3, 2010, ahead of its planned September 14 date.

belle and sebastian|the state i am in.fact: "The State I Am In" opens Belle and Sebastian's debut album Tigermilk, which was recorded in Glasgow in March 1996 in about three days of recording and two of mixing. It came out on the Stow College label Electric Honey in a run limited to 1,000 copies.

neutral milk hotel|oh comely.fact: "Oh Comely" is the 8-minute-plus track on Neutral Milk Hotel's In the Aeroplane Over the Sea, recorded in 1997 at Pet Sounds Studio in Denver and produced by Robert Schneider. Released on Merge in 1998, the album never charted on the Billboard 200 yet has sold more than 393,000 copies, and Pitchfork later ranked it 4th among the best albums of the 1990s.

big thief|certainty.fact: Big Thief wrote "Certainty" during a three-day power outage at Flying Cloud Studios in upstate New York and recorded it straight to a four-track tape machine in the kitchen, powered by the truck's cigarette lighter. They used take three because it took about that many tries to learn the chords. It later appeared on the 2022 album Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You.

the cure|friday i'm in love.fact: "Friday I'm in Love" was released in May 1992 from The Cure's album Wish and climbed to No. 6 in the UK. In the US it reached No. 18 on the Hot 100 and spent four weeks at No. 1 on the Modern Rock Tracks chart. It also won European Viewer's Choice for Best Music Video at the 1992 MTV Video Music Awards.

arctic monkeys|505.fact: "505" closes Arctic Monkeys' 2007 album Favourite Worst Nightmare, produced by James Ford and Mike Crossey, with Miles Kane on guitar and Matt Helders on a 140 BPM motorik beat. It peaked at No. 74 in the UK in 2007 but returned to the charts in 2022 after a TikTok revival, and it is now certified 4x Platinum in the UK.

parquet courts|instant disassembly.fact: "Instant Disassembly" is a roughly seven-minute track from Parquet Courts' 2014 album Sunbathing Animal. Stereogum described it as a sprawling, expansive zone-out with serious echoes of The Modern Lovers.

animal collective|bluish.fact: "Bluish" is track six on Animal Collective's 2009 album Merriweather Post Pavilion, recorded at Sweet Tea Recording Studio in Oxford, Mississippi. The album is named for the Maryland concert venue that band members Dave Portner and Brian Weitz attended as teenagers. It peaked at No. 13 on the Billboard 200 and was named Pitchfork's 2009 Album of the Year.

frankie cosmos|caramelize.fact: "Caramelize" opens Frankie Cosmos's 2018 album Vessel, an 18-track record that runs just over 33 minutes. It was the group's first album for Sub Pop, released March 30, 2018, and it peaked at No. 21 on the US Independent Albums chart.

my morning jacket|i'm amazed.fact: "I'm Amazed" was the lead single from My Morning Jacket's 2008 album Evil Urges, which was recorded at Avatar Studios in New York City with co-producer Joe Chiccarelli. The band performed it on Saturday Night Live in May 2008, and it reached No. 5 on the US Adult Alternative Airplay chart. Rolling Stone ranked it No. 8 on its list of the best songs of 2008.

nick cave & the bad seeds|red right hand.fact: "Red Right Hand" appeared on Nick Cave & The Bad Seeds' 1994 album Let Love In, produced by Tony Cohen and recorded in late 1993. It has since become a screen favorite: it was used in Scream (1996) and the first three films of that series, and it serves as the main theme of the TV series Peaky Blinders. Cave even recorded a separate version for Scream 3.

big audio dynamite ii|rush.fact: "Rush" was the biggest hit for Big Audio Dynamite II, which was led by former Clash guitarist Mick Jones. From the 1991 album The Globe, it spent four weeks at No. 1 on Billboard's Modern Rock Tracks chart in August 1991. It also topped the singles chart in Australia.

primus|jerry was a race car driver.fact: "Jerry Was a Race Car Driver" was Primus's first single, taken from the 1991 album Sailing the Seas of Cheese, which was recorded at Fantasy Studios in Berkeley, California. It reached No. 23 on Billboard's Modern Rock Tracks chart. Its video, mixing live-gig footage with claymation, became an MTV favorite.

public image ltd.|rise.fact: "Rise" was the lead single from Public Image Ltd's 1986 album Album, released in January 1986. John Lydon worked with producer Bill Laswell, who brought in an all-star cast of session players including guitarist Steve Vai, drummer Ginger Baker and keyboardist Bernie Worrell. The single reached No. 11 on the UK singles chart.

mitski|stay soft.fact: "Stay Soft" is a synth-pop track from Mitski's 2022 album Laurel Hell, released on Dead Oceans. Critics compared its sound to 1970s pop and 1980s David Bowie-style arrangements. Mitski performed it on Jimmy Kimmel Live! in March 2022, barefoot in a flowing white gown with choreographed dancing.

primal scream|movin' on up.fact: "Movin' On Up" opens Primal Scream's 1991 album Screamadelica and was the lead track of the 1992 Dixie-Narco EP on Creation Records. Producer Jimmy Miller, famous for his work with the Rolling Stones, mixed it at Eden Studios. Bobby Gillespie credits him with playing two Coca-Cola bottles as percussion on the track.

talking heads|new feeling.fact: "New Feeling" was first recorded in December 1976 as the B-side of Talking Heads' debut single "Love -> Building on Fire," cut at Sundragon Studios before keyboardist Jerry Harrison joined the band. The group re-recorded it for their 1977 debut album Talking Heads: 77, where it is track 2.

superchunk|the first part.fact: "The First Part" was a single from Superchunk's 1994 album Foolish, their fourth album and first full-length released on their own Merge Records. The album was originally recorded with producer Brian Paulson, who has also worked with Wilco and Slint. The A.V. Club called the song the album's defining track.

bully|lose you (feat. soccer mommy).fact: "Lose You," featuring Soccer Mommy, was released on February 15, 2023, as Bully's first single in nearly three years. It led into the album Lucky for You, which came out on June 2, 2023, and reached the Top 20 of Billboard's Heatseekers chart.

gang of four|damaged goods.fact: "Damaged Goods" was Gang of Four's debut single, released in late 1978 on the independent Edinburgh label Fast Product. It topped the UK indie chart, became a favorite of DJ John Peel, and helped lead to a record deal with EMI. The band re-recorded it for their 1979 debut album Entertainment!

parquet courts|human performance.fact: "Human Performance" is the title track of Parquet Courts' fifth studio album, released April 8, 2016, and their first full-length for the London label Rough Trade. The album earned a 2017 Grammy nomination for Best Recording Package.

rogue wave|10:1.fact: "10:1" was released as an EP on Sub Pop on August 23, 2005, and reached No. 14 on Billboard's Hot Single Sales chart. The title track also appears on Rogue Wave's second Sub Pop album, Descended Like Vultures, which was recorded in about ten days at Supernatural Sound in Oregon City, Oregon. A 20th anniversary reissue of the album arrived in 2026.

slowdive|catch the breeze.fact: "Catch the Breeze" was the lead track on Slowdive's Holding Our Breath EP, released in June 1991 with a 7-inch single version. It was then included on their debut album Just for a Day, released on Creation Records on 2 September 1991, which reached No. 32 on the UK Albums Chart.

perez prado|patricia.fact: Perez Prado's "Patricia" (1958) was the last record to reach No. 1 on Billboard's Jockeys and Top 100 charts before they were replaced by the new Hot 100. On the Hot 100's first week, it debuted at No. 2, behind Ricky Nelson's "Poor Little Fool." Billboard ranked it the No. 5 song of 1958, and Fellini later used it in his film La Dolce Vita.

the foundations|build me up buttercup.fact: "Build Me Up Buttercup" was written by Mike d'Abo and producer Tony Macaulay, and was the first Foundations hit with Colin Young on lead vocals, after he replaced original singer Clem Curtis. It reached No. 2 in the UK and No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100 in early 1969, and was certified gold by the RIAA.

def leppard|have you ever needed someone.fact: "Have You Ever Needed Someone So Bad" was the third single from Def Leppard's 1992 album Adrenalize, following "Make Love Like a Man." It reached No. 12 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 7 on the Album Rock Tracks chart, and logged 20 weeks on the Hot 100.

donna lewis|i love you always forever.fact: Donna Lewis's "I Love You Always Forever" was the lead single from her 1996 album Now in a Minute. It spent nine weeks at No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100, held back by "Macarena," and became the first single to pass one million radio plays in the US, making it one of the most-played songs of the 1990s.

spandau ballet|true.fact: Gary Kemp wrote "True" for Spandau Ballet as a tribute to Altered Images singer Clare Grogan. The title track of the band's 1983 album was recorded at Compass Point Studios in Nassau, Bahamas, and reached No. 1 on the UK singles chart in April 1983.

cut copy|hearts on fire.fact: Cut Copy began in Melbourne in 2001 as a solo project of DJ and graphic designer Dan Whitford. "Hearts on Fire" first came out as a single in 2007, and a re-recorded version appeared on their second album, In Ghost Colours (Modular Recordings, March 2008), which debuted at No. 1 on Australia's ARIA albums chart.

harry styles|sign of the times.fact: "Sign of the Times," released 7 April 2017, was Harry Styles's debut solo single and went to No. 1 on the UK Singles Chart. It opens his self-titled debut album and was produced by Jeff Bhasker, with additional production by Alex Salibian and Tyler Johnson.

little willie john|fever.fact: Little Willie John recorded "Fever" at King Records' Cincinnati studio on 1 April 1956, and it topped Billboard's R&B chart and reached No. 24 on the pop chart. Co-writer Otis Blackwell was under contract elsewhere and was credited as "John Davenport." Peggy Lee's 1958 version, with its added lyrics and stripped-down snaps-and-bass arrangement, became the best-known take.

jessie j|domino.fact: Jessie J's "Domino," produced by Dr. Luke, reached No. 6 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 24 weeks on the chart, making it her first US top-ten single. It also became her second UK No. 1 when released there in January 2012 as the sixth single from her debut album Who You Are.

dionne farris|i know.fact: Dionne Farris first became known as a guest vocalist on Arrested Development's 1992 hit "Tennessee." Her solo debut single "I Know," from the album Wild Seed - Wild Flower, peaked at No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100, spent 10 weeks at No. 1 on the Top 40/Mainstream chart, and earned a 1996 Grammy nomination for Best Female Pop Vocal Performance.

squeeze|tempted.fact: On Squeeze's 1981 single "Tempted," written by Glenn Tilbrook and Chris Difford, the lead vocal was sung by keyboardist Paul Carrack, a choice suggested by producer Elvis Costello. It came from the album East Side Story, co-produced by Costello and Roger Bechirian, and became the band's first charting US single.

starship|we built this city.fact: "We Built This City" was written by Bernie Taupin and Martin Page, with producers Peter Wolf and Dennis Lambert reshaping it and adding a bigger chorus. The lead single from Starship's 1985 album Knee Deep in the Hoopla, it hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and was the first chart-topper for any incarnation of Jefferson Airplane/Starship.

grimes|you'll miss me when i'm not aroun.fact: This track is from Grimes's 2020 album Miss_Anthropocene. For its video, she posted the raw video files and audio stems online so fans could make their own music videos, including a green-screen clip of herself swaying with a sword.

elton john|daniel.fact: "Daniel," with lyrics by Bernie Taupin, was recorded on 10 June 1972 at the Chateau d'Herouville in France. It opens the album Don't Shoot Me I'm Only the Piano Player, which was Elton John's second straight US No. 1 album, and the single reached No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100.

the pointer sisters|yes we can can.fact: "Yes We Can Can" was written by Allen Toussaint and first recorded by Lee Dorsey in 1970. Producer David Rubinson suggested the Pointer Sisters cover it, and their 1973 version, one of the first tracks cut for their debut album, reached the top 15 on the Billboard Hot 100 and became their first gold record.

arcade fire|wake up.fact: Arcade Fire formed in Montreal in 2003, and "Wake Up" from their 2004 debut Funeral (recorded largely at the band's own Hotel2Tango studio) became a crowd favorite and encore staple. U2 later used it as their walk-on music during the 2005-06 Vertigo tour.

the everly brothers|walk right back.fact: Sonny Curtis wrote "Walk Right Back" while in Army basic training and mailed a second verse to the Everly Brothers, but they had already recorded it with the first verse repeated. That single-verse version reached No. 7 on the US Hot 100 and spent four weeks at No. 1 in the UK in 1961.

stampeders|sweet city woman.fact: "Sweet City Woman," written by Stampeders member Rich Dodson and produced by Mel Shaw, spent four weeks at No. 1 in Canada in 1971 and was RPM's No. 2 single of the year. In the US it reached No. 8 on the Billboard Hot 100.

r.e.m.|the great beyond.fact: R.E.M. wrote "The Great Beyond" for the 1999 Andy Kaufman biopic Man on the Moon. It reached No. 3 on the UK Singles Chart in January 2000, the band's highest UK chart position ever, and earned a Grammy nomination for Best Song Written for a Motion Picture, Television or Other Visual Media.

elvis presley|wear my ring around your n.fact: Elvis Presley recorded "Wear My Ring Around Your Neck," written by Bert Carroll and Russell Moody, on 1 February 1958 at Radio Recorders in Hollywood, with Scotty Moore, Bill Black and D. J. Fontana. It topped the Billboard R&B chart and reached No. 3 in the UK.

arctic monkeys|fluorescent adolescent.fact: "Fluorescent Adolescent" was the second single from Arctic Monkeys' 2007 album Favourite Worst Nightmare, released 9 July 2007, and peaked at No. 5 on the UK Singles Chart. Its music video was loosely based on John Cooper Clarke's poem "Out of Control Circus."

diana ross & the supremes|love child.fact: "Love Child" reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in the week of 30 November 1968, ending the nine-week run of The Beatles' "Hey Jude" at the top. Its writing team of R. Dean Taylor, Frank Wilson, Pam Sawyer and Deke Richards worked as Motown's "The Clan."

lcd soundsystem|call the police.fact: "Call the Police" was released at midnight in May 2017 as a double A-side with "American Dream," announced as LCD Soundsystem's comeback single. The band performed both songs on Saturday Night Live that month, their first appearance on the show, and the parent album American Dream (September 2017) reached No. 1 on the Top Rock Albums chart.

blind melon|no rain.fact: Bassist Brad Smith wrote most of "No Rain," which reached No. 20 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 1 on both the Album Rock and Modern Rock charts. Its Samuel Bayer-directed video made a star of the "Bee Girl," and the band's debut album cover shows a 1975 photo of drummer Glenn Graham's sister in a bee costume.

qt|hey qt.fact: "Hey QT" was released on 26 August 2014 via XL Recordings, written by A. G. Cook and SOPHIE of the PC Music collective. QT was a conceptual pop-star project: Hayden Dunham played the character on screen, while the vocals were sung by Harriet Pittard, who also records as Zoee.

steve perry|oh sherrie.fact: "Oh Sherrie" was the debut solo single from Journey frontman Steve Perry, released in 1984 from his album Street Talk. It reached #3 on the Billboard Hot 100 and topped the rock chart, becoming his biggest solo hit. Perry wrote it with Randy Goodrum, Craig Krampf and Bill Cuomo.

styx|mr. roboto.fact: "Mr. Roboto" was the lead single from Styx's 1983 concept album Kilroy Was Here. Dennis DeYoung wrote it after hearing the Japanese word for robot on a tour of Japan. It climbed to #3 on the Billboard Hot 100 and hit #1 in Canada.

stealers wheel|stuck in the middle with.fact: Gerry Rafferty and Joe Egan of Stealers Wheel wrote "Stuck in the Middle with You" as a playful send-up of Bob Dylan's style, and plenty of listeners still mistake it for a Dylan song. The band's debut was produced by the famed songwriting team Jerry Leiber & Mike Stoller. The 1973 single got a second life in Quentin Tarantino's 1992 film Reservoir Dogs.

pure prairie league|amie.fact: Craig Fuller's "Amie" first appeared on Pure Prairie League's 1972 album Bustin' Out and originally failed to chart. Radio airplay in 1975 revived it, and RCA re-released it as a single, reissued the album, and re-signed the band. It peaked around #27 on the Billboard Hot 100, and Fuller had already left the group by then.

bob dylan|when the ship comes in.fact: Bob Dylan wrote "When the Ship Comes In" in August 1963, reportedly after a hotel clerk balked at giving the scruffy young singer a room until Joan Baez vouched for him. Dylan and Baez performed it together at the March on Washington that August. It was released on the 1964 album The Times They Are a-Changin'.

rod stewart|(i know) i'm losing you.fact: Rod Stewart's version of the Temptations' 1966 hit appeared on his 1971 album Every Picture Tells a Story, as the follow-up single to "Maggie May." Credited to Rod Stewart with Faces, it reached #24 on the Billboard Hot 100. Stewart had performed the song earlier with the Jeff Beck Group, including a 1967 BBC radio session.

green day|when i come around.fact: "When I Come Around" from Green Day's 1994 album Dookie spent a then-record seven weeks at #1 on Billboard's Modern Rock Tracks chart in early 1995. It was never issued as a commercial U.S. single, yet it reached #6 on the Hot 100 Airplay chart. It also hit #2 on the Mainstream Rock chart.

ricky nelson|lonesome town.fact: Baker Knight wrote both sides of Ricky Nelson's 1958 single: "Lonesome Town" and its flip side "I Got a Feeling." The A-side reached #7 on the Billboard Hot 100 and the B-side reached #10, so both were Top 10 hits.

bobby \"blue\" bland|i'll take care of y.fact: Brook Benton wrote "I'll Take Care of You," and Bobby "Blue" Bland recorded it for Duke Records around 1959. Bland's version was a major R&B hit, and Teddy Reynolds' eerie organ line is a signature of the arrangement. The song has been widely covered and its original recording has been sampled in hip-hop.

john prine|summer's end.fact: "Summer's End" was the first single from John Prine's 2018 album The Tree of Forgiveness, his first collection of new songs in 13 years. Prine co-wrote it with Pat McLaughlin. The album, produced by Dave Cobb, was recorded at Nashville's historic RCA Studio A and released on Prine's own Oh Boy Records.

the jam|when you're young.fact: The Jam's "When You're Young" was released as a stand-alone single on 17 August 1979 and reached #17 on the UK Singles Chart. It was not on any of the band's albums at the time. Its B-side, "Smithers-Jones," was re-recorded in a different arrangement for the album Setting Sons.

tom petty & the heartbreakers|refugee.fact: "Refugee" was the second single from Tom Petty & the Heartbreakers' 1979 album Damn the Torpedoes, and it reached #15 on the Billboard Hot 100. The band reportedly cut it in a huge number of takes, with accounts ranging from about 50 to 100 or more, as co-producer Jimmy Iovine and the band chased the sound they wanted.

rolling stones|beast of burden.fact: "Beast of Burden" was the second single from the Rolling Stones' 1978 album Some Girls, following "Miss You," and reached #8 on the Billboard Hot 100. The album was recorded at the Pathe Marconi studios in Paris, and it was the first Stones album with Ronnie Wood fully involved. The band used no outside musicians in order to capture its live sound.

stevie wonder|superstition.fact: Stevie Wonder originally wrote "Superstition" for guitarist Jeff Beck, who had played on the Talking Book sessions, but Motown boss Berry Gordy urged Wonder to release it himself. Wonder's 1972 version went to #1 in the U.S. and is often credited as an early mainstream showcase for the clavinet. Beck's own take came out the following year with Beck, Bogert & Appice.

foo fighters|all my life.fact: "All My Life" was recorded in May 2002 for Foo Fighters' album One by One, made at Dave Grohl's 606 studio in Alexandria, Virginia. Grohl has said it began as an instrumental before he decided how to sing it. It won the Grammy for Best Hard Rock Performance at the 2003 ceremony.

t. rex|bang a gong (get it on).fact: In the U.K. this T. Rex hit is simply "Get It On" and spent four weeks at #1 in 1971. In North America it was retitled "Bang a Gong (Get It On)" to avoid confusion with a song of the same name by the band Chase. It was produced by Tony Visconti for the album Electric Warrior, and it was T. Rex's only big American hit.

4 non blondes|what's up.fact: "What's Up?" was the second single from 4 Non Blondes' 1992 album Bigger, Better, Faster, More!, and it reached the Top 20 in the U.S. while hitting #1 in several European countries. Linda Perry's song has been covered widely, including by Dolly Parton with Perry herself in 2023. Many fans misremember its title as "What's Going On."

portugal the man|feel it still.fact: "Feel It Still" from Portugal. The Man's 2017 album Woodstock took about eight months to climb to #4 on the Billboard Hot 100. Its melody is drawn from the Marvelettes' 1961 hit "Please Mr. Postman." It won the Grammy for Best Pop Duo/Group Performance in January 2018.

beyonce|irreplaceable.fact: "Irreplaceable" was the third U.S. single from Beyonce's 2006 album B'Day. It was co-written by Ne-Yo and produced by Stargate with Beyonce, and it spent ten consecutive weeks at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 from December 2006 into early 2007. It was her fourth U.S. #1.

lady gaga|born this way.fact: "Born This Way" debuted at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in February 2011 and was the 1,000th song to top the chart in its history. Its first-week sales of 448,000 downloads were the best for a female artist at that time.

bette midler|from a distance.fact: Julie Gold wrote "From a Distance" in 1985, and Nanci Griffith recorded it first, on her 1987 album Lone Star State of Mind. Bette Midler's 1990 version reached #2 on the Billboard charts, and the song won the Grammy for Song of the Year in 1991.

dj jazzy jeff & the fresh prince|summert.fact: "Summertime" was the lead single from DJ Jazzy Jeff & the Fresh Prince's 1991 album Homebase. It samples Kool & the Gang's 1974 instrumental "Summer Madness." The single reached #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and won the Grammy for Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group.

tracy chapman|fast car.fact: Tracy Chapman's 1988 "Fast Car" reached #6 on the Billboard Hot 100, and she won a Grammy for Best Female Pop Vocal Performance for it. In 2023 Luke Combs's country cover sent it back up the country charts, and the song won CMA Song of the Year, with Chapman as songwriter.

wang chung|everybody have fun tonight.fact: "Everybody Have Fun Tonight" reached #2 on the Billboard Hot 100 over the 1986 holidays and topped the Canadian chart in January 1987. It is from the album Mosaic. The band's name, Wang Chung, is Chinese for "yellow bell," the first note of the Chinese classical scale, and they first recorded as Huang Chung.

weezer|all my favorite songs.fact: "All My Favorite Songs" was the lead single from Weezer's 14th album, OK Human, released in January 2021. The album was produced by longtime collaborator Jake Sinclair and recorded with a 38-piece orchestra.

sugarloaf|green-eyed lady.fact: Sugarloaf's "Green-Eyed Lady" was the Denver band's first single, and it peaked at No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1970. The album version runs nearly 7 minutes, so Liberty issued edited single versions, including a radio edit under 3 minutes.

the everly brothers|cathy's clown.fact: "Cathy's Clown" was the Everly Brothers' first single for Warner Bros. after three years on Cadence Records. It spent five weeks at No. 1 in the US and seven weeks at No. 1 in the UK in 1960, and was added to the National Recording Registry in 2013.

robert palmer|bad case of loving you.fact: Robert Palmer's "Bad Case of Loving You" was written by Moon Martin, who first recorded it in 1978 on his album Shots From a Cold Nightmare. Palmer heard it, added it to his live set, then recorded it for his 1979 album Secrets, and his version reached No. 14 on the Billboard Hot 100.

brenton wood|the oogum boogum song.fact: Brenton Wood wrote "The Oogum Boogum Song" under his birth name, Alfred Smith. Released on Double Shot Records in April 1967, it reached No. 34 on the Billboard Hot 100, and the follow-up "Gimme Little Sign" became his biggest hit at No. 9.

tower of power|what is hip?.fact: "What Is Hip?" is on Tower of Power's 1973 self-titled album and is credited to Emilio Castillo, Stephen Kupka and drummer David Garibaldi. Garibaldi, known for his polyrhythmic style, was fooling around with a new groove while Kupka was working on lyrics. The album reached No. 15 on the Billboard album chart and went gold.

pavement|carrot rope.fact: "Carrot Rope" closes Pavement's 1999 album Terror Twilight, produced by Nigel Godrich. It was released as a single only in the UK, in May 1999. The "...and" in the album's track listing marks it as the album's last song and is not part of the title.

arcade fire|neighborhood #1 (tunnels).fact: "Neighborhood #1 (Tunnels)" opens Arcade Fire's 2004 debut album Funeral. It was recorded in Montreal at the band's Hotel2Tango studio, with the album done in analogue and produced by the band.

black sheep|the choice is yours (revisit.fact: "The Choice Is Yours" was the 1991 single from Black Sheep's debut album A Wolf in Sheep's Clothing, produced by Dres and Mista Lawnge. It samples Johnny Hammond Smith's "Big Sur Suite", and VH1 later ranked it No. 74 on its list of the 100 greatest hip-hop songs.

aaron neville|everybody plays the fool.fact: "Everybody Plays the Fool" was first a No. 3 hit for The Main Ingredient in 1972. Aaron Neville's 1991 remake, from his album Warm Your Heart, reached No. 8 on the Hot 100 and No. 1 on the adult contemporary chart.

whitesnake|is this love.fact: David Coverdale has said "Is This Love" was first written with Tina Turner in mind. Co-written with guitarist John Sykes, it was the second single from Whitesnake's 1987 self-titled album and peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100, behind George Michael's "Faith".

willie nelson|always on my mind.fact: Willie Nelson's 1982 "Always on My Mind" was far from the first recording of the song. Gwen McCrae, Brenda Lee and Elvis Presley all recorded it in 1972. Nelson's version hit No. 1 on the country chart and won Song of the Year at the 1983 Grammys for its writers, plus a Grammy for Nelson's vocal performance.

eagles|desperado.fact: "Desperado" was never released as an Eagles single, yet it became one of the band's best-loved songs. It is often cited as one of the first songs Don Henley and Glenn Frey fully wrote together, and Linda Ronstadt, whose backing band they had played in, covered it in 1973.

bobby vinton|roses are red (my love).fact: Bobby Vinton's "Roses Are Red (My Love)" was written by Paul Evans and Al Byron and recorded in New York in February 1962. It reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 for four weeks that July and is credited with launching Vinton's career at Epic Records.

billy joel|just the way you are.fact: The alto sax solo on Billy Joel's "Just the Way You Are" was played by jazz saxophonist Phil Woods. The song, from the 1977 album The Stranger and produced by Phil Ramone, won both Record of the Year and Song of the Year at the 1979 Grammys.

del shannon|runaway.fact: Del Shannon's 1961 No. 1 "Runaway" was co-written with keyboardist Max Crook, who played the instrumental break on a self-built keyboard called the Musitron. It was recorded at Bell Sound in New York in early 1961 and was later ranked No. 472 on Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Songs list.

bob seger & the silver bullet band|still.fact: "Still the Same" was the lead single from Bob Seger's 1978 album Stranger in Town and peaked at No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100. Although much of the album was cut with the Muscle Shoals Rhythm Section in Alabama, this song was one of four recorded with Seger's own Silver Bullet Band.

madonna|beautiful stranger.fact: Madonna co-wrote and co-produced "Beautiful Stranger" with William Orbit for the 1999 film Austin Powers: The Spy Who Shagged Me. It won the Grammy for Best Song Written for Visual Media and reached No. 2 on the UK singles chart.

miley cyrus|wrecking ball.fact: "Wrecking Ball" gave Miley Cyrus her first No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2013. Billboard had just begun counting YouTube views in its formula, and the song's music video helped it climb. It sold 477,000 downloads in its top week.

electric six|danger! high voltage.fact: "Danger! High Voltage" was Electric Six's debut single and the lead single from their first album, Fire (2003). It reached No. 2 on the UK Singles Chart and went on to earn a UK Silver certification.

boards of canada|music is math.fact: "Music Is Math" is the second track on Boards of Canada's 2002 album Geogaddi, released on Warp Records. Marcus Eoin and Michael Sandison recorded the album between 1999 and 2001 at their Hexagon Sun studio in Scotland's Pentland Hills.

psy|gangnam style.fact: In December 2012, Psy's "Gangnam Style" became the first YouTube video to reach one billion views, just 159 days after it was uploaded. Two years later YouTube had to upgrade its view counter from a 32-bit to a 64-bit integer because the video exceeded 2,147,483,647 views.

aerosmith|crazy.fact: The 1994 video for Aerosmith's "Crazy" was directed by Marty Callner and starred Alicia Silverstone alongside Liv Tyler, Steven Tyler's daughter. Silverstone appeared in three Aerosmith videos in a row, which helped lead to her starring role in the 1995 film Clueless. The song peaked at No. 17 on the Billboard Hot 100.

zz top|legs.fact: "Legs" from ZZ Top's 1983 album Eliminator peaked at No. 8 on the Billboard Hot 100, giving the band its first top 10 hit. Its video completed a loose trilogy with "Gimme All Your Lovin'" and "Sharp Dressed Man", and won an MTV Award for Best Group Video in 1984.

the carpenters|yesterday once more.fact: "Yesterday Once More" was written by Richard Carpenter and John Bettis and released in May 1973 from the album Now & Then. It peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100, held out of the top spot by Jim Croce's "Bad, Bad Leroy Brown", and was No. 1 on the easy listening chart. It leads into an oldies medley on the album.

b.j. thomas|raindrops keep fallin' on my.fact: Burt Bacharach and Hal David wrote "Raindrops Keep Fallin' on My Head" for the film Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid, where it won the Oscar for Best Original Song. B.J. Thomas was recovering from laryngitis when he recorded the film version, so his vocal is raspier than on the version released separately. The song hit No. 1 on January 3, 1970.

paul mccartney and wings|silly love song.fact: "Silly Love Songs" spent five non-consecutive weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1976 and was Billboard's top song of the year. That made Paul McCartney the first person to have a year-end No. 1 with two different acts, after the Beatles' "I Want to Hold Your Hand" and "Hey Jude".

blood, sweat & tears|spinning wheel.fact: David Clayton-Thomas wrote "Spinning Wheel" in 1967 while performing around Toronto's Yorkville club scene. It peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 for three weeks and topped Canada's RPM singles chart. The band's self-titled album went on to win the Grammy for Album of the Year, famously beating the Beatles' Abbey Road.

howlin' wolf|smokestack lightnin'.fact: Howlin' Wolf cut "Smokestack Lightnin'" in Chicago for Chess Records in January 1956, with Hubert Sumlin's guitar line and Willie Dixon on bass. It reached the Top Ten of Billboard's R&B chart. A 1964 British reissue put it at No. 42 on the UK pop chart, when young British bands were eager to play Wolf's music.

ike and tina turner|river deep - mountai.fact: Phil Spector's "River Deep - Mountain High" used his Wall of Sound approach, with around 21 session musicians and 21 backing vocalists, and cost a then-huge $22,000. It reached No. 3 in the UK but stalled in the US. Spector reportedly stepped away from the studio for years afterward.

pitbull|feel this moment.fact: "Feel This Moment" features Christina Aguilera and interpolates a-ha's 1985 hit "Take On Me." It's from Pitbull's 2012 album Global Warming, peaked at No. 8 on the Billboard Hot 100, and was certified quadruple platinum.

herbie hancock|rockit.fact: "Rockit" was co-written by Herbie Hancock with Bill Laswell and Michael Beinhorn, with turntablist Grand Mixer DXT's scratching as the driving lead sound. It reached No. 1 on the US dance club chart and No. 8 in the UK, won a Grammy, and its robot-filled video took home five MTV Video Music Awards.

love and rockets|so alive.fact: "So Alive" was Love and Rockets' biggest US hit, climbing to No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100 in the summer of 1989. It also spent five weeks at No. 1 on the Modern Rock Tracks chart and topped Canada's RPM singles chart for two weeks.

taylor swift|mastermind.fact: "Mastermind" is the 13th and final track on the standard edition of Midnights (2022), co-written and co-produced by Taylor Swift and Jack Antonoff. It was the first track title Swift revealed from the album, drawn from a lottery cage on her TikTok series.

steve miller band|take the money and run.fact: "Take the Money and Run" was a single from the Steve Miller Band's 1976 album Fly Like an Eagle, released in the spring of 1976. It peaked at No. 11 on the Billboard Hot 100, while the album climbed to No. 3 and went multi-platinum.

black sabbath|n.i.b..fact: "N.I.B." is the fourth track on Black Sabbath's 1970 debut album. Bassist Geezer Butler has said the title refers to drummer Bill Ward's beard, which the band thought looked like a pen nib. The working title was just "Nib," and the periods were added later for effect.

beck|the golden age.fact: "The Golden Age" opens Beck's 2002 album Sea Change, which was produced by Nigel Godrich (also known for his work with Radiohead) and recorded in Los Angeles over about two months. Beck's father, David Campbell, arranged the strings for the album.

bruce channel|hey! baby.fact: Delbert McClinton's harmonica riff made "Hey! Baby" a US No. 1 hit for three weeks. Bruce Channel and McClinton toured Britain in 1962 on a bill with the Beatles, and John Lennon's harmonica playing on "Love Me Do" is often said to have been influenced by the riff.

carly simon|you belong to me.fact: "You Belong to Me" was co-written by Carly Simon and Michael McDonald, who first recorded it with the Doobie Brothers on Livin' on the Fault Line (1977). Simon's version, the lead single from her 1978 album Boys in the Trees, reached No. 6 on the Billboard pop chart and earned a Grammy nomination.

hootie & the blowfish|only wanna be with.fact: Hootie & the Blowfish formed in 1986 at the University of South Carolina in Columbia, with Darius Rucker, Mark Bryan, Dean Felber and Jim "Soni" Sonefeld. "Only Wanna Be with You" was a single from their 1994 debut Cracked Rear View, which won the band a Grammy for Best New Group.

ok go|i wont let you down.fact: OK Go's video for "I Won't Let You Down" was shot in Japan as a single take captured by drone, with the band riding Honda UNI-CUB personal mobility devices. It featured choreography by air:man and thousands of dancers and volunteers, and was reportedly filmed in more than 50 takes.

phil collins|do you remember?.fact: "Do You Remember?" was the fourth single from Phil Collins' 1989 album ...But Seriously, co-produced with Hugh Padgham, with Stephen Bishop on backing vocals. It reached No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 1 on the US Adult Contemporary chart.

rod stewart|have i told you lately.fact: Van Morrison wrote and first recorded "Have I Told You Lately" for his 1989 album Avalon Sunset. Rod Stewart recorded it on Vagabond Heart (1991), and his live version from Unplugged...and Seated became a 1993 hit, reaching No. 5 in both the US and UK.

minnie riperton|loving you.fact: Minnie Riperton's signature song, written with her husband Richard Rudolph, is known for her high whistle-register passage and the chirping songbirds heard throughout. Stevie Wonder co-produced the Perfect Angel album, and the single reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1975, reportedly without any percussion instrument.

paul mccartney|no more lonely nights.fact: Pink Floyd's David Gilmour played the guitar solo on "No More Lonely Nights," reportedly laying it down in one take. The ballad was the main song of the 1984 film Give My Regards to Broad Street, and became a Top 10 hit in the US and a No. 2 hit in the UK.

crystals|then he kissed me.fact: "Then He Kissed Me" was written by Phil Spector, Ellie Greenwich and Jeff Barry, with Dolores "LaLa" Brooks singing lead for the Crystals. It reached No. 6 in the US and No. 2 in the UK. The Beach Boys covered it on their 1965 album Summer Days (And Summer Nights!!), and their version hit No. 4 in the UK as a 1967 single.

herman's hermits|i'm henry the viii, i a.fact: Herman's Hermits took "I'm Henry VIII, I Am" to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1965, even though it was never released as a single in the UK. It's a remake of a 1910 music hall song, and Peter Noone's spoken "Second verse, same as the first!" is part of the recording.

kool & the gang|funky stuff.fact: Kool & the Gang formed in Jersey City, New Jersey in 1964, going through names like the Jazziacs and Kool & the Flames. "Funky Stuff" came from their 1973 breakthrough album Wild and Peaceful, which also included "Jungle Boogie" and "Hollywood Swinging," all of which reached the R&B top 10.

extreme|more than words.fact: "More Than Words" is an acoustic ballad built on Nuno Bettencourt's guitar and Gary Cherone's lead vocal, from Extreme's 1990 album Pornograffitti. It hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1991, as well as No. 1 in Canada, Belgium, the Netherlands and New Zealand.

chromatics|in the city.fact: "In the City" is a nearly nine-minute centerpiece of Chromatics' 2012 album Kill for Love. The band, led by Johnny Jewel, is also known for "Tick of the Clock," which was edited down to about five minutes for the 2011 film Drive.

bobby vinton|blue velvet.fact: Bobby Vinton's "Blue Velvet" hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in the fall of 1963. It was a cover of a 1951 Tony Bennett recording, which had been only a modest hit, peaking around No. 18 on Billboard's best-selling singles chart.

the flaming lips|this here giraffe.fact: "This Here Giraffe" is from the Flaming Lips' seventh album, Clouds Taste Metallic (1995, Warner Bros.). It was issued as a UK-only single in February 1996, and its video was directed by Sofia Coppola.

patty smyth|the warrior.fact: "The Warrior" was credited to Scandal featuring Patty Smyth and written by Holly Knight and Nick Gilder, with Mike Chapman producing. It reached No. 7 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1984 and hit No. 1 on the Mainstream Rock chart.

patrice rushen|forget me nots.fact: Patrice Rushen's 1982 hit "Forget Me Nots" was famously sampled for Will Smith's 1997 single "Men in Black." Freddie Washington's bass line is central to the original, and the song earned a Grammy nomination.

bleachers|i wanna get better.fact: "I Wanna Get Better" was Bleachers' debut single, released in February 2014 and written and produced by Jack Antonoff with John Hill. It appears on the 2014 album Strange Desire, and Rolling Stone ranked it 18th among its 50 best songs of 2014.

feist|1234.fact: Feist's "1234" got a huge boost in 2007 when it was featured in an Apple iPod nano commercial. It went on to peak at No. 8 on the Billboard Hot 100, her biggest US hit.

elvis presley|suspicious minds.fact: Elvis recorded "Suspicious Minds" at American Sound Studio in Memphis in early 1969. Written by Mark James, whose own version had flopped, it became Presley's final No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in November 1969.

the folk implosion|natural one.fact: "Natural One" was written by Lou Barlow and John Davis of The Folk Implosion with producer Wally Gagel. It opens the Kids soundtrack and reached No. 29 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 4 on the Modern Rock chart in 1995-96.

nicki minaj|super bass.fact: "Super Bass" peaked at No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100 and was produced by Kane Beatz and JMIKE, with Ester Dean among the writers. It was a hit from the deluxe edition of Nicki Minaj's debut album Pink Friday.

bon iver|flume.fact: "Flume" is from Bon Iver's debut, For Emma, Forever Ago, which Justin Vernon recorded during a winter at his family's remote cabin in northern Wisconsin. Jagjaguwar reissued the album in February 2008, and 4AD released it in the UK and Europe that May.

karmin|broken hearted.fact: Karmin's "Brokenhearted" was the lead single from their 2012 EP Hello and peaked at No. 16 on the Billboard Hot 100. Amy Heidemann and Nick Noonan met at Berklee College of Music and first gained attention with covers posted on YouTube.

a tribe called quest|buggin' out.fact: "Buggin' Out" from The Low End Theory (1991) was the album's first showcase of Phife Dawg and Q-Tip trading verses. Phife's opening verse is widely regarded as a career highlight.
