madonna|cherish.fact: "Cherish" was the third single from Madonna's 1989 album Like a Prayer, written and produced with Patrick Leonard. It reached No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100, and its black-and-white video was directed by Herb Ritts at Paradise Cove in Malibu.

pete townshend|let my love open the door.fact: "Let My Love Open the Door" came out in June 1980 from Pete Townshend's solo album Empty Glass. It reached No. 9 on the Billboard Hot 100, his only solo top 10 hit there.

willie nelson|blue eyes crying in the ra.fact: Fred Rose's song was recorded by Roy Acuff in 1947 before Willie Nelson's version, from the concept album Red Headed Stranger, gave him his first country No. 1 in 1975. It won a Grammy in 1976 and was added to the National Recording Registry in 2010.

diana ross & the supremes|where did our.fact: "Where Did Our Love Go" was the Supremes' first Billboard Hot 100 No. 1, in August 1964, and began a run of five straight chart-toppers. Written by Holland-Dozier-Holland, it was reportedly turned down by the Marvelettes first.

ringo starr|it don't come easy.fact: "It Don't Come Easy" was produced by George Harrison, who also helped with the song, and features Stephen Stills on piano. Released in April 1971, it reached No. 4 on both the US and UK charts.

archie bell and the drells|tighten up.fact: "Tighten Up," written by Archie Bell and Billy Butler, was a Houston hit before Atlantic Records picked it up for distribution in April 1968. By summer it topped both the Billboard R&B and pop charts.

the roches|hammond song.fact: "Hammond Song" was written by Maggie Roche and appears on The Roches' 1979 self-titled debut album. The album was produced by Robert Fripp of King Crimson, who also played electric guitar on it.

andy shauf|i'm not falling asleep.fact: Andy Shauf made his album The Bearer of Bad News at home, playing nearly every instrument himself. He wrote close to 100 songs for it and trimmed them down to 11, and it was first released independently in 2012 before being reissued in 2015.

beach fossils|down the line.fact: "Down the Line" was released as a single on May 1, 2017, ahead of Beach Fossils' third album Somersault. Dustin Payseur co-produced the record with Jonathan Rado of Foxygen, and reviewers pointed to the song's sliding guitars and key-changing chorus.

beach house|chariot.fact: "Chariot" was recorded during the sessions for Beach House's Depression Cherry and Thank Your Lucky Stars albums but sat unreleased for years. It finally came out in May 2017 as the lead single from the compilation B-Sides and Rarities, with a video the band directed themselves.

bon iver|things behind things behind thi.fact: "Things Behind Things Behind Things" opens Bon Iver's 2024 EP SABLE, the project's first new release in more than five years. It was recorded at Justin Vernon's April Base studio in Wisconsin and produced by Vernon and Jim-E Stack.

golden smog|until you came along.fact: Golden Smog is an all-star side project whose 1995 debut Down by the Old Mainstream featured members of The Jayhawks (Gary Louris, Marc Perlman) and Soul Asylum, plus Wilco's Jeff Tweedy. The musicians originally recorded under pseudonyms because of their other record contracts, and Louris wrote many of the album's best-loved songs.

helado negro|best for you and me.fact: "Best For You and Me" was the lead single from Helado Negro's eighth album Phasor, released in February 2024 on 4AD. Stereogum described it as a soft, lilting track with heavily processed vocals and a samba-flavored rhythm.

kevin morby|1234.fact: "1234" is a 1:45 burst of doo-wop-flavored punk on Kevin Morby's 2017 album City Music, and it is a tribute to the Ramones. Morby has said the Ramones were to punk what Woody Guthrie was to folk music.

alex g|bug.fact: "Bug" was the lead single from Alex G's seventh album Beach Music, released in October 2015 on Domino. Rolling Stone noted the song's pitch-shifted vocals, and the video was directed by Micah Van Hove in Ojai, California.

bully|kills to be resistant.fact: "Kills to Be Resistant" is track two on Bully's second album Losing (2017). Frontwoman Alicia Bognanno produced the album herself and recorded it at Electrical Audio in Chicago, the studio founded by engineer Steve Albini.

glass beach|the cia.fact: "the CIA" was the lead single from Glass Beach's second album plastic death, released in January 2024 on Run for Cover Records. The band's own drummer, William White, directed the music video.

kurt vile|kv crimes.fact: "KV Crimes" is the second track on Kurt Vile's 2013 album Waking on a Pretty Daze. Vile, from Philadelphia, recorded the album with his band The Violators.

meat puppets|plateau.fact: "Plateau" first appeared on the Meat Puppets' 1984 album Meat Puppets II on SST Records. Nirvana covered it on their 1993 MTV Unplugged performance, with Meat Puppets brothers Curt and Cris Kirkwood joining them onstage.

my morning jacket|touch me i'm going to.fact: This 8-minute-plus track comes from My Morning Jacket's fifth album Evil Urges (2008), which earned a Grammy nomination for Best Alternative Music Album. It follows "Touch Me I'm Going to Scream Pt. 1" on the record.

nick cave & the bad seeds|o children.fact: "O Children" closes the 2004 double album Abattoir Blues / The Lyre of Orpheus, which the Bad Seeds finished in just twelve days. It reached a huge new audience in 2010 when it played during the wordless dance scene in Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows Part 1.

pavement|cut your hair.fact: "Cut Your Hair" was the single from Pavement's 1994 album Crooked Rain, Crooked Rain, and it peaked at number 10 on Billboard's Alternative Songs chart. Its video got MTV airplay and was even lampooned on Beavis and Butt-head, though the band admitted they didn't enjoy making videos.

phosphorescent|song for zula.fact: "Song for Zula" was the lead single from Phosphorescent's 2013 album Muchacho. Matthew Houck wrote most of the album during a stay at a beach hut in Mexico, then returned to New York to record it in his own studio.

radiohead|karma police.fact: The title "Karma Police" came from a running joke on tour that "the karma police will catch up with him sooner or later." The buzzing sound in the song reportedly came from an over-worked fridge, and Jonathan Glazer directed the video, which put Thom Yorke in the back of a 1976 Chrysler New Yorker.

radiohead|lift.fact: Radiohead first recorded "Lift" in 1996 and planned it as the first single from OK Computer, but dropped it, with Ed O'Brien saying the band worried it would be too commercial. A studio version was finally officially released in 2017 on the OKNOTOK reissue.

soccer mommy|cool.fact: "Cool" is from Soccer Mommy's 2018 debut album Clean, written and recorded by Sophie Allison. One review singled out its droning opening guitar riff and its de-tuned ending that leaves the song unresolved.

st. vincent|cheerleader.fact: "Cheerleader" was the third single from St. Vincent's 2011 album Strange Mercy. Its video, directed by Hiro Murai, shows Annie Clark as a giant museum exhibit and took inspiration from Ron Mueck's oversized sculptures.

the decemberists|severed.fact: "Severed" is a synth-driven track from The Decemberists' 2018 album I'll Be Your Girl, made with producer John Congleton as a way to push the band out of its comfort zone. It reached number one on Billboard's Adult Alternative Songs chart.

the germs|forming.fact: "Forming" was the debut single from the Germs in 1977 and is generally regarded as the first punk single to come out of Los Angeles. It was reportedly recorded with just two microphones, and an alternate take with drummer D. J. Bonebrake wasn't officially released until 1993.

the jam|that's entertainment.fact: "That's Entertainment" was never released as a UK single during The Jam's lifetime, yet it still charted as an import, peaking at number 21. Paul Weller reportedly wrote it in about fifteen minutes, and it appears on the 1980 album Sound Affects.

the national|terrible love.fact: "Terrible Love" opens The National's 2010 album High Violet, which was largely made in a studio the band built in the two-car garage behind guitarist Aaron Dessner's Brooklyn home. Further recording and mixing happened at Tarquin Studios in Connecticut with producer Peter Katis.

the strokes|alone, together.fact: "Alone, Together" is the sixth track on The Strokes' 2001 debut album Is This It, released on RCA Records. Guitarists Nick Valensi and Albert Hammond Jr. share the song's interlocking guitar work.

tom waits|rain dogs.fact: The title Rain Dogs, from Tom Waits's 1985 album, comes from a phrase he coined for dogs that lose their way when storms wash away the scents they navigate by. The album, on Island Records, features guitarists Keith Richards and Marc Ribot.

toro y moi|cake.fact: "Cake" is a track on Toro y Moi's 2013 album Anything in Return, released on Carpark Records. Paste Magazine called it the most boisterous song on the record, built around propulsive chords.

turnstile|t.l.c. (turnstile love connect.fact: "T.L.C. (Turnstile Love Connection)" is track 13 on Turnstile's 2021 album Glow On, which was produced by Mike Elizondo with Brendan Yates co-producing. The song first appeared on the band's Turnstile Love Connection EP and companion short film, and the band performed it on Late Night with Seth Meyers.

wild nothing|partners in motion.fact: "Partners in Motion" is the third track on Wild Nothing's 2018 album Indigo and was its second single. Jack Tatum has said the song was inspired by helping friends assemble a dollhouse for their daughter, and its 1980s-style sound features a saxophone.

lucy dacus|my mother & i.fact: "My Mother & I" was released around Mother's Day 2019 as the second entry in Lucy Dacus's holiday singles series, after her Valentine's Day cover of "La Vie En Rose." Dacus and her mother both have birthdays in Taurus season, which inspired the song's Taurean theme.

samia|fit n full.fact: "Fit N Full" is track two on Samia's 2020 debut album The Baby and was released as a single ahead of it, with a video directed by Martin MacPherson. Samia has said she likes that the words "fit" and "full" feel mutually exclusive.

shirley & lee|let the good times roll.fact: "Let the Good Times Roll" was written by Shirley Goodman and Leonard Lee and recorded in New Orleans in 1956 for Aladdin Records. It reached No. 1 on the R&B chart and peaked at No. 20 on the pop chart.

camera obscura|lloyd, i'm ready to be he.fact: "Lloyd, I'm Ready to Be Heartbroken" was the lead single from Camera Obscura's 2006 album Let's Get Out of This Country. The Scottish band wrote it as an answer song to Lloyd Cole and the Commotions' 1984 track "Are You Ready to Be Heartbroken?"

gary lewis & the playboys|everybody love.fact: "Everybody Loves a Clown" was released in August 1965 on Liberty Records and reached No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100. It was co-written by Gary Lewis, Leon Russell and producer Snuff Garrett, and became the title track of the band's November 1965 album.

kim carnes|bette davis eyes.fact: "Bette Davis Eyes" was written by Donna Weiss and Jackie DeShannon, and DeShannon recorded it in 1974. Kim Carnes' 1981 version spent nine weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and won the Grammy for Record of the Year.

malcolm todd|roommates.fact: "Roommates" was released in June 2023 as the second single from Malcolm Todd's mixtape Sweet Boy. Todd co-wrote and co-produced it with Charlie Ziman, and it has since been certified Gold by the RIAA.

roberta flack|killing me softly with his.fact: "Killing Me Softly with His Song" was written by Norman Gimbel and Charles Fox and first recorded by Lori Lieberman in 1972. Roberta Flack's 1973 version topped the Billboard Hot 100 and won the Grammy for Record of the Year, with Gimbel and Fox winning Song of the Year.

paul simon|mother and child reunion.fact: Paul Simon recorded the backing track for "Mother and Child Reunion" in Kingston, Jamaica, with Jimmy Cliff's studio musicians, making it an early reggae-flavored hit by a non-Jamaican artist. It was the lead single from his 1972 self-titled album and reached No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100.

bobby lewis|tossin' and turnin'.fact: "Tossin' and Turnin'" by Bobby Lewis, released on the Beltone label, spent seven weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in the summer of 1961. Billboard ranked it the top single of that year.

rod stewart|maggie may.fact: "Maggie May" was released in 1971 as the B-side of Rod Stewart's cover of Tim Hardin's "Reason to Believe." Radio DJs began playing the flip side instead, and it went to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100. Stewart co-wrote it with guitarist Martin Quittenton.

elvis presley|hound dog.fact: "Hound Dog" was written by Jerry Leiber and Mike Stoller and first recorded by Big Mama Thornton, whose version spent seven weeks at No. 1 on the R&B chart. Elvis Presley's 1956 version spent 11 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard pop chart, a record that stood for 36 years.

bee gees|to love somebody.fact: The Bee Gees recorded "To Love Somebody" at IBC Studios in London in April 1967 and released it as a single that June. Barry and Robin Gibb wrote it in a soul style, and it was first offered to Otis Redding, though Barry later said it was really written for their manager Robert Stigwood.

thom yorke|dawn chorus.fact: "Dawn Chorus" is on Thom Yorke's third solo album, Anima, released in June 2019 on XL Recordings and produced by Nigel Godrich. Yorke had named it back in 2009 as his favourite song he had written for Radiohead, but it went unreleased until Anima.

yo la tengo|speeding motorcycle.fact: "Speeding Motorcycle" was written by Austin singer-songwriter Daniel Johnston, and Yo La Tengo recorded it for their 1990 album Fakebook. They later recorded it with Johnston himself, who sang his part over the phone from West Virginia while the band played in the studio at WFMU.

aerosmith|angel.fact: "Angel" was written by Steven Tyler and Desmond Child and released in 1988 as the third single from Aerosmith's 1987 album Permanent Vacation. It peaked at No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100, the band's highest-charting single at the time.

cyndi lauper|true colors.fact: "True Colors" was written by Billy Steinberg and Tom Kelly, who first offered it to Anne Murray before it went to Cyndi Lauper. Lauper's version reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 on October 25, 1986.

kassi valazza|weight of the wheel.fact: "Weight of the Wheel" was the first single from Kassi Valazza's 2025 album From Newman Street, released on May 2 via Loose Music. The album was made with her six-piece touring band, who are credited as co-producers and co-arrangers, and the song features Erik Clampitt's pedal steel.

stevie wonder|i wish.fact: "I Wish" was released as a single from Stevie Wonder's 1976 album Songs in the Key of Life in November 1976. It reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and won the Grammy for Best R&B Vocal Performance, Male.

death cab for cutie|the sound of settlin.fact: "The Sound of Settling" was the second single from Death Cab for Cutie's album Transatlanticism. Ben Gibbard wrote it and Chris Walla produced it. It reached No. 84 on the UK Singles Chart and was featured on the TV show The O.C.

b.b. king|the thrill is gone.fact: "The Thrill Is Gone" was first recorded by Roy Hawkins in 1951, and B.B. King recorded his version in June 1969 for the album Completely Well. Producer Bill Szymczyk suggested adding strings. The single reached No. 3 on the R&B chart and No. 15 on the Hot 100, and won King a Grammy.

raspberries|go all the way.fact: "Go All the Way" was written by Eric Carmen and released on Capitol in July 1972 as the Raspberries' debut single. It peaked at No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100 and sold over a million copies, earning the band its only Gold record.

archie bleyer|hernando's hideaway.fact: "Hernando's Hideaway" is a tango from the 1954 Broadway musical The Pajama Game, written by Richard Adler and Jerry Ross. Archie Bleyer's recording on his own Cadence Records was a top-five US hit in 1954.

crystals|da doo ron ron.fact: "Da Doo Ron Ron" was written by Jeff Barry and Ellie Greenwich with Phil Spector, who produced the Crystals' recording at Gold Star Studios in Los Angeles. La La Brooks is the lead singer on the released single, backed by the Wrecking Crew session musicians.

duran duran|hungry like the wolf.fact: Duran Duran wrote and recorded "Hungry Like the Wolf" in a single Saturday in the spring of 1982 at EMI's London studios. Its Russell Mulcahy-directed video, filmed in Sri Lanka, won the Grammy for Best Short Form Music Video in 1984, the first video to win that award.

boyz ii men|end of the road.fact: "End of the Road" was written and produced by Babyface and L.A. Reid for the Boomerang soundtrack in 1992. It spent 13 consecutive weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and was the year's top-ranked single, and it won two Grammys in 1993.

elton john|tiny dancer.fact: "Tiny Dancer" opens Elton John's 1971 album Madman Across the Water and was recorded at Trident Studios in London with producer Gus Dudgeon. It only reached No. 41 on the US Hot 100 as a 1972 single, but the 2000 film Almost Famous helped make it one of his best-known songs.

audioslave|like a stone.fact: "Like a Stone" was the second single from Audioslave's 2003 debut album, produced by Rick Rubin and the band. It topped both the US Mainstream Rock and Modern Rock charts and peaked at No. 31 on the Hot 100, the band's biggest US hit.

flo rida|low feat. t-pain.fact: "Low" was the lead single from Flo Rida's debut album Mail on Sunday and appeared on the Step Up 2: The Streets soundtrack. It spent ten weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and became the first song to sell four million digital copies in the US.

brandy and monica|the boy is mine.fact: "The Boy Is Mine" was released in May 1998 as the lead single from both Brandy's Never Say Never and Monica's The Boy Is Mine, with Rodney "Darkchild" Jerkins among its writers and producers. It spent 13 consecutive weeks at No. 1 on the Hot 100, the first chart-topper for both singers, and won a Grammy.

mariah carey|hero.fact: Mariah Carey and Walter Afanasieff wrote "Hero" for a 1992 film soundtrack, with Gloria Estefan in mind to sing it, but Carey kept it for herself. It became the second single from her 1993 album Music Box and spent four weeks at No. 1 on the Hot 100.

waylon jennings & willie nelson|mammas d.fact: Ed and Patsy Bruce wrote this song, and Ed Bruce first recorded it in 1975. Waylon Jennings and Willie Nelson's version, from their 1978 album Waylon & Willie, went to No. 1 on the country chart and won the 1979 Grammy for Best Country Performance by a Duo or Group.

drifters with ben e. king|save the last.fact: Doc Pomus and Mort Shuman wrote "Save the Last Dance for Me," and the Drifters recorded it in 1960 with Ben E. King on lead, produced by Leiber & Stoller. It was first released as the B-side of "Nobody But Me" before reaching No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.

eagles|take it to the limit.fact: "Take It to the Limit" was written by Randy Meisner, Don Henley and Glenn Frey, and it is the only Eagles A-side with Meisner on lead vocals. Released in 1975 as the third single from One of These Nights, it reached No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100.

audioslave|show me how to live.fact: "Show Me How to Live" was the third single from Audioslave's 2003 debut album, produced by Rick Rubin, and reached No. 2 on the Mainstream Rock chart. Its video mixes clips from the 1971 film Vanishing Point with the band performing in the Nevada desert.

the fixx|one things leads to another.fact: "One Thing Leads to Another" is the second of three singles from The Fixx's 1983 album Reach the Beach, produced by Rupert Hine. It reached No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 2 on the Mainstream Rock chart, and hit No. 1 in Canada.

amerie|1 thing.fact: "1 Thing" is from Amerie's 2005 album Touch and was produced by Rich Harrison, built on a sample of the Meters' 1970 recording "Oh, Calcutta!" It topped the US R&B/Hip-Hop chart, reached No. 8 on the Hot 100 and No. 4 in the UK, and earned a Grammy nomination.

fleetwood mac|say you love me.fact: Christine McVie wrote "Say You Love Me" for Fleetwood Mac's self-titled 1975 album, and it was the first track the band rehearsed for it. Released as a single in 1976, it reached No. 11 on the Billboard Hot 100.

the beach boys|cabin essence.fact: Brian Wilson and Van Dyke Parks wrote "Cabinessence" for the unfinished Smile album, and Wilson called it a "rock and roll waltz." Recording ran from 1966 to 1968, and it closed the Beach Boys' 1969 album 20/20. Wilson remade it for Brian Wilson Presents Smile in 2004.

john cougar mellencamp|lonely ol' night.fact: "Lonely Ol' Night" was the lead single from John Cougar Mellencamp's album Scarecrow, recorded in April 1985 at Belmont Mall in Belmont, Indiana. It reached No. 6 on the Hot 100 and spent five weeks at No. 1 on the Top Rock Tracks chart.

soundgarden|outshined.fact: "Outshined" is the second single from Soundgarden's 1991 album Badmotorfinger. It is played in drop D tuning with verses in 7/4 time, which guitarist Kim Thayil called "a total accident." Its video, directed by Matt Mahurin, shows the band performing in a steel mill.

journey|faithfully.fact: "Faithfully" was written by Journey keyboardist Jonathan Cain and released in April 1983 as the second single from the album Frontiers. Produced by Kevin Elson and Mike Stone, it reached number 12 on the Billboard Hot 100.

kraftwerk|numbers.fact: "Numbers" appears on Kraftwerk's 1981 album Computer World, which was recorded between 1979 and 1981 at the band's Kling Klang studio in Dusseldorf. Produced by Ralf Hutter and Florian Schneider, the album was released in both German- and English-language editions.

chicago|beginnings.fact: "Beginnings" was written by Robert Lamm and recorded in January 1969 for Chicago's debut album, Chicago Transit Authority. It missed the Billboard chart as a 1969 single, but when it was re-released in 1971 backed with "Colour My World," it reached number 7 on the Hot 100 and number 1 on the Easy Listening chart.

dee clark|raindrops.fact: Dee Clark wrote and recorded "Raindrops" in a three-hour session at Universal Recording in Chicago, with Bruce Swedien engineering. Released on Vee-Jay in 1961, it peaked at number 2 on the Billboard Hot 100, held out of the top spot by Gary U.S. Bonds' "Quarter to Three."

elvis presley|moody blue.fact: "Moody Blue" was written by Mark James, who first recorded it himself in 1975. Elvis Presley recorded it in February 1976 in the Jungle Room at Graceland, and it hit number 1 on the Billboard country chart in 1977, his last country number 1 in his lifetime.

bee gees|massachusetts.fact: The Bee Gees recorded "Massachusetts" in August 1967 at IBC Studios in London, with Robin Gibb on lead vocals. It was their first of five UK number 1s, topped the charts in 12 other countries, and sold over five million copies worldwide.

olivia newton-john|if you love me (let m.fact: "If You Love Me (Let Me Know)" was written by John Rostill and produced by John Farrar, and released in 1974. It reached number 5 on the Billboard Hot 100, number 1 on the Cashbox country chart, and was nominated for the CMA Single of the Year award.

the flamingos|i only have eyes for you.fact: "I Only Have Eyes for You" was written by Harry Warren and Al Dubin for the 1934 film Dames. The Flamingos' doo-wop version, recorded at Bell Sound Studios in New York and produced by George Goldner, reached number 11 on the Hot 100 in 1959.

four tops|baby i need your loving.fact: "Baby I Need Your Loving" was written by Holland-Dozier-Holland and recorded at Motown's Hitsville U.S.A. in July 1964. It was the Four Tops' first Motown single and first million-seller, and Johnny Rivers' 1967 cover actually climbed higher, to number 3 on the Hot 100.

deee-lite|groove is in the heart.fact: "Groove Is in the Heart" was Deee-Lite's debut single and lead single from World Clique (1990), built on samples from Herbie Hancock and Vernon Burch. It features Q-Tip, Bootsy Collins, Maceo Parker and Fred Wesley, and reached number 4 on the Billboard Hot 100 and number 2 in the UK.

madonna|frozen.fact: "Frozen" was the lead single from Madonna's 1998 album Ray of Light, written by Madonna and Patrick Leonard and produced with William Orbit. It debuted at number 1 in the UK, peaked at number 2 in the US, and its video was directed by Chris Cunningham.

peter gabriel|big time.fact: "Big Time" is from Peter Gabriel's 1986 album So and reached number 8 on the Billboard Hot 100. Its stop-motion video won three 1987 Billboard Video Music Awards, and the track features Stewart Copeland on drums and Tony Levin on bass.

pet shop boys|what have i done to deserv.fact: This duet with Dusty Springfield, from Pet Shop Boys' 1987 album Actually, was recorded in London in December 1986 and produced by Stephen Hague. It reached number 2 in both the UK and US and revived Springfield's career, leading the duo to write songs for her 1990 album Reputation.

elton john|this train don't stop there a.fact: "This Train Don't Stop There Anymore" was the second single from Elton John's 2001 album Songs from the West Coast, produced by Patrick Leonard. Its David LaChapelle-directed video features Justin Timberlake as a younger Elton John.

styx|lorelei.fact: "Lorelei" is from Styx's 1975 album Equinox and was written by Dennis DeYoung and James Young. Released as a single in 1976, it reached number 27 on the Billboard Hot 100 and number 6 on Canada's RPM chart.

cece peniston|finally.fact: "Finally" was CeCe Peniston's debut single, released by A&M in 1991 ahead of her 1992 album of the same name. It topped the US dance chart, reached number 5 on the Hot 100, and peaked at number 2 in the UK after a 1992 re-release.

alexandra stan|mr. saxobeat.fact: "Mr. Saxobeat" was released in 2010 as the second single from Romanian singer Alexandra Stan's debut album Saxobeats. It topped the charts in Romania, Germany and several other countries, reached number 3 in the UK, and peaked at number 21 on the US Hot 100.

daft punk|get lucky feat. pharrell willi.fact: "Get Lucky" was the lead single from Daft Punk's 2013 album Random Access Memories, with vocals by Pharrell Williams and guitar by Nile Rodgers. It reached number 1 in the UK, France and Germany, number 2 in the US, and won Record of the Year at the 2014 Grammys.

the police|don't stand so close to me.fact: "Don't Stand So Close to Me" was the lead single from the Police's 1980 album Zenyatta Mondatta, spending four weeks at number 1 in the UK. It won the 1982 Grammy for Best Rock Performance by a Duo or Group, and the band re-recorded it in 1986 for the compilation Every Breath You Take: The Singles.

pretenders|back on the chain gang.fact: "Back on the Chain Gang" was written by Chrissie Hynde, produced by Chris Thomas, and recorded in July 1982 at AIR Studios in London. It first appeared on The King of Comedy soundtrack, then on Learning to Crawl, and reached number 5 on the Billboard Hot 100.

the four seasons|c'mon marianne.fact: "C'mon Marianne" was written by L. Russell Brown and Raymond Bloodworth and produced by Bob Crewe. Released in 1967, it reached number 9 on the Billboard Hot 100 and was the last Four Seasons single to reach the top ten in the 1960s.

the_slits|typical girls.fact: "Typical Girls" is from the Slits' 1979 debut album Cut, which was produced by Dennis Bovell and recorded at Ridge Farm Studios in Rusper, England. The album blended punk and reggae and peaked at number 30 on the UK album chart.

diana ross & the supremes|come see about.fact: "Come See About Me" was written by Holland-Dozier-Holland and reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100 twice, in December 1964 and January 1965. It was the Supremes' third consecutive chart-topper, and Shakin' Stevens took a cover to number 24 in the UK in 1987.

wings|let 'em in.fact: "Let 'Em In" was recorded at Abbey Road Studios on 4 February 1976 for the album Wings at the Speed of Sound. It reached number 2 in the UK and number 3 in the US, and it opens with the sound of a Westminster-chime doorbell.

neutral milk hotel|two-headed boy.fact: "Two-Headed Boy" appears on Neutral Milk Hotel's 1998 album In the Aeroplane Over the Sea. Robert Schneider produced the album, which was recorded from July to September 1997 at Pet Sounds Studio in Denver, Colorado, and released on Merge Records on February 10, 1998.

a tribe called quest|dis generation.fact: "Dis Generation" is track 5 on A Tribe Called Quest's final album, We Got It from Here... Thank You 4 Your Service, and was its second single, released February 10, 2017. The album debuted at number one on the Billboard 200, and the song samples Musical Youth's "Pass the Dutchie."

the avalanches|since i left you.fact: "Since I Left You" was the third single from the Avalanches' 2001 debut album of the same name, and its chorus is built on a sample of the Main Attraction's 1968 song "Everyday." It peaked at number 16 on the UK Singles Chart, and its video won Best Video at the 2001 MTV Europe Music Awards.

a tribe called quest|the space program.fact: "The Space Program" opens A Tribe Called Quest's final album, We Got It from Here... Thank You 4 Your Service, released November 11, 2016, 18 years after their previous album. The album, produced by Q-Tip with Blair Wells as co-producer, debuted at number one on the Billboard 200.

311|down.fact: "Down" is the first track on 311's self-titled 1995 album and was released as a single on July 9, 1996. Produced by Ron Saint Germain, it became the band's first number-one single on Billboard's Modern Rock Tracks chart.

destiny's child|say my name.fact: "Say My Name" is from Destiny's Child's 1999 album The Writing's on the Wall and was produced by Rodney Jerkins. It became the group's second US number-one single and won two Grammy Awards in 2001, for Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals and Best R&B Song.

rick springfield|i've done everything fo.fact: "I've Done Everything for You" was written by Sammy Hagar, who released it in 1978. Rick Springfield's 1981 version, from the album Working Class Dog, was first unsuccessful, but after "Jessie's Girl" became a hit it was re-released and peaked at number eight on the Billboard Hot 100.

turnstile|holiday.fact: "HOLIDAY" is track 5 on Turnstile's 2021 album Glow On and was the fifth and final single from it, released in 2022. It was nominated for a Grammy at the 65th Grammy Awards.

joni mitchell|the hissing of summer lawn.fact: The Hissing of Summer Lawns was released by Asylum Records on November 17, 1975, and recorded at A&M Studios in Hollywood. It reached number 4 on the Billboard 200 and remains Joni Mitchell's last top-10 album.

the everly brothers|when will i be loved.fact: Phil Everly wrote "When Will I Be Loved," which the Everly Brothers released in May 1960 and which reached number 8 on the Billboard Hot 100. Linda Ronstadt's 1975 cover did even better in the US, peaking at number 2 and topping the country chart.

pink floyd|have a cigar.fact: "Have a Cigar" is the third track on Pink Floyd's 1975 album Wish You Were Here, recorded at Abbey Road Studios between March and July 1975. English folk-rock singer Roy Harper sang lead, making it one of only three Pink Floyd recordings with a guest lead vocalist.

count five|psychotic reaction.fact: "Psychotic Reaction" was the debut single by the California garage rock band Count Five, released in June 1966. It peaked at number 5 on the Billboard Hot 100, and its "rave-up" section is often compared to the Yardbirds' style.

grateful dead|eyes of the world.fact: "Eyes of the World" was the second single from the Grateful Dead's 1973 album Wake of the Flood, issued in January 1974 on the band's own label with "Weather Report Part I" on the B-side. Jerry Garcia composed the music and Robert Hunter wrote the lyrics, and it became a fan favorite and live staple.

lloyd price|lawdy miss clawdy.fact: Lloyd Price recorded "Lawdy Miss Clawdy" in New Orleans on March 13, 1952, in a session produced by Dave Bartholomew with Fats Domino on piano. It spent seven weeks at number one on Billboard's R&B chart, and Elvis Presley recorded his own version four years later.

fray|over my head (cable car).fact: "Over My Head (Cable Car)" was released on October 7, 2005, as the lead single from the Fray's debut album How to Save a Life. It peaked at number 8 on the Billboard Hot 100 and number 2 on the Adult Pop Airplay chart.

rolling stones|she's so cold.fact: "She's So Cold" was the second single from the Rolling Stones' 1980 album Emotional Rescue. It was recorded in October 1979, produced by the Glimmer Twins (Jagger and Richards), and reached number 26 on the US Billboard Hot 100.

tina turner|private dancer.fact: The title track of Tina Turner's 1984 album Private Dancer was written by Mark Knopfler, produced by John Carter, and features a guitar solo by Jeff Beck. The album version runs 7:11, while the album itself peaked at number three on the Billboard 200.

wreckless eric|whole wide world.fact: "Whole Wide World" was released on Stiff Records in August 1977, produced by Nick Lowe, who also played bass and guitar. It has been covered by the Monkees, the Proclaimers, and Cage the Elephant, among others.

william devaughn|be thankful for what yo.fact: William DeVaughn recorded "Be Thankful for What You Got" in 1972 at Sigma Sound Studios in Philadelphia with members of MFSB. The 1974 single sold nearly two million copies, hit number one on the R&B chart and number 4 on the Hot 100, and was later covered by Massive Attack on their 1991 debut album Blue Lines.

beck|think i'm in love.fact: "Think I'm in Love" is track 2 on Beck's 2006 album The Information, produced by Nigel Godrich, and was the album's second and final US single. The album came with a blank sleeve and sticker sheets so fans could make their own cover art, and it reached number 7 on the Billboard 200.

buffalo springfield|sit down i think i l.fact: Stephen Stills wrote "Sit Down I Think I Love You" in 1966, and Buffalo Springfield recorded it for their debut album. The Mojo Men's 1967 cover, arranged by Van Dyke Parks, was their biggest US hit, peaking at number 36 on the Hot 100.

toto|hold the line.fact: "Hold the Line" was Toto's first single, the lead release from their 1978 self-titled debut album on Columbia. David Paich wrote it and played piano, and Steve Lukather's guitar solo was recorded in one take except for the ending, which he multitracked for harmonies. It reached No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100.

beck|mixed bizness.fact: "Mixed Bizness" was the second single from Beck's 1999 album Midnite Vultures, released in March 2000 on Geffen. Beck produced it with Tony Hoffer, and it peaked at No. 34 on the UK Singles Chart and No. 36 on the US Modern Rock chart.

black pumas|colors.fact: "Colors" was the third single from Black Pumas' self-titled 2019 debut album. Eric Burton wrote it and Adrian Quesada produced it, and the video was filmed in the Bronx. It earned Grammy nominations for Record of the Year and Best American Roots Performance in 2021.

dave matthews band|the space between.fact: "The Space Between" is from Dave Matthews Band's 2001 album Everyday and was released as a single in April 2001. Dave Matthews co-wrote it with producer Glen Ballard, and it reached No. 22 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 1 on Adult Alternative Airplay.

the decemberists|los angeles, i'm yours.fact: "Los Angeles, I'm Yours" is from The Decemberists' second album, Her Majesty the Decemberists, released September 9, 2003 on Kill Rock Stars. The album was recorded in February and March 2003 and produced by the band with Larry Crane and Adam Selzer.

brandi carlile|the joke.fact: "The Joke" was the lead single from Brandi Carlile's sixth album, By the Way, I Forgive You (2017), produced by Dave Cobb and Shooter Jennings. It was nominated in four categories at the 2019 Grammys, including Record of the Year and Song of the Year, and won Best American Roots Song and Best American Roots Performance.

bjork|venus as a boy.fact: "Venus as a Boy" was the second single from Björk's 1993 album Debut, produced by Nellee Hooper. Its strings were recorded by a Bombay film-studio orchestra arranged through tabla player Talvin Singh, and the track features vibraphone. It reached No. 1 in Iceland and No. 29 in the UK.

peter schilling|major tom (coming home).fact: "Major Tom (Coming Home)" was first released in German in 1982 and hit No. 1 in West Germany, Austria and Switzerland. The English version, released in the US in September 1983, reached No. 1 in Canada and No. 14 on the Billboard Hot 100. It is the lead single from Peter Schilling's album Error in the System.

klymaxx|i miss you.fact: "I Miss You" was the third single from Klymaxx's 1984 album Meeting in the Ladies Room. Keyboardist Lynn Malsby wrote it and co-produced it. It reached No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 1 in Canada.

wild cherry|play that funky music.fact: Rob Parissi wrote and produced "Play That Funky Music," released by Wild Cherry in April 1976 on the Sweet City label. It hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 on September 18, 1976 and went platinum. Vanilla Ice's 1990 version reached No. 4.

david ruffin|my whole world ended (the m.fact: "My Whole World Ended (The Moment You Left Me)" was released by Motown in January 1969 and is the title track of David Ruffin's solo debut LP. Harvey Fuqua, Johnny Bristol, Pam Sawyer and James Roach wrote it, and it reached No. 9 on the Hot 100 and No. 2 on the R&B chart.

the beach boys|feel flows.fact: "Feel Flows" opens side two of The Beach Boys' 1971 album Surf's Up. It was written by Carl Wilson and band manager Jack Rieley, with Charles Lloyd on saxophone and flute. A 2021 archival release, Feel Flows: The Sunflower & Surf's Up Sessions 1969-1971, took its title from the song.

gary lewis & the playboys|count me in.fact: "Count Me In" was released by Gary Lewis & The Playboys on Liberty Records in March 1965. Glen Hardin wrote it, Snuff Garrett produced it, and Leon Russell arranged it. It peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100, behind Herman's Hermits' "Mrs. Brown, You've Got a Lovely Daughter."

blondie|hanging on the telephone.fact: "Hanging on the Telephone" was written by Jack Lee for his band The Nerves, whose 1976 release was a commercial failure. Blondie covered it on their 1978 album Parallel Lines, and it reached No. 5 on the UK Singles Chart. Def Leppard later recorded it for their 2006 covers album Yeah!.

u2|so cruel.fact: "So Cruel" is track six on U2's 1991 album Achtung Baby, recorded at Elsinore in Dalkey and Windmill Lane Studios in Dublin. The song began when Bono picked up a guitar during a reel change and the band joined in on a first take. Depeche Mode recorded a version for the 2011 tribute album AHK-toong BAY-bi Covered.

fatboy slim|weapon of choice.fact: "Weapon of Choice" is from Fatboy Slim's 2000 album Halfway Between the Gutter and the Stars. Its Spike Jonze-directed video, with Christopher Walken dancing in a hotel lobby, won six MTV Video Music Awards in 2001 and a Grammy for Best Music Video in 2002. The song samples Sly & the Family Stone's "Into My Own Thing."

del shannon|hats off to larry.fact: Del Shannon wrote and sang "Hats Off to Larry," released on the Bigtop label in May 1961. It peaked at No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100, reached No. 1 on Canada's CHUM chart, and hit No. 6 in the UK.

cali swag district|teach me how to dougi.fact: Cali Swag District is from Inglewood, California. "Teach Me How to Dougie" was produced by RunWay Star for their 2011 album The Kickback and peaked at No. 28 on the Billboard Hot 100, No. 9 on Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs and No. 6 on Hot Rap Songs.

kid creole and the coconuts|annie (i'm n.fact: "Annie, I'm Not Your Daddy" was the third and final single from Kid Creole & The Coconuts' 1982 album Tropical Gangsters. August Darnell wrote and produced it, and it reached No. 2 on the UK Singles Chart, the band's highest UK placing.

the killers|bright lights.fact: "Bright Lights" is a non-album single by The Killers, released August 9, 2024 alongside their 20 Years of Hot Fuss residency. Brandon Flowers wrote it, and Stuart Price and Shawn Everett produced it. It reached No. 12 on Adult Alternative Airplay and No. 7 on Canada's Modern Rock chart.

the cars|it's all i can do.fact: "It's All I Can Do" is track three on The Cars' 1979 album Candy-O. Ric Ocasek wrote it and Roy Thomas Baker produced it. It peaked at No. 41 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 17 in Canada.

cat stevens|another saturday night.fact: Sam Cooke wrote "Another Saturday Night" while touring England, and his 1963 original reached No. 10 on the Hot 100. Cat Stevens released his version in July 1974, and it reached No. 6 on the Hot 100, No. 1 in Canada and No. 19 in the UK.

happenings|see you in september.fact: The Happenings formed in 1961 in Paterson, New Jersey, originally as The Four Graduates after the members finished high school. Their 1966 version of "See You in September," first recorded by the Tempos in 1959, reached No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 1 in Canada.

commodores|still.fact: "Still" was written by Lionel Richie and appears on the Commodores' 1979 album Midnight Magic. Produced by James Anthony Carmichael and the Commodores, it reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, their last US No. 1, and No. 4 in the UK.

doris day|a guy is a guy.fact: Doris Day recorded "A Guy Is a Guy" on February 7, 1952, and Columbia released it that spring. Oscar Brand published the song in 1952, and Day's version peaked at No. 4 on Billboard's Best-Selling Records chart.

midnight sister|foxes.fact: "Foxes" is the third track on Midnight Sister's second album, Painting the Roses, released in January 2021 on Jagjaguwar. The Los Angeles duo of Juliana Giraffe and Ari Balouzian followed their 2017 debut Saturn Over Sunset with it, and the video was directed by Oliver Bernsen. Reviewers heard a baroque, ELO-style opening that turns into glitter-funk.

sobs|air guitar.fact: "Air Guitar" is the title track of the second album from Singapore indie-pop band Sobs, released in October 2022 on Topshelf Records. It was their first full album in about four years, after 2018's Telltale Signs. NME described its sound as bubble-grunge meets skate-punk, with nods to Weezer and Liz Phair.

the knife|heartbeats.fact: Swedish duo The Knife's "Heartbeats" found a huge new audience when Jose Gonzalez covered it acoustically on his 2003 album Veneer. Sony used his version in a Bravia TV ad filmed with a flood of bouncing balls rolling down San Francisco hills. The cover reached the UK Top 10 as a single in 2006, and Veneer went platinum.

ween|voodoo lady.fact: "Voodoo Lady" comes from Ween's 1994 album Chocolate and Cheese and was its third and final single. It reached No. 32 on Billboard's Modern Rock Tracks chart, one of only two Ween songs to chart there. A UK EP version came out on Flying Nun Records in January 1995, with cover art by Gene Ween.

khruangbin|todavía viva.fact: "Todavia Viva" is the sixth track on Khruangbin's fourth album, A La Sala (2024), whose title means "To the Room" in Spanish. The album was built from song fragments that grew out of soundchecks and off-stage ideas. Drummer DJ Johnson's rim-shots and synth strings give the track its noir-soul feel.

tv on the radio|i was a lover.fact: "I Was a Lover" is the opening track on TV on the Radio's 2006 album Return to Cookie Mountain. One reviewer heard some of the best noise-sculpting since My Bloody Valentine's Loveless in its first minutes. Tunde Adebimpe's voice and Kyp Malone's falsetto blend together over the song's broken guitars and hip-hop beats.

angel olsen|never be mine.fact: "Never Be Mine" is the second track on Angel Olsen's 2016 album My Woman, right after "Intern." NPR described its chorus as her version of a 1960s girl-group ballad, and reviewers compared its reverb-heavy sound to 1950s rock. The album came out on Jagjaguwar.

bon iver|lump sum.fact: "Lump Sum" is from Bon Iver's debut, For Emma, Forever Ago, which Justin Vernon recorded at his father's hunting cabin in northwestern Wisconsin between late 2006 and early 2007. A Stereophile review noted how he layers his voice over simple guitar strumming on this track to create an almost religious hue.

idles|model village.fact: "Model Village" is the fourth single from IDLES' third album, Ultra Mono (September 2020), produced by Nick Launay and Adam "Atom" Greenspan. The album was built to feel like a hip-hop record, and Kenny Beats added drum programming on this track. The animated video was made by Michel and Olivier Gondry.

caroline rose|chow mein.fact: "Chow Mein" is a 2026 single from Caroline Rose's album Gentling the Horse at the Walt Whitman Mall, out October 23 on their own SUCK records, where it is track 2. Rose has described it as a story about someone trying too hard to be cool and act normal while everything goes wrong.

courtney barnett|pedestrian at best.fact: "Pedestrian at Best" was the lead single from Courtney Barnett's debut album Sometimes I Sit and Think, and Sometimes I Just Sit, released February 16, 2015. She wrote it at the last minute, and the recorded take was the first time she had sung the words out loud. Rolling Stone ranked it No. 4 on its list of the best songs of 2015.

wire|eardrum buzz.fact: "Eardrum Buzz" was released in April 1989 from Wire's album It's Beginning To And Back Again. It reached No. 2 on Billboard's Modern Rock Tracks chart and No. 68 in the UK, making it the band's biggest charting single.

beach fossils|don't fade away.fact: "Don't Fade Away" was the lead single from Beach Fossils' album Bunny, released June 2, 2023 on Bayonet Records, the label run by frontman Dustin Payseur. It was the band's first album since 2017's Somersault. It is the third track on the album.

the clash|police on my back.fact: The Clash's "Police on My Back," from the 1980 triple album Sandinista!, is a cover of a song written by Eddy Grant for his 1960s group The Equals. The Clash turned the mid-paced soul-pop original into a charged-up rocker. Their version is now the best-known one.

talking heads|and she was.fact: The video for "And She Was" (1985, from Little Creatures) was made by avant-garde animator Jim Blashfield in a cut-out collage style, after David Byrne saw his short film Suspicious Circumstances and gave him near-total creative freedom. The song reached No. 54 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 17 in the UK.

the decemberists|i'll be your girl.fact: "I'll Be Your Girl" is the title track of The Decemberists' eighth album, released March 16, 2018 on Capitol and produced by John Congleton. The album moved beyond folk-rock, with first single "Severed" drawing comparisons to New Order and Roxy Music.

sault|strong.fact: "Strong" opens the 2020 SAULT album Untitled (Rise). It was written by Cleo Sol and Inflo and produced by Inflo. Reviewers singled out its wriggling disco-funk, with a drumline interjection and ascending synths and strings that give the album its opening drive.

pulp|common people.fact: Pulp's "Common People" was released May 22, 1995 and entered the UK chart at No. 2. A month later the band headlined Glastonbury's Pyramid Stage with about ten days' notice, after The Stone Roses pulled out when guitarist John Squire was injured. Jarvis Cocker later said it was the first time he heard a crowd sing the band's words back.

mazzy star|fade into you.fact: "Fade Into You" is the best-known song by Mazzy Star, from the 1993 album So Tonight That I Might See. It was written by singer Hope Sandoval and guitarist David Roback, who also produced it. It reached No. 44 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 3 on the Modern Rock Tracks chart, and Pitchfork ranked it No. 19 on its list of the top 200 songs of the 1990s.

real estate|two arrows.fact: "Two Arrows" is a roughly seven-minute track from Real Estate's 2017 album In Mind, released on Domino. Martin Courtney told NPR he likened it to the Beatles' Abbey Road, and the song stops cold at the end as a joke.

mission of burma|mica.fact: "Mica" is on Mission of Burma's 1982 album Vs., credited to Clint Conley and Holly Anderson. A Treble review of the reissue praised its jagged harmonics. The song was later included on the 2004 compilation A Gun to the Head: A Selection from the Ace of Hearts Era.

misfits|night of the living dead.fact: "Night of the Living Dead" was the Misfits' fourth single, released around Halloween 1979 on Glenn Danzig's own Plan 9 Records, with only 2,000 copies pressed. It is named after George Romero's 1968 zombie film, which the band loved. Its B-sides were "Where Eagles Dare" and a cover of Allan Sherman's "Rat Fink."

andy shauf|try again.fact: "Try Again" is from Andy Shauf's 2020 album The Neon Skyline on ANTI-, and came out as a single in November 2019. Its stop-motion video by directors Gerald Fleury and Timo Hateau was influenced by 1970s French animation like Chapi Chapo and The Magic Roundabout.

kurt vile|check baby.fact: "Check Baby" is track 7 on Kurt Vile's 2018 album Bottle It In (Matador) and runs nearly eight minutes. It was inspired by the sound check at every show, and the title track follows right after it. Vile wrote all the songs on the album.

sylvan esso|didn't care.fact: "Didn't Care" is from Sylvan Esso's 2022 album No Rules Sandy (Loma Vista). The duo debuted the song and announced the album in July 2022, right after a surprise full-album performance at the Newport Folk Festival. Amelia Meath and Nick Sanborn wrote and produced it.

husker du|new day rising.fact: "New Day Rising" opens the 1985 Husker Du album of the same name, one of two albums the Minneapolis trio released on SST that year. The band wanted to produce it themselves, but SST insisted on in-house producer Spot. It was recorded in July 1984 and clocks in at just over two and a half minutes.

sigur ros|hoppipolla.fact: "Hoppipolla" is from Sigur Ros's 2005 album Takk.... It was used in trailers for the BBC's Planet Earth, which led to the single being re-released on May 1, 2006. For Planet Earth II in 2016, the band made a new version of the song with BBC Creative.

ramones|rockaway beach.fact: "Rockaway Beach" was written by Dee Dee Ramone and released as a single in November 1977 from the album Rocket to Russia. It is named for a Queens, New York beach he liked, and its sound draws on the Beach Boys and surf bands. It reached the Billboard Hot 100.

the stone roses|waterfall.fact: "Waterfall" is on The Stone Roses' 1989 debut album, produced by John Leckie. It was recorded between September 1988 and February 1989 and wasn't released as a single until 1991, when it reached No. 27 on the UK chart.

radiohead|exit music (for a film).fact: Radiohead wrote "Exit Music (For a Film)" for the end credits of Baz Luhrmann's 1996 movie Romeo + Juliet. They kept it off the soundtrack album so it could appear on OK Computer seven months later. The vocals were recorded in a stone stairwell at St Catherine's Court near Bath, and Ed O'Brien called it the only song the band ever made on demand.

r.e.m.|so. central rain.fact: "So. Central Rain (I'm Sorry)" was the lead single from R.E.M.'s second album, Reckoning (1984), recorded at Reflection Sound in Charlotte, North Carolina. It peaked around No. 85 on the Billboard Hot 100. Michael Stipe refused to lip-sync in its video, which was filmed at the studio during the album sessions.

tame impala|dracula.fact: "Dracula" was released September 26, 2025 as the third single from Tame Impala's fifth album, Deadbeat (Columbia, October 17, 2025). Kevin Parker produced it, and Julian Klincewicz directed the video. The album was inspired by Western Australia's bush doof rave culture.

kate bush|hounds of love.fact: The title track of Kate Bush's 1985 album Hounds of Love opens with a spoken sample from the 1957 British horror film Night of the Demon, directed by Jacques Tourneur. The line, "It's in the trees! It's coming!", comes from a seance scene. The film was adapted from an M.R. James story called "Casting the Runes."

phoebe bridgers|chinese satellite.fact: "Chinese Satellite" is track 6 on Phoebe Bridgers' 2020 album Punisher, whose guests include Conor Oberst, Lucy Dacus and Julien Baker. AllMusic singled out its glistening strings. In 2022 she released a live version recorded at Sound City Studios to raise money for the charity New Hope For Families.

the cramps|goo goo muck.fact: The Cramps' "Goo Goo Muck" is on their 1981 album Psychedelic Jungle and is a cover of a 1962 song by Ronnie Cook and the Gaylads. It got a huge boost in 2022 when it played during Jenna Ortega's dance scene in Netflix's Wednesday, jumping from about 2,500 to over 209,000 daily streams in about a week.

beck|rowboat.fact: Beck first released "Rowboat" on his 1994 album Stereopathetic Soulmanure. Johnny Cash later covered it as the opening track of his 1996 album Unchained, after producer Rick Rubin brought him the song. Cash reportedly said it sounded like something he might have written in the sixties.

fontaines d.c.|where is gone? (with rosa.fact: "Where Is Gone?" is a duet with Rosalia from Fontaines D.C.'s fifth album Dopamine Chamber, released October 16 and produced by James Ford. Rosalia is the only featured artist on the album's tracklist, and the single arrived October 12.

Sting|If I Ever Lose My Faith In You.fact: Sting won the 1994 Grammy for Best Male Pop Vocal Performance for If I Ever Lose My Faith in You. The song comes from his 1993 album Ten Summoner's Tales and reached No. 17 on the Billboard Hot 100.

The Cardigans|Lovefool.fact: Lovefool was written by Peter Svensson and Nina Persson for the Cardigans' third album, First Band on the Moon (1996). It reached a much wider audience after appearing in Baz Luhrmann's film Romeo + Juliet.

MGMT|Electric Feel.fact: Electric Feel was released in 2008 as the second single from MGMT's debut album Oracular Spectacular, which was produced by Dave Fridmann and the band. A remix of the song by Justice won the Grammy for Best Remixed Recording, Non-Classical.

Modest Mouse|The World At Large.fact: The World at Large opens Modest Mouse's 2004 album Good News for People Who Love Bad News, which was produced by Dennis Herring and released by Epic Records. It was recorded in 2003 and appears just ahead of the album's first single, Float On.

Mantronix|Needle To The Groove.fact: Needle to the Groove was written by MC Tee and Kurtis Mantronik, and it features a vocoder hook. That hook was later sampled by Beck on his 1996 song Where It's At.

Gorillaz|Rhinestone Eyes.fact: Rhinestone Eyes was released as a promotional single from Gorillaz's 2010 album Plastic Beach. It was first planned as the fourth single, but the band chose Doncamatic instead, and a storyboard version of a video was posted to YouTube in October 2010.

Robert John|The Lion Sleeps Tonight.fact: Robert John's 1972 version of The Lion Sleeps Tonight reached No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100 and earned a gold record. It was a remake of the Tokens' 1961 No. 1 hit, and Jay Siegel of the Tokens sang backing vocals.

Gorillaz|Stylo feat. Mos Def and Bobby W.fact: Stylo was the lead single from Gorillaz's third album, Plastic Beach, released in January 2010. Mos Def appears in the video as an animated character, and the song leaked online before its official release.

Alice Merton|run away girl.fact: Run Away Girl is the lead single from Alice Merton's 2024 EP Heron, released on her own label, Paper Plane Records. She co-wrote and produced it with James Dring and Paul Whalley.

The Hollies|The Air That I Breathe.fact: The Air That I Breathe was written by Albert Hammond and Mike Hazlewood, and Hammond recorded it first on his 1972 debut album. The Hollies' 1974 version reached No. 2 in the UK and was engineered by Alan Parsons.

Barbra Streisand|People.fact: People was written by Jule Styne and Bob Merrill for the 1964 Broadway musical Funny Girl, where Barbra Streisand introduced it. It became her first hit single and reached No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100.

Justin Timberlake|CAN'T STOP THE FEELING.fact: Can't Stop the Feeling! was written by Justin Timberlake, Max Martin, and Shellback for the animated film Trolls. It was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Original Song, and Timberlake performed it at the 2017 Oscars ceremony.

Elton John|Rocket Man.fact: Rocket Man appeared on Elton John's 1972 album Honky Chateau, produced by Gus Dudgeon and recorded at the Chateau d'Herouville in France. The single reached No. 2 in the UK and No. 6 in the US.

Justin Timberlake|Say Something feat. Ch.fact: Say Something was released in January 2018 ahead of Justin Timberlake's album Man of the Woods. Chris Stapleton first worked on the album as a songwriter before being asked to sing on the track, and it debuted at No. 9 on the Billboard Hot 100.

Beyonce|BREAK MY SOUL.fact: Break My Soul was the lead single from Beyonce's 2022 album Renaissance and samples Robin S's Show Me Love and Big Freedia's Explode. It reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in August 2022.

Bobby \"Boris\" Pickett|The Monster Mash.fact: The Monster Mash reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in October 1962, shortly before Halloween. Its backing band, the Crypt-Kickers, included Leon Russell on piano, and Gary Paxton produced the session and released it on his Garpax label.

Dion & The Belmonts|Where Or When.fact: Where Or When was released by Dion and the Belmonts in November 1959 and reached number 3 on the Billboard Hot 100. It followed their earlier hit A Teenager in Love, which peaked at number 5 that same year.

Huey Lewis & The News|Heart And Soul.fact: Heart And Soul was first recorded by the band Exile in 1981, and Huey Lewis and the News largely followed that arrangement. It was released on August 30, 1983 as the first single from the album Sports, and reached number 8 on the Billboard Hot 100.

The Beach Boys|Help Me, Rhonda.fact: Help Me, Rhonda was released in April 1965 and became the Beach Boys' second number one single, after I Get Around. Al Jardine sings the lead vocal, which was unusual for the group at the time.

The Jesus and Mary Chain|Head On.fact: Head On appeared on the Jesus and Mary Chain's 1989 album Automatic. The Pixies covered it on their 1991 album Trompe le Monde, and that version reached number 6 on the US Modern Rock Tracks chart.

Foo Fighters|Rope.fact: Rope debuted at number one on Billboard's Rock Songs chart in 2011, only the second song ever to do so. It is from Wasting Light, which was recorded in Dave Grohl's garage using only analog equipment and co-produced by Butch Vig.

Little Simz|Introvert.fact: Introvert was the lead single from Little Simz's fourth album, Sometimes I Might Be Introvert, released in 2021. The album was executive produced by Inflo and won the 2022 Mercury Prize.

Guns N' Roses|November Rain.fact: At just under nine minutes, November Rain was the longest song to enter the Billboard top ten at the time of its release. It peaked at number 3 on the Billboard Hot 100 and number 4 in the UK.

Weather Report|Birdland.fact: Joe Zawinul wrote Birdland as a tribute to the New York jazz club and it appeared on Weather Report's 1977 album Heavy Weather. The Manhattan Transfer recorded a vocal version with lyrics by Jon Hendricks, which won Grammy Awards.

Big Country|Fields of Fire.fact: Fields of Fire was released in February 1983 as the second single from Big Country's debut album, The Crossing. Steve Lillywhite produced it, and the single version, subtitled 400 Miles, reached number 10 in the UK.

Player|Baby Come Back.fact: Baby Come Back was written by Player founders Peter Beckett and J.C. Crowley. Released in late 1977, it spent three weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in January 1978.

Leaders Of The New School|International.fact: International Zone Coaster is from the 1991 debut album A Future Without a Past..., on Elektra. The group included a teenage Busta Rhymes, and the album topped the Billboard Heatseekers chart.

Silhouettes|Get A Job.fact: Get A Job reached number one on both the Billboard pop and R&B charts in February 1958. The revival group Sha Na Na took its name from the nonsense syllables in the song's chorus.

Culture Club|I'll Tumble 4 You.fact: I'll Tumble 4 Ya was the fifth single from Culture Club's debut album, Kissing to Be Clever, and reached number 9 in the US. Culture Club became the first band since the Beatles to score three US top 10 singles from a debut album.

Diana Ross & The Supremes|My World Is Em.fact: My World Is Empty Without You was written by Holland-Dozier-Holland and released on Motown in December 1965. It peaked at number 5 in the US, one of the few songs the team wrote for the Supremes that did not reach number one.

Jason Isbell and the 400 Unit|Hope the H.fact: Hope the High Road was the first single from The Nashville Sound, released in 2017. It was the first album since 2011 to give Isbell's band, the 400 Unit, title billing, and it won the Grammy for Best Americana Album.

The Whispers|And the Beat Goes On.fact: And the Beat Goes On was written by Leon Sylvers, Stephen Shockley and William Shelby and released on Solar Records in 1979. It reached number one on the R&B chart and number 19 on the Hot 100, the Whispers' first top 20 pop hit.

Portishead|Strangers.fact: Strangers is the third track on Portishead's debut album Dummy, released in August 1994. The album was produced by Geoff Barrow with Adrian Utley as co-producer, and it won the 1995 Mercury Music Prize.

The Jeremy Spencer Band|Cool Breeze.fact: Cool Breeze is from Flee, a 1979 album credited to the Jeremy Spencer Band. The single reached number 21 on the US Billboard Adult Contemporary chart, even though the album was not a commercial success.

Goldfinger|Superman.fact: Superman first appeared on Goldfinger's 1997 album Hang-Ups and was also used in the film Kingpin. It reached a wider audience through the Tony Hawk's Pro Skater video game soundtrack, and Tony Hawk joined the band on stage to play it in 2023.

Joni Mitchell|In France They Kiss on Mai.fact: In France They Kiss on Main Street is from Joni Mitchell's 1976 album The Hissing of Summer Lawns and reached number 66 on the Billboard Hot 100. It features David Crosby, Graham Nash and James Taylor on backing vocals and Jeff Skunk Baxter on guitar.

The Magnetic Fields|I Think I Need a New.fact: I Think I Need a New Heart is on 69 Love Songs, a three-volume album released by Merge Records in 1999. Stephin Merritt wrote and produced the entire set and sings lead on this track.

Jackson Browne|Tender Is The Night.fact: Tender Is the Night was the second single from Jackson Browne's 1983 album Lawyers in Love. It entered the Billboard Hot 100 at number 79, peaked at number 25, and spent 17 weeks on the chart.

John Prine|Fish and Whistle.fact: Fish and Whistle opens Bruised Orange, John Prine's fifth album, released in May 1978. Prine's friend Steve Goodman produced it at the Chicago Recording Company, and the track ends with a soprano saxophone solo.

Florence + The Machine|Shake It Out.fact: Shake It Out was written by Florence Welch and Paul Epworth and produced by Epworth, who produced the whole standard edition of the 2011 album Ceremonials. That album debuted at number one on the UK Albums Chart.

Cat Stevens|Morning Has Broken.fact: Morning Has Broken appeared on Cat Stevens's 1971 album Teaser and the Firecat, with Rick Wakeman playing piano. The single reached number six on the US Billboard Hot 100 and number one on the US easy listening chart in 1972.

Gorillaz|Humility feat. George Benson.fact: Humility was released on 31 May 2018 as the first single from Gorillaz's sixth album, The Now Now. It debuted at number 85 on the Billboard Hot 100, giving guitarist George Benson his first Hot 100 entry since 1985.

Dixie Cups|Chapel Of Love.fact: Chapel of Love was written by Jeff Barry, Ellie Greenwich and Phil Spector, and was the first single released on the Red Bird label. The Dixie Cups' version reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in June 1964 and sold over a million copies.

Gorillaz|On Melancholy Hill.fact: On Melancholy Hill was the third single from Gorillaz's 2010 album Plastic Beach. Its video, directed by Jamie Hewlett, follows the animated guitarist Noodle, and the song has been certified Platinum in the UK.

Blondie|Call Me.fact: Call Me was written for the 1980 film American Gigolo, with music by producer Giorgio Moroder and lyrics by Debbie Harry. It spent six weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 and was Blondie's second chart-topper. Moroder originally offered the song to Stevie Nicks.

Pink Floyd|Echoes.fact: Echoes fills the entire second side of Pink Floyd's 1971 album Meddle and runs 23 minutes 29 seconds. It grew out of a studio experiment in which Richard Wright ran a single piano note through a Leslie speaker. The band first played it live in April 1971 under the title Return of the Son of Nothing.

Dire Straits|Walk Of Life.fact: Walk of Life, from the 1985 album Brothers in Arms, reached number two in the UK, tying with Private Investigations as Dire Straits' biggest UK hit. In the US it peaked at number seven on the Billboard Hot 100.

Elvis Presley|Mystery Train.fact: Elvis Presley recorded Mystery Train on July 11, 1955, at Sam Phillips's Memphis studio, with Scotty Moore on lead guitar and Bill Black on bass. Released as the B-side of I Forgot to Remember to Forget, it was his last single for Sun Records. The song was first recorded by Junior Parker in 1953.

The Everly Brothers|All I Have To Do Is.fact: All I Have to Do Is Dream was written by Boudleaux and Felice Bryant and reached number one in May 1958. Chet Atkins, a family friend of the Everlys, played the guitar part. It topped the pop, country and R&B charts.

The Gap Band|I Don't Believe You Want To.fact: The song is from the 1979 album The Gap Band II. The group was formed in Tulsa, Oklahoma, by the Wilson brothers Ronnie, Charlie and Robert, and took its name from Greenwood, Archer and Pine, three streets in Tulsa's historic Black business district.

Grateful Dead|Estimated Prophet.fact: Estimated Prophet opens the Grateful Dead's 1977 album Terrapin Station and is written by Bob Weir and John Perry Barlow in an unusual seven-beat meter. Producer Keith Olsen brought in Tom Scott to play a solo on the lyricon, an electric woodwind instrument.

Bobby Vee|Rubber Ball.fact: Rubber Ball was co-written by Gene Pitney and Aaron Schroeder, who was credited under Pitney's mother's maiden name, Orlowski. Bobby Vee's version, produced by Snuff Garrett on Liberty Records, peaked at number six on the Billboard Hot 100 and was number one in Australia.

The Four Seasons|Candy Girl.fact: Candy Girl was released on Vee-Jay in 1963 and reached number three on the Billboard Hot 100. Written by Larry Santos, it was the first original Four Seasons single written by neither Bob Crewe nor Bob Gaudio.

David Bowie|Where Are We Now?.fact: Where Are We Now? was released with no advance promotion on David Bowie's 66th birthday, 8 January 2013, and was produced by Tony Visconti. It announced The Next Day, his first studio album in ten years, which debuted at number one in the UK.

Mr. Big|To Be With You.fact: To Be With You was the second single from Mr. Big's 1991 album Lean into It. It spent three weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in early 1992. It was written by singer Eric Martin with David Grahame.

Queen|Keep Yourself Alive.fact: Keep Yourself Alive was Queen's debut single, released in the UK in July 1973. Guitarist Brian May wrote it, and it opens the band's self-titled first album. It was part of the first demo the band recorded in December 1971.

Miley Cyrus|Flowers.fact: Flowers spent eight weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2023. It won Miley Cyrus her first Grammy Awards, including Record of the Year and Best Pop Solo Performance, at the 2024 ceremony.

Foreigner|Urgent.fact: Junior Walker played the tenor saxophone solo on Foreigner's Urgent, from the 1981 album 4. He happened to be performing in New York during the sessions, and producer Mutt Lange reportedly preferred his rough first take. The album spent ten weeks at number one on the Billboard album chart.

Jimmy Cliff|I Can See Clearly Now.fact: Jimmy Cliff's version of I Can See Clearly Now was recorded for the 1993 film Cool Runnings and reached number 18 on the Billboard Hot 100. The song was written by Johnny Nash, whose 1972 original went to number one. Cliff has said he played bongo drums on Nash's recording.

Connie Francis|Everybody's Somebody's Fo.fact: Everybody's Somebody's Fool gave Connie Francis her first number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in June 1960. It began as the B-side of Jealous of You, but disc jockeys preferred it. It was written by Jack Keller and Howard Greenfield.

Gnarls Barkley|Crazy.fact: Crazy became the first song to reach number one on the UK singles chart on download sales alone, in April 2006, before the CD was released. It stayed at the top for nine weeks and was the UK's best-selling single of 2006. It comes from the duo's debut album St. Elsewhere.

Four Tops|It's The Same Old Song.fact: It's the Same Old Song was written and released by Motown in about 24 hours in July 1965, as a quick follow-up to I Can't Help Myself. Holland-Dozier-Holland had first cut a track of it for the Supremes. The Four Tops' version reached number five on the Billboard Hot 100.

The Cars|Shake It Up.fact: Shake It Up was the title track of the Cars' fourth album, released in November 1981. It reached number four on the Billboard Hot 100 and was the band's first top-ten single there. Ric Ocasek wrote it.

Ween|The Mollusk.fact: The Mollusk was released by Elektra in June 1997 and produced by Andrew Weiss. It is a concept album with a nautical theme. It was the first Ween album to feature keyboardist Glenn McClelland, and bassist Dave Dreiwitz joined just before its release, completing the five-member lineup.

Justice|We Are Your Friends.fact: We Are Your Friends began as a remix of the Simian single Never Be Alone, made for a remix contest that Justice did not win. A record company heard it and released it as Justice vs. Simian in 2006. Its video won the 2006 MTV Europe Music Award for Best Video.

Seals & Crofts|Summer Breeze.fact: Summer Breeze was Seals & Crofts' first Billboard Hot 100 hit, peaking at number six in November 1972. The Isley Brothers recorded a version with prominent electric guitar by Ernie Isley on their 1973 album 3 + 3.

Al Green|Love and Happiness.fact: Al Green co-wrote Love and Happiness with guitarist Teenie Hodges, and Willie Mitchell produced it during the 1972 sessions for the album I'm Still in Love with You. Hodges was part of Hi Records' house band, the Hi Rhythm Section.

Dell-Vikings|Come Go With Me.fact: The Del-Vikings formed in 1955 among Air Force servicemen stationed in Pittsburgh, and were one of the few racially mixed vocal groups of the era. Come Go With Me was first released on the small Fee Bee label and then picked up nationally by Dot Records. It reached the top five on the Billboard pop chart in 1957.

Sugar Ray|Every Morning.fact: Every Morning, from Sugar Ray's 1999 album 14:59, reached number 3 on the Billboard Hot 100. It also topped the Modern Rock Tracks chart in the United States and the RPM chart in Canada.

Phil Collins|In The Air Tonight.fact: The big gated-reverb drum sound on In The Air Tonight grew out of experiments at Townhouse Studios in London, where engineers Hugh Padgham and Steve Lillywhite processed Collins's drums during Peter Gabriel sessions. The sound became a signature of 1980s records.

Jan & Dean|The Little Old Lady (From Pas.fact: The Little Old Lady (From Pasadena) was inspired by a Dodge ad campaign in Southern California in 1964 that starred actress Kathryn Minner. Jan Berry, Don Altfeld and Roger Christian wrote the song, and it was released on Liberty in June 1964.

Bangles|Walk Like An Egyptain.fact: Walk Like an Egyptian was written by Liam Sternberg and released in 1986 as the third single from the Bangles' album Different Light. It became the band's first number one single in the United States.

Gorillaz|Andromeda feat. D.R.A.M..fact: Andromeda was released in March 2017 as a single from Gorillaz's album Humanz. It earned a Grammy nomination for Best Dance Recording.

Chicago|You're The Inspiration.fact: You're the Inspiration was written by Peter Cetera and David Foster for Chicago's 1984 album Chicago 17. It reached number 3 on the Billboard Hot 100 and topped the Adult Contemporary chart in early 1985.

Stephen Stills|Love The One You're With.fact: Stephen Stills wrote Love the One You're With after borrowing a phrase he heard Billy Preston say, and Preston gave his permission. David Crosby and Graham Nash sing backing vocals on the track.

Elton John|Little Jeannie.fact: Little Jeannie, from the 1980 album 21 at 33, has lyrics by Gary Osborne, who added words to Elton John's music. It reached number 3 on the Billboard Hot 100 and number 1 on the Adult Contemporary chart.

George Harrison|Got My Mind Set On You.fact: Got My Mind Set On You is a cover of a 1962 song by James Ray, written by Rudy Clark. Harrison recorded it for Cloud Nine, co-produced with Jeff Lynne, and it reached number 1 in the US in January 1988, his first chart-topper in 15 years.

The Four Seasons|Rag Doll.fact: Rag Doll was written by Bob Crewe and Bob Gaudio and released in June 1964 on Philips Records. It became a number one hit for the Four Seasons, with Silence Is Golden on the B-side.

Doobie Brothers|Long Train Runnin'.fact: Long Train Runnin' began as an instrumental jam the Doobie Brothers played for nearly three years under other names. It missed the cut for 1972's Toulouse Street and was recorded for 1973's The Captain and Me, where it reached number 8 on the Billboard Hot 100.

father john misty|god's favorite custome.fact: The title track of Father John Misty's 2018 album God's Favorite Customer features vocals from Natalie Mering of Weyes Blood. It was produced by Josh Tillman, Jonathan Rado, and Jonathan Wilson. The album reached number 18 on the Billboard 200 and number 1 on the US Alternative Albums chart.

toro y moi|all alone.fact: "All Alone" opens Toro y Moi's 2011 Freaking Out EP, which came out on Carpark Records. Chaz Bundick recorded it in June of that year during a break in touring, and it was first offered as a free download.

anna burch|with you every day.fact: "With You Every Day" closes Anna Burch's debut album Quit the Curse, released February 2, 2018 on Polyvinyl. The video for the song was directed by Ben Collins and shows Burch and her band performing in a big, open room.

jungle|truth.fact: "Truth" was the fourth single from Jungle's third album, Loving in Stereo (August 13, 2021). With its driving motorik rhythm and punk-flavored energy, it sounded unlike their earlier work, and it became their second song to reach the Top 40 of Billboard's Alternative Airplay chart.

the postal service|such great heights.fact: Ben Gibbard and Jimmy Tamborello finished "Such Great Heights" in 2002, and it became the lead single from the Postal Service's album Give Up on Sub Pop. Sub Pop offered a free download that passed nine million downloads by 2005, and Iron & Wine's quiet acoustic cover later appeared in the film Garden State.

milly|drip from the fountain.fact: "Drip From The Fountain" was the lead single from MILLY's second album, Your Own Becoming (2024, Dangerbird). The Los Angeles band began as Brendan Dyer's solo project and the album was produced by Sonny DiPerri.

kim gordon|bye bye.fact: "BYE BYE" is the opening track and lead single from Kim Gordon's second solo album, The Collective (Matador, March 8, 2024). Producer Justin Raisen sent Gordon instrumental tracks, and she recorded her vocals over them and added distortion effects.

mount kimbie|dumb guitar.fact: "Dumb Guitar" is the second track on Mount Kimbie's fourth album, The Sunset Violent (Warp, April 2024), a shift from their electronic roots toward indie rock and their first album as a quartet. It was released as a single on November 2, 2023, on 7-inch backed with "Boxing", which features King Krule.

jenny hval|ashes to ashes.fact: "Ashes to Ashes" is the fifth track on Jenny Hval's 2019 album The Practice of Love (Sacred Bones). It was released as a single on July 10, 2019, and Hval pointed out on Twitter that despite the title it is not a cover of the David Bowie song.

mgmt|dancing in babylon ft. christine an.fact: "Dancing in Babylon" from MGMT's 2024 album Loss of Life is the first outside guest feature on any MGMT album. Andrew VanWyngarden said it began as a jokey song and became more like a big ballad once Christine and the Queens joined. Extra production came from Daniel Lopatin and Danger Mouse.

bartees strange|wants needs.fact: "Wants Needs" is the sixth track on Bartees Strange's third album, Horror (4AD, February 14, 2025), and was released as the album's fourth single on January 14, 2025.

beach house|lemon glow.fact: "Lemon Glow" was the lead single from Beach House's 2018 album 7, released February 15, 2018 on Sub Pop. Pitchfork named it a "Best New Track" and called it a new direction for the band, built around a warped organ sample and a persistent hi-hat pattern. The album followed on May 11, 2018.

husker du|these important years.fact: "These Important Years" opens Warehouse: Songs and Stories, the sixth and final studio album by Hüsker Dü, released in 1987 on Warner Bros. Bob Mould wrote the song, and he and Grant Hart co-produced the album. Its mid-tempo feel was a contrast to the blistering openers of the band's earlier records.

grizzly bear|lullabye.fact: "Lullabye" is the second track on Grizzly Bear's 2006 album Yellow House, released on Warp Records. The album took its name from the house on Cape Cod belonging to Ed Droste's mother, where it was recorded. Chris Taylor is credited as producer.

radiohead|climbing up the walls.fact: On this OK Computer track, Jonny Greenwood wrote a string part for 16 stringed instruments playing in quarter tones. He has said he was excited to write strings that did not sound like the Beatles' "Eleanor Rigby." The dense, unsettling orchestral wall is often compared to the work of composer Krzysztof Penderecki.

idles|roy.fact: "Roy" is the fourth track on IDLES' fifth studio album, TANGK, released in February 2024 on Partisan Records. Guitarist Mark Bowen is credited with writing the song, and the album was produced by Nigel Godrich, Kenny Beats and Bowen. The band later reworked the song for a Spotify Singles session.

young fathers|in my view.fact: "In My View" was the second single from Young Fathers' third album, Cocoa Sugar, released March 9, 2018 on Ninja Tune. The Scottish trio had won the 2014 Mercury Prize for their debut album Dead. The song's video was directed by Jack Whiteley.

iggy pop|lust for life.fact: On Iggy Pop's "Lust for Life," the drums are credited to Hunt Sales and the bass to his brother Tony Sales. NPR has noted that the song's famous bouncy beat, accenting the 2nd and 4th beats, echoes an earlier Motown record by the Supremes.

the national|bloodbuzz ohio.fact: "Bloodbuzz Ohio" was the first single from The National's album High Violet. The band made it available as a free download on their website on March 24, 2010, and a 7-inch vinyl followed in May 2010 with the exclusive B-side "Sin-Eaters."
