It peaked at number 16 on Belgium's Ultratop chart.

califone|funeral singers.fact: "Funeral Singers" comes from Califone's 2009 album All My Friends Are Funeral Singers, their first release on the Dead Oceans label. Bandleader Tim Rutili made the record to accompany a feature film of the same name that he wrote.

kate bush|the big sky.fact: "The Big Sky" was the fourth and final single from Kate Bush's No. 1 album Hounds of Love, released in April 1986. Kate Bush played the Fairlight CMI synthesizer and piano on it, and her brother Paddy Bush added didgeridoo. The 12-inch single featured a longer "Meteorological mix."

radiohead|15 step.fact: "15 Step" opens Radiohead's 2007 album In Rainbows and is written in an unusual 5/4 time signature, giving it a lopsided, stuttering groove. The title is often tied to the odd count of beats in its looping drum pattern.

beck|blackbird chain.fact: "Blackbird Chain" was recorded during a 2011 session with Jack White at Third Man Records. It sat unreleased for a few years before landing on Beck's 2014 album Morning Phase, which was billed as a companion piece to his 2002 album Sea Change.

unknown mortal orchestra|the world is cr.fact: "The World Is Crowded" is the sixth track on Unknown Mortal Orchestra's 2015 album Multi-Love, released on Jagjaguwar. The album followed 2013's II, and a reviewer noted this track has a faint whiff of Hall & Oates about it.

madi diaz|don't do me good (feat. kacey.fact: "Don't Do Me Good" is a duet between Madi Diaz and Kacey Musgraves, released in November 2023 as a pre-release single from Diaz's album Weird Faith (ANTI-, February 9, 2024). The arrangement is sparse, built mostly on piano and an airy drum kit so the two voices stay front and center.

mk.gee|rockman.fact: "ROCKMAN" is a standalone single from Mk.gee, the project of New Jersey musician Michael Gordon, released after his 2024 debut album Two Star & the Dream Police. Its title is presumably a nod to the Rockman headphone amplifier invented by Boston's Tom Scholz.

anamanaguchi|magnet.fact: "Magnet" was released as a single in June 2025 ahead of Anamanaguchi's album Anyway, their first full-length since 2019's [USA]. Its music video has a Batman theme, and the band joked that they really wanted to be in a Batman soundtrack.

the breeders|off you.fact: "Off You" was the lead single from The Breeders' 2002 album Title TK, issued as a limited 10-inch on 4AD in March 2002 before the album arrived in May. The album was recorded with Steve Albini at Electrical Audio in Chicago, and the song later appeared in Spike Jonze's 2013 film Her.

wolf parade|under glass.fact: "Under Glass" is the opening track on Wolf Parade's 2020 album Thin Mind, released on Sub Pop. The band made the record as a trio of Dan Boeckner, Spencer Krug, and Arlen Thompson after bassist Dante DeCaro left, and reviewers heard a return to their early 80s-synth-flavored sound.

Opus III|It's A Fine Day.fact: Opus III's 1992 hit was a cover of a song first recorded a cappella in 1983 by an artist known as Jane. The dance version, fronted by singer Kirsty Hawkshaw, reached the UK Top 10 and topped the US dance club play chart.

Jennifer Paige|Crush.fact: Crush was Jennifer Paige's debut single and peaked at number 3 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1998, holding that spot for several weeks. It also went to number 1 in Australia and number 4 in the UK.

Gordon Lightfoot|Sundown.fact: Sundown became Gordon Lightfoot's only number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1974. The album of the same name also hit number 1 on the Billboard 200, after replacing Paul McCartney and Wings' Band on the Run at the top.

Peter Gabriel|In Your Eyes.fact: On this track from Peter Gabriel's album So, Senegalese singer Youssou N'Dour improvised Wolof vocals over the ending. The song became a hit with a new audience after it was used in the 1989 film Say Anything...

The Strokes|Hard To Explain..fact: Hard To Explain was a single from The Strokes' debut album Is This It. The album was recorded in March and April 2001 at Transporterraum in New York City with producer Gordon Raphael.

Martha Reeves & The Vandellas|(Love Is L.fact: Heat Wave was written and produced by the Motown team of Holland-Dozier-Holland and reached number 4 on the Billboard Hot 100 and number 1 on the R&B chart. It earned the group a Grammy nomination, making them the first Motown group nominated for a Grammy.

Ricky Nelson|I'm Walkin'.fact: Ricky Nelson's first single was a cover of Fats Domino's I'm Walkin', released in 1957. He performed it on his family's TV show The Adventures of Ozzie and Harriet, and it reached number 4, matching Domino's chart peak.

House of Pain|Jump Around.fact: Since 1998, the University of Wisconsin has played Jump Around between the third and fourth quarters of home football games at Camp Randall Stadium. It started at a Homecoming game against Purdue and became an instant tradition.

The Strokes|Last Nite..fact: Last Nite was a single from The Strokes' debut album Is This It. The album was recorded in 2001 at Transporterraum in New York City with producer Gordon Raphael.

The Strokes|The Modern Age..fact: The Modern Age appears on The Strokes' debut album Is This It. The album was recorded in March and April 2001 at Transporterraum in New York City with producer Gordon Raphael, who also produced the follow-up Room on Fire.

Johnny Rivers|Secret Agent Man.fact: Secret Agent Man was written by P.F. Sloan and Steve Barri for the opening titles of the US broadcast of the British spy series Danger Man, which aired in America as Secret Agent. Johnny Rivers' version became a Top 10 hit in 1966.

The Strokes|Someday..fact: Someday was the third single from The Strokes' debut album Is This It. The album was recorded in 2001 at Transporterraum in New York City with producer Gordon Raphael.

Kool & The Gang|Hollywood Swinging.fact: Hollywood Swinging was released in April 1974 on De-Lite Records and became Kool & the Gang's first number 1 on the R&B chart. It comes from their album Wild and Peaceful.

The Strokes|The Way It Is.fact: The Way It Is is a track on The Strokes' debut album Is This It. The album was recorded in March and April 2001 at Transporterraum in New York City with producer Gordon Raphael.

Minako Hamano|Brain Age 2: More Training.fact: Minako Hamano composed the music for Brain Age 2: More Training in Minutes a Day!, the Nintendo DS sequel to Brain Age. She worked on music for the Brain Age series.

Dave Matthews Band|Satellite.fact: Satellite was a single from Dave Matthews Band's 1994 debut studio album Under the Table and Dreaming, produced by Steve Lillywhite and recorded at Bearsville Studios in Woodstock, New York. The album was later certified six times platinum in the US.

The Police|Message In A Bottle.fact: Message in a Bottle was the first single from The Police's second album Reggatta de Blanc and became their first UK number one in 1979. The album also hit number one in the UK.

Rare Earth|I Just Want To Celebrate.fact: I Just Want to Celebrate reached number 7 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1971, the last Top 10 single for Rare Earth. It was released on the band's own Rare Earth label, which was part of Motown.

Air|All I Need (feat. Beth Hirsch).fact: Air invited American singer Beth Hirsch to record for Moon Safari after hearing her demo, and she wrote the lyrics and melody of All I Need. It was the album's third single, released in November 1998, and was produced by Nicolas Godin and Jean-Benoit Dunckel.

Coasters|Yakety Yak.fact: Written and produced by Jerry Leiber and Mike Stoller, Yakety Yak topped the R&B chart in 1958 and reached number one on the pop Top 100. King Curtis played the tenor sax on the record, and his solo helped inspire Boots Randolph's 1963 instrumental Yakety Sax. The song was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame in 1999.

Green Day|She.fact: She was the fifth and final single from Green Day's 1994 album Dookie, released in May 1995. Billie Joe Armstrong is credited as lyricist, with Mike Dirnt and Tre Cool credited on the music.

Hall & Oates|Sara Smile.fact: Sara Smile first charted in early 1976 and peaked at number 4 on the Billboard Hot 100. It was written about Daryl Hall's girlfriend Sara Allen, and although both men are credited, John Oates has described it as Daryl's song.

The Strokes|The End Has No End.fact: The End Has No End is track 10 on The Strokes' second album, Room on Fire (2003). It was the album's third and final single, released in November 2004, and reached number 27 on the UK Singles Chart.

Prince and The Revolution|Raspberry Bere.fact: Raspberry Beret, from the 1985 album Around the World in a Day, peaked at number 2 on the Billboard Hot 100. Wendy Melvoin and Lisa Coleman of The Revolution sang background vocals on it. The album itself reached number 1 on the Billboard 200.

James Taylor|Mexico.fact: Mexico opens James Taylor's 1975 album Gorilla, his sixth studio album, and was released as a single from it that year. It was a modest hit, reaching number 49 on the US chart.

OK Go|White Knuckles.fact: The video for White Knuckles, from OK Go's 2010 album Of the Blue Colour of the Sky, features a dozen dogs, mostly shelter dogs, performing alongside the band in one continuous shot. It premiered on The Ellen DeGeneres Show in September 2010 and passed a million views in about a day.

Paul McCartney|New.fact: New is the title track of Paul McCartney's 2013 album, which reached number 3 on the UK album chart. The track was produced by Mark Ronson, while the album's other producers included Paul Epworth, Ethan Johns and Giles Martin, who also served as executive producer.

The Strokes|Take It or Leave It..fact: Take It or Leave It is the closing track on The Strokes' 2001 debut album, Is This It. The band performed it with Charli XCX as a guest at the Outside Lands festival in San Francisco.

Kacey Musgraves|Jade Green.fact: Jade Green is track 9 on Kacey Musgraves' 2024 album Deeper Well, released March 15, 2024. Musgraves co-produced the album with Daniel Tashian and Ian Fitchuk, who also worked on her Grammy-winning Golden Hour, and it debuted at number 2 on the Billboard 200.

Judee Sill|Crayon Angels.fact: Crayon Angels opens Judee Sill's self-titled 1971 debut album, released on David Geffen's Asylum Records. Sill is widely described as the label's first signed artist. She accompanies herself on nylon-string guitar on the track.

Hall & Oates|So Close.fact: So Close, from the 1990 album Change of Season, was produced by Danny Kortchmar and Jon Bon Jovi and peaked at number 11 on the pop chart. Daryl Hall wrote it with George Green.

Alanis Morissette|Head Over Feet.fact: Head Over Feet was co-written and produced by Glen Ballard and released in July 1996 as the fifth single from Jagged Little Pill. It reached number 7 on the UK chart and spent weeks at number one on the Canadian singles chart.

Trouble Funk|Pump Me Up.fact: Pump Me Up is on Drop the Bomb, the 1982 album by Washington, D.C. go-go band Trouble Funk, released on Sugar Hill Records. The track has been sampled by many hip-hop artists, including Public Enemy on Fight the Power.

Fats Domino|Blue Monday.fact: Dave Bartholomew wrote Blue Monday for Smiley Lewis in 1954, but Fats Domino's 1956 version was the big hit, reaching number 5 on the pop chart and number 1 on the R&B chart. Domino also performed it in the 1956 film The Girl Can't Help It.

Stan Getz & Astrud Gilberto|The Girl Fro.fact: The Girl From Ipanema won Record of the Year at the 1965 Grammy Awards, credited to Stan Getz and Astrud Gilberto. The album it comes from, Getz/Gilberto, won Album of the Year, the first jazz album to do so.

Sharon Jones and the Dap-Kings|100 Days,.fact: The title track comes from the 2007 album 100 Days, 100 Nights, the third studio album by Sharon Jones & the Dap-Kings. It was released on Daptone Records on October 2, 2007, and produced by Bosco Mann (Gabriel Roth).

Young MC|Bust A Move.fact: Young MC won the 1990 Grammy for Best Rap Performance for this song from his debut album Stone Cold Rhymin'. It peaked at No. 7 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 39 weeks on the chart.

Sam Cooke|Another Saturday Night.fact: Sam Cooke's 1963 song became an even bigger hit when Cat Stevens covered it in 1974. Stevens' version reached No. 6 on the US Hot 100, No. 19 in the UK, and No. 1 in Canada.

The Strokes|When It Started..fact: "When It Started" was released as the B-side of The Strokes' 2001 single "Last Nite." It also replaced the track "New York City Cops" on the US version of their debut album Is This It.

Michael W. Smith|Place In This World.fact: Released in 1991 as the second single from Go West Young Man, this became Michael W. Smith's biggest mainstream hit. It reached No. 6 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 5 on the Adult Contemporary chart.

The Sugarhill Gang|Rapper's Delight.fact: Released in 1979, this was the Sugarhill Gang's debut single and built its groove on Chic's "Good Times." Nile Rodgers and Bernard Edwards were later added to the songwriting credits, and the song was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame in 2014.

Rolling Stones|Get Off My Cloud.fact: The Rolling Stones recorded this single at RCA Studios in Hollywood on September 6-7, 1965. It reached number one in both the US and the UK.

Orlons|Don't Hang Up.fact: The Philadelphia group the Orlons released this single on Cameo Records in 1962. It reached No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 3 on the R&B chart.

Lisa Loeb|I Do.fact: "I Do" was the lead single from Lisa Loeb's 1997 album Firecracker. It peaked at No. 17 on the US Billboard Hot 100.

Marc Cohn|Walking In Memphis.fact: Marc Cohn won the Grammy for Best New Artist (1992 ceremony) and the song reached No. 13 on the Billboard Hot 100. Cher later covered it on her 1995 album It's a Man's World.

Hall & Oates|You've Lost That Lovin' Fee.fact: Hall & Oates' cover of the Righteous Brothers' 1964 No. 1 hit appears on their 1980 album Voices. It reached No. 12 on the Hot 100, their highest-charting single in over three years since "Rich Girl."

Radiohead|Codex.fact: "Codex" is a piano ballad on Radiohead's 2011 album The King of Limbs. It features string arrangements performed by the London Telefilmonic Orchestra.

Pavement|Rattled By The Rush.fact: "Rattled by the Rush" was the first single from Pavement's 1995 album Wowee Zowee, released on Matador. It is the album's second track, and Stephen Malkmus played a Gibson SG with P-90 pickups on it.

Rolling Stones|Ruby Tuesday.fact: "Ruby Tuesday" was a double A-side with "Let's Spend the Night Together" and became the Stones' fourth US number one in 1967. Brian Jones' recorder gives the song its signature sound.

Madonna|I'll Remember.fact: Madonna co-wrote and co-produced this 1994 song with Patrick Leonard and Richard Page for the film With Honors. It topped Billboard's Hot Adult Contemporary chart and later appeared on her 1995 ballads collection Something to Remember.

Elvis Presley|All Shook Up.fact: Written by Otis Blackwell, "All Shook Up" spent about nine weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard pop chart in 1957. Billboard named it the top song of the year for 1957.

R.E.M.|The One I Love.fact: From the 1987 album Document, this was R.E.M.'s first Top 10 hit in the US, peaking at No. 9 on the Billboard Hot 100.

Janet Jackson|Runaway.fact: "Runaway" was the lead single from Janet Jackson's 1995 compilation Design of a Decade: 1986-1996. It was written by Jackson with Jimmy Jam, Terry Lewis, and James Harris III, and produced by Jackson with Jam and Lewis.

Soft Cell|Tainted Love.fact: Soft Cell's 1981 cover of a song written by Ed Cobb and first recorded by Gloria Jones in the 1960s hit number one in the UK. It was Britain's biggest-selling single of 1981 and spent 43 weeks on the US Hot 100.

Rose Royce|I'm Going Down.fact: "I'm Going Down" is on the 1976 Car Wash movie soundtrack album, which was produced by Norman Whitfield. The album produced three Billboard R&B Top Ten singles.

*NSYNC|It's Gonna Be Me.fact: Written by Max Martin, Andreas Carlsson, and Rami Yacoub, this was the second single from *NSYNC's 2000 album No Strings Attached. It spent two weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and was their only chart-topper in the US.

Todd Rundgren|Bang The Drum All Day.fact: Though only a modest hit on release (No. 63 in the US), this Todd Rundgren song became a sports-arena favorite. Football, baseball, and hockey teams adopted it as a celebration song, including the Packers at Lambeau Field.

Sweet|Ballroom Blitz.fact: "The Ballroom Blitz" was written by the songwriting team Nicky Chinn and Mike Chapman and recorded in London in June 1973. It entered the UK singles chart at number two.

Otis Redding|Pain in My Heart.fact: Otis Redding's 'Pain in My Heart' is an adaptation of Irma Thomas's 1963 New Orleans recording 'Ruler of My Heart', written by Allen Toussaint under the pen name Naomi Neville. The Rolling Stones covered it shortly afterward on their album Out of Our Heads.

William Onyeabor|Good Name.fact: 'Good Name' is the third track on Who Is William Onyeabor?, a 2013 compilation released by David Byrne's Luaka Bop label. The Nigerian electro-funk artist had self-released eight albums between 1977 and 1985, and the compilation introduced his music to many listeners worldwide.

Johnny Cash|Orange Blossom Special.fact: 'Orange Blossom Special' was written by fiddler Ervin T. Rouse, who copyrighted the tune before the famous Florida passenger train of that name reached Jacksonville. Johnny Cash recorded it on his 1965 album Orange Blossom Special and again live at Folsom Prison in 1968.

OK Go|This Too Shall Pass.fact: The famous second video for 'This Too Shall Pass' features a huge Rube Goldberg machine filling a Los Angeles warehouse. About 55 to 60 people from Syyn Labs, Caltech and the MIT Media Lab helped build it, with no computer tricks, at an estimated cost of about $90,000.

Chappell Roan|HOT TO GO!.fact: Chappell Roan calls 'HOT TO GO!' a cheer song, and its arm-spelling dance routine spread widely on TikTok and at festivals. The song comes from her debut album The Rise and Fall of a Midwest Princess, and its video was filmed in Springfield, Missouri.

I Monster|Daydream In Blue.fact: 'Daydream in Blue' by Sheffield duo I Monster (Jarrod Gosling and Dean Horner) was built on a sample of 'Daydream' by The Wallace Collection, a 1969 recording. Their vocoder-led version reached number 20 on the UK chart.

The McCoys|Hang On Sloopy.fact: The McCoys' 'Hang On Sloopy' hit number one on the Billboard Hot 100 on October 2, 1965. In 1985 the Ohio legislature named it the official state rock song, and it is a staple of Ohio State marching band performances.

Kate Bush|Babooshka.fact: 'Babooshka' was the second single from Kate Bush's 1980 album Never for Ever, released June 27, 1980. It reached number 5 on the UK Singles Chart and number 2 in Australia.

The Undertones|My Perfect Cousin.fact: 'My Perfect Cousin' by Derry, Northern Ireland band The Undertones reached number 9 in both the UK and Ireland in 1980, their only top 10 single. It was written by Damian O'Neill and Michael Bradley and appears on the album Hypnotised, which hit number 6 in the UK.

Ohio Players|Fire.fact: The Ohio Players' 'Fire' was both a number one single on the Billboard Hot 100 (February 1975) and the title of the album that topped the Billboard 200 and R&B albums charts. It was the band's second album for Mercury Records.

Marcels|Blue Moon.fact: The Marcels' doo-wop version of 'Blue Moon', a 1934 song, reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in April 1961 and also topped the UK chart. It sold over a million copies, and it is listed among the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame's 500 Songs that Shaped Rock and Roll.

Patsy Cline|I Fall To Pieces.fact: 'I Fall to Pieces' was written by Hank Cochran and Harlan Howard and produced by Owen Bradley. It became Patsy Cline's first number one on the Billboard country chart in 1961 and also crossed over to the pop Top 15.

Chappell Roan|Pink Pony Club.fact: Chappell Roan first released Pink Pony Club in 2020, then re-released it on her 2023 debut album The Rise and Fall of a Midwest Princess. Five years after its first release it climbed to No. 1 on Billboard's Pop Airplay chart in 2025.

K-Ci & JoJo|All My Life.fact: All My Life reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 for three weeks in 1998 and was K-Ci & JoJo's only Hot 100 chart-topper. It comes from their 1997 debut album Love Always.

Yo La Tengo|Big Day Coming.fact: Big Day Coming is an early Yo La Tengo song that opens their album Painful. The band later recorded a second, louder version with distorted guitar and driving drums.

Jackson Browne|Doctor My Eyes.fact: Doctor, My Eyes was Jackson Browne's debut single, released in 1972 from his self-titled first album. It reached No. 8 on the Billboard Hot 100, with David Crosby and Graham Nash singing backing vocals.

The Strokes|Alone, Together..fact: Alone, Together is on The Strokes' debut album Is This It, released July 30, 2001. The album was recorded in about six weeks in spring 2001 with producer Gordon Raphael at his basement studio Transporterraum in New York City.

The Strokes|Trying Your Luck..fact: Trying Your Luck is on The Strokes' debut album Is This It, released July 30, 2001. The album was recorded in March and April 2001 with producer Gordon Raphael at Transporterraum in New York City.

The Strokes|Is This It..fact: The title track of The Strokes' debut album Is This It, released July 30, 2001. The band tried working with producer Gil Norton first, then returned to Gordon Raphael, who recorded the album at Transporterraum in New York City.

Missy Elliott|The Rain (Supa Dupa Fly).fact: The Rain (Supa Dupa Fly) was Missy Elliott's debut solo single in 1997. Timbaland produced it, and it samples Ann Peebles' 1973 soul hit I Can't Stand the Rain. Hype Williams directed the video, famous for its fish-eye lens look and shiny inflated jumpsuit.

Prince|Manic Monday.fact: Prince wrote Manic Monday under the pseudonym Christopher, and The Bangles turned it into their first big hit in 1986. It was the lead single from their album Different Light and peaked at No. 2 in the US and UK. Prince's own demo was not released until the 2019 collection Originals.

Echo & The Bunnymen|Bring on the Dancing.fact: Echo & the Bunnymen recorded Bring on the Dancing Horses for the Pretty in Pink soundtrack. It was released as a single in November 1985 and also appeared on their compilation Songs to Learn & Sing.

Beyonce|BODYGUARD.fact: Bodyguard is from Beyonce's 2024 album Cowboy Carter, which opened at No. 1 on the Billboard 200. The song debuted at No. 26 on the Billboard Hot 100 when the album came out.

Gene Vincent & His Blue Caps|Be-Bop-A-Lu.fact: Gene Vincent and His Blue Caps recorded Be-Bop-A-Lula in Nashville on May 4, 1956, originally as the B-side of Woman Love. It became a top-ten hit and is considered an early rockabilly landmark, with Cliff Gallup on lead guitar.

Deftones|Genesis.fact: Genesis is the opening track of Deftones' ninth studio album Ohms, released September 25, 2020 and produced by Terry Date. The album debuted at No. 5 on the Billboard 200.

Deftones|Ohms.fact: Ohms is the title track and closer of Deftones' ninth studio album, released September 25, 2020 and produced by Terry Date. The album debuted at No. 5 on the Billboard 200, and it was the week's top-selling vinyl LP.

Guided by Voices|Motor Away.fact: Motor Away was the lead single from Guided by Voices' 1995 album Alien Lanes, their first for Matador Records. The album was recorded in Tobin Sprout's home studio in Dayton, Ohio.

Timbuk 3|The Future's So Bright I Gotta.fact: Timbuk 3 was a husband-and-wife duo, Pat and Barbara K. MacDonald. This song was the lead track on their debut album Greetings from Timbuk3 and reached No. 19 on the Billboard Hot 100. The duo was also nominated for a Grammy for Best New Artist.

Johnny Cash|A Boy Named Sue.fact: Shel Silverstein wrote A Boy Named Sue, and Johnny Cash recorded the live version for his album At San Quentin in February 1969. It reached No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 and won Cash a Grammy for Best Country Vocal Performance, Male.

Simon & Garfunkel|Homeward Bound.fact: Homeward Bound was released in 1966 as the follow-up to The Sound of Silence and appears on Parsley, Sage, Rosemary and Thyme. Paul Simon wrote it during his time in England, and Widnes railway station has a plaque claiming it, though other accounts place it near Liverpool or Manchester.

Phoenix|1901.fact: 1901 topped Billboard's Alternative Songs chart in February 2010 after a record 31 weeks of climbing. Its parent album, Wolfgang Amadeus Phoenix, won the Grammy for Best Alternative Music Album.

Santana|Oye Como Va.fact: Oye Como Va was written by Tito Puente and first recorded around 1962. Santana's version on the 1970 album Abraxas reached No. 13 on the Billboard Hot 100, and Abraxas spent six weeks at No. 1 on the album chart.

Supertramp|The Logical Song.fact: The Logical Song reached No. 6 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 7 in the UK. Its album Breakfast in America won Grammys for Best Album Package and Best Engineered Non-Classical Recording.

lcd soundsystem|disco infiltrator.fact: "Disco Infiltrator" was released as a single on June 6, 2005, from LCD Soundsystem's self-titled debut album. James Murphy wrote it and produced it with Tim Goldsworthy as the production team The DFA. The 7-inch B-side was a cover of Siouxsie and the Banshees' "Slowdive."

laura misch|portals.fact: "Portals" was the lead single from London musician and saxophonist Laura Misch's debut album Sample the Sky. The album came out on October 13, 2023 on the label One Little Independent. In 2024 she followed it with Sample the Earth, a companion collection regrown from the original songs.

rogue wave|let my love open the door.fact: Rogue Wave's version is a cover of Pete Townshend's 1980 song from his solo album Empty Glass. It appeared on Cover Me, a Record Store Day 2016 album of 1980s covers. A video for the track followed in February 2017.

the nerves|hanging on the telephone.fact: Jack Lee wrote this in 1976 for his band The Nerves, and it led off their self-released four-song EP. Blondie covered it on their 1978 album Parallel Lines, with producer Mike Chapman keeping the original's ringing-phone intro. Blondie's single reached number 5 in the UK.

fleet foxes|battery kinzie.fact: "Battery Kinzie" is track four on Fleet Foxes' second album Helplessness Blues (2011), which was recorded at studios in Seattle, Woodinville, Washington, and West Hurley, New York. Phil Ek co-produced and mixed the album with the band. The song premiered on Zane Lowe's radio show on March 22, 2011, and was issued on a European Record Store Day 12-inch backed with "Grown Ocean."

empath|passing stranger.fact: Empath formed in 2015 in Philadelphia, when Catherine Elicson, Jem Shanahan and Garrett Koloski were roommates. "Passing Stranger" was released as a single ahead of their second album Visitor, which came out on February 11, 2022. Elicson has said she wanted a song where she could show off her sweep-picking guitar technique.

sigur ros|sæglópur.fact: "Sæglópur" is Icelandic for "lost at sea" or "lost seafarer." It was released as a single from Sigur Rós's 2005 album Takk... on August 16, 2005, and part of it is sung in Hopelandic, the band's invented language. The song has since been used in trailers and soundtracks, including Life of Pi and Aquaman.

goldfrapp|strict machine.fact: "Strict Machine" was written by Alison Goldfrapp, Will Gregory and Nick Batt for the 2003 album Black Cherry. After a 2004 re-release it became Goldfrapp's first UK top-20 single. It also reached number 1 on the US Billboard Dance Club Songs chart and won the dance award at the Ivor Novello Awards.

the national feat. rosanne cash|crumble.fact: "Crumble" is the penultimate track on The National's 2023 album Laugh Track, which the band surprise-released at midnight on September 18, 2023, after their Homecoming festival in Cincinnati. Rosanne Cash sings harmonies on the chorus and takes lead vocals on the bridge. It came out only months after the band's earlier 2023 album First Two Pages of Frankenstein.

deerhunter|agoraphobia.fact: "Agoraphobia" is track two on Deerhunter's 2008 album Microcastle, written and sung by guitarist Lockett Pundt. The album was recorded in about a week in April 2008 at Rare Book Room Studios in Brooklyn with producer Nicolas Vernhes, who played a Casio SK-1 keyboard on this song. Microcastle was released by Kranky in the US and 4AD in Europe.

stephen malkmus and the jicks|cold son.fact: "Cold Son" is track three on Real Emotional Trash (2008), released on Matador Records. The album was recorded in 2007 in Whitefish, Montana, and Chicago, produced by Stephen Malkmus and mixed in Brooklyn. Drummer Janet Weiss of Quasi and Sleater-Kinney played on the record, and it peaked at number 64 on the Billboard 200.

alvvays|belinda says.fact: "Belinda Says" is a tribute to Belinda Carlisle's "Heaven Is a Place on Earth," which the song references directly. Produced by Shawn Everett, it was released September 22, 2022 from the album Blue Rev. It earned a nomination for Best Alternative Music Performance at the 66th Grammy Awards.

tame impala|'cause i'm a man.fact: "'Cause I'm a Man" was released in April 2015 as the first single from Tame Impala's third album Currents. A 3D video for the song was directed by WEIRDCORE. A remix featuring the band Haim was released afterward.

angel olsen|heart shaped face.fact: "Heart Shaped Face" is track six on Angel Olsen's third album, My Woman, released September 2, 2016 on Jagjaguwar. The album was recorded at Vox Studios in Los Angeles and produced by Justin Raisen and Olsen. It reached number 47 on the Billboard 200 and number 40 on the UK Albums chart.

the replacements|kiss me on the bus.fact: "Kiss Me on the Bus" was the lead single from The Replacements' 1985 album Tim, which was produced by Tommy Erdelyi, better known as Tommy Ramone of the Ramones. The band performed the song on Saturday Night Live in January 1986. A 2023 reissue box set included a new remaster of Erdelyi's original mix.

songs ohia|farewell transmission.fact: "Farewell Transmission" opens the 2003 album The Magnolia Electric Co., the last album released under the Songs: Ohia name. Steve Albini recorded the album live at Electrical Audio in Chicago over three days in July 2002.

sparks|amateur hour.fact: "Amateur Hour" was the second single from Sparks' 1974 breakthrough album Kimono My House, which was produced by Muff Winwood. The song reached number 7 on the UK singles chart, following the number 2 hit "This Town Ain't Big Enough for Both of Us."

xtc|earn enough for us.fact: "Earn Enough for Us" is from XTC's 1986 album Skylarking, produced by Todd Rundgren and largely recorded at his Utopia Sound Studio in Woodstock, New York. The song opens the album's second side.

band of horses|no one's gonna love you.fact: "No One's Gonna Love You" comes from Band of Horses' 2007 album Cease to Begin. In 2010 Cee Lo Green recorded a cover that later appeared on his album The Lady Killer, and Band of Horses answered by covering his song "Georgia" with the University of Georgia Redcoat Marching Band for a shared 7-inch single.

king gizzard and the lizard wizard|polyg.fact: King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard released Polygondwanaland in November 2017 as a free download, the fourth album they put out that year. The band invited fans to make their own tapes, CDs, and records, and supplied the artwork and audio masters to do it.

arctic monkeys|fake tales of san francis.fact: "Fake Tales of San Francisco" first circulated on the demo collection Beneath the Boardwalk, then appeared on the band's 2005 EP Five Minutes with Arctic Monkeys. It was re-recorded for their 2006 debut album Whatever People Say I Am, That's What I'm Not.

talking heads|radio head.fact: "Radio Head" is from Talking Heads' 1986 album True Stories, written for David Byrne's film of the same name. The English band On a Friday took the name Radiohead from this song after signing with EMI in 1991, and Byrne later inducted them into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2019.

big star|september gurls.fact: "September Gurls" was written by Alex Chilton for Big Star's 1974 album Radio City, recorded at Ardent Studios in Memphis. The Bangles covered it on their 1986 album Different Light.

bad brains|banned in d.c..fact: Bad Brains formed in Washington, D.C., in 1977 after starting out as a jazz-fusion group called Mind Power. "Banned in D.C." appears on their self-titled debut, released on the cassette-only label ROIR in 1982 and nicknamed "The Yellow Tape."
